speaker: Fremiet
en: My son! Oh, my poor boy! Why will they not leave me in peace? I want nothing but to return home to grieve my loss. They hanged him for no good reason! I've taken a small pendant from his neck. Please sir, could you protect me as I take it back to our family home? My hope is to bless this pendant with the last rites. Is that unreasonable?

speaker: Crowd
en: Death to aristocrats! Hang her from the lamp post! She's an aristo too! À la lanterne! And now his mother! À la lanterne! He doesn't deserve a decent burial! He's not dead enough. Chop off his head! Toss him in the rubbish pit! It's not enough to hang him. Hang the mother too!

speaker: Fremiet
en: Thank you, kind sir. At least I have something to remember him by. May he rest in peace!

speaker: Assassin
en: There's a document that the Council wants to recover, "The Rights of Man". The author is in the prison just down the street. You've got a good chance to talk to him right now, while they give the prisoners an exercise break. His name is Thomas Paine.

speaker: Prisoner 1
en: Every time they bring us out here, I expect to get loaded into a dunghill.

speaker: Prisoner 2
en: Some bastard's turned off...

speaker: Prisoner 3
en: Exercise? It's food we need.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Get movin', we haven't got all day!

speaker: Guard 2
en: They're all out.

speaker: Guard 1;
en: Search the rooms for contraband.

speaker: Guard 2
en: Too much bother. Ain't seem right.

speaker: Prisoner 4
en: Where's Paine?

speaker: Guard 3
en: Who's this man, "Paine"?

speaker: Guard 4
en: Writer or something. Got on the wrong side of Robespierre.

speaker: Guard 3
en: Thank God. I couldn't take another minute listening to that writer.

speaker: Guard 5
en: I wish somebody would execute these people, I'm sick of the lot.

speaker: Guard 6
en: I've got this area!

speaker: Guard 7
en: How's the wife?

speaker: Guard 8
en: Sick again. Went a little extra to get her to a doctor.

speaker: Thomas
en: "Furthermore... ... in common cause with ... ... tyranny" Can't you see I'm busy! Shit.

speaker: Thomas
en: What is it?!

speaker: Arno
en: I'm here to get the "Rights of Man".

speaker: Thomas
en: That'll take some doin'. Damn warden took it! Bastard took all my scribblings. I'll tell you what. You go find it and my other two tracts, and I'll let you keep it. It's all rubbish anyway. But I'd like those other two back. I wasn't finished with those. He's got a post estate over by Les Invalides. Go nose about there.

speaker: Thomas
en: Piss off! What's this, didn't you listen to me?! Don't come back here without all of them! Half wit.

speaker: Woman 1
en: What a delightful soirée.

speaker: Woman 2
en: Thank God Madame Fetelle didn't come.

speaker: Man 1
en: I wonder what the poor people are doing tonight.

speaker: Man 2
en: One would think he could afford better wine.

speaker: Woman 3
en: But even so, I'll have another!

speaker: Arno
en: There's one.

speaker: Arno
en: "Age of Reason". Good.

speaker: Arno
en: All three.

speaker: Thomas
en: Have you got them all? I don't know why I wanted them back! It's all rubbish. Here, keep the Rights of Man if it's so damned important to you!

speaker: Arno
en: I could break you out of here.

speaker: Thomas
en: Break out? Christ, no! Let them do what they will with me. It's a matter of principle, man!

speaker: Madame Teragon (Wife of victim)
en: Oh, monsieur (sir)! I am distraught! Who could have done such a thing? He had not a single enemy. All I know is, there was an article in the newspaper that made him very upset.

speaker: Victor de Prasi (Friend of victim. Bleeding from a cut)
en: A woman just tried to kill me! Me! I managed to wound her, but she ran off. She grabbed a dagger, an heirloom! I twisted it away and stabbed her. This is her blood here. She fled through here. You can see the blood.

speaker: Anne de Molay (Descendant of Jacques de Molay)
en: They glory in their ancestors' deeds! Vile torturers!

speaker: Bishop
en: That's La Madeleine. One of Paris' many churches. It's currently "under construction", meaning it's closed. But, we've spotted the Templars going in and out of the building. Seems they've found a First Civilization site underneath the church and the artifacts are being hidden in these houses. You need to get the artifacts. Many chests, but only one is the right one. Do you split up, or stick together? Your choice, Initiates. More Assassins, more loot! Well, actually all but one are fake - you need to find the right one. Go. We rejigged this a bit, so it's a bit more of a training run. And I put in a few extra chests. You need to find the right one. Time to mix it up with some training. Which treasure is the right one? You need to find it, then get the goods. Rebecca and I thought you'd like a challenge - you need to find the right chest before you can get the loot.

speaker: Bishop
en: Sorry, that one's empty. Oooh, sorry. It's empty. Nothing here.

speaker: Bishop
en: Good work! Yep. That's the one. You got the goods. Yes. You found it. We have a winner.

speaker: Aquarius
en: was a virtual representation of one of Arno Dorian's genetic memories, relived by a Helix initiate through the Helix Navigator.

speaker: Aries
en: was a virtual representation of one of Arno Dorian's genetic memories, relived by a Helix initiate through the Helix Navigator.

speaker: Théroigne
en: Citizen, I could use your help.

speaker: Arno
en: How can I help, Théroigne?

speaker: Théroigne
en: Paris will never overthrow its chains with rifles like the ones it has. Its enemies are much better equipped.

speaker: Arno
en: Where are these guns coming from?

speaker: Théroigne
en: The local criminals have a mysterious new gunsmith, and very wealthy backers.

speaker: Arno
en: Seems suspicious.

speaker: Théroigne
en: Kill the gunsmith, and collect his blueprints for our own manufacturing.

speaker: Criminal
en: My employers won't be pleased with these delays!

speaker: Gunsmith
en: We appreciate your patience, and that of your employers.

speaker: Criminal
en: I'm losing patience. I didn't come down to this stinking hole to wait around on supplies!

speaker: Gunsmith
en: We're doing our best. But Méricourt's people are proving resourceful.

speaker: Criminal
en: If you can't prevail with superior weapons, maybe you're not right for this task.

speaker: Gunsmith
en: I assure you, the next shipment will arrive this afternoon.

speaker: Arno
en: The blueprints aren't here. They must be at their armory.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Méricourt's pretty tough. For a woman.

speaker: Guard 2
en: Don't matter how tough she is, we're gonna rule this city soon enough.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Heh heh. Well, we'll start with Théroigne de Méricourt.

speaker: Guard 3
en: Damn Méricourt robbing our carts again.

speaker: Guard 4
en: Once this new batch of rifles is ready, that'll be the last we hear of Méricourt.

speaker: Guard 5
en: How's it coming along?

speaker: Guard 6
en: They're doing well. Think they're getting the hang of these new designs.

speaker: Guard 7
en: Give me ten men and some of these new rifles, Méricourt will rue the day she was born.

speaker: Guard 8
en: Heh. Think you could take her with ten men?

speaker: Guard 9
en: New shipment almost ready?

speaker: Théroigne
en: Well done, citizen! With better rifles, Paris' enemies will fall!

speaker: Arno
en: My pleasure.

speaker: Council
en: Alexandre Lenoir is trying to preserve French art and create a national museum in the Palais du Louvre. Sadly, a band of looters is rampaging through the Marais looting valuable artworks. They loot churches, mansions and common dwellings, uncaring as to whether these are still occupied or not. Assassinate the leader of the smugglers at the Hôtel de Sens and put a stop to their destructive spree. --The Council

speaker: Charlotte Corday (A Girondist supporter)
en: You'll find the proof it's me soon enough. I just wanted his death to send fear into the hearts of Marat's believers for as long as I could.

speaker: Jasper Lasalle (A prisoner of St. Germain Prison)
en: I did it! The bastard deserved it! He got my father killed! My father was no traitor, that filthy scum Marat was!

speaker: Theron Brignac (A Girondist prisoner)
en: I was sent to his house to kill him but the job was finished by the time I got there. With what Marat was publishing it was either him or us. I don't recognize that list of names as Girondin, but you could ask some of our leaders. I'll write you an address, go there and show the list.

speaker: Dominique Bûches (A Girondist Deputy)
en: I don't recognize that list of names either. But it's quite the coincidence that the first letters of those names spell the word "providence."

speaker: Chantelle Naves (A curious onlooker of the crime scene)
en: They rounded up suspects and took them to the St. Germain Prison by the Gendarme. They're lucky if they survive the trip.

speaker: Jacqueline Perel (A neighbor of Jean-Paul Marat)
en: I've seen so many women coming in and out of that house, you'd think he was running a brothel.

speaker: Bishop
en: Paris, 1792, and Austria is knocking at the door.

speaker: Danton
en: You're late.

speaker: Spy
en: I was dodging patrols. Danton gave quite the speech. We should return to Austria as soon as possible.

speaker: Danton
en: Then why not stay as my guest, traitor!

speaker: Bishop
en: Georges Danton, a revolutionary leader with a leaky ship. Danton and Robespierre were the big daddies of the French Revolution. A revolution about to be crushed by an Austrian army with spies all over Paris. The Assassins knew there was a spymaster pulling the strings. The Spymaster was funneling information on Paris' defenses to the Austrians.

speaker: Spy
en: King Louis will be back in Versailles within the week.

speaker: Danton
en: Hah! Over my dead body.

speaker: Bishop
en: Danton rallied Paris against the Austrian threat, so he's a target. You need to protect Danton, then take down the spymaster.

speaker: Danton
en: You're just in time. Hold them off while I find a way out of here!

speaker: Danton
en: Is there no way out of here?

speaker: Danton
en: The doors are locked! There must be another way out!

speaker: Danton
en: We're out of time! The spies are sending information to Austria. You need to find them before they meet their couriers.

speaker: Bishop
en: All right. Let's grab those documents.

speaker: Bishop
en: These documents were sent by the Comte de Gambais. Infiltrate his house, then take out the count and his accomplices.

speaker: Vicomte de Gambais
en: Were you at the assembly? Did you hear his speech?

speaker: Guard
en: No sir. I was on duty here...

speaker: Vicomte de Gambais
en: Audacity. MORE Audacity, he said... As if a revolution weren't audacity enough!

speaker: Bishop
en: That's all of them. Okay time to get out of there.

speaker: Bishop
en: Paris' secrets are safe from the Austrians. Well done.

speaker: Gouze
en: It seems some royalist fanatics called Les Actes des Apôtres are on a book-burning spree. Many rare manuscripts are in danger - meet my contact at Place Dauphine and save what you can. We'll find them a good home here.

speaker: Contact
en: Thank God you're here! They've burned most of ' library already. Please, save what you can!

speaker: Gouze
en: I much prefer books in libraries to on bonfires, don't you?

speaker: Letter
en: Defend the funeral procession of Joseph Bara.

speaker: Driver
en: Where's the rest of the men?

speaker: Guard
en: Killed in the ambush.

speaker: Driver
en: Damn! We're trying to take Joseph Bara's body to the Panthéon, but some bloody royalists want to stop us.

speaker: Arno
en: I'll help defend you.

speaker: Driver
en: There's a crowd of people waitin' to give respects to this lad. He is a hero the Revolution. We've got to reach the ceremony in time. Let's go!

speaker: Spectators
en: The casket! The martyr! Bara! Look! It's Bara! Bara is a hero! Joseph Bara! It's the young boy! It's Bara!

speaker: Officer
en: Thank you, citizen, for defending the memory of this young hero of France.

speaker: Officer
en: Now that the remains of Joseph Bara have arrived, we can begin. Though Joseph Bara was hardly more than a child, he served the Revolution as a hero in Vendée. When royalists demanded his horse, he refused to give it up! They killed him for it. Faithful to the people of France, Bara cried 'Long live the Republic' with his dying breath! I agree with Robespierre when he says 'Only the French have thirteen-year old heroes'!

speaker: Guard
en: More royalists! To arms, men! For the memory of Bara! To arms! For Bara!

speaker: Bertrand Jouvet (Café Owner)
en: – Barto, the actor? I rent him a room upstairs for his "discreet encounters." This evening, he arrived with a bouquet and said a young lady would soon follow. I went out back briefly. When I returned, I found these flowers scattered in a trail out into the street. Then a man dressed in shabby black robes, you know, like a poor student, came running down the stairs and out the door. Very odd. Nothing bad has happened, I hope.

speaker: Ficarron (Comic actor)
en: I am the actor Ficarron! Loved by all from Marseille to Ghent! We have a tight-knit theatre troupe here. We all get along very nicely. Although... well, Pascal can be difficult and argues endlessly with Barto, but nothing serious. Why do you ask?

speaker: Pascal (Second lead actor)
en: My name is Pascal. I generally play Second Lead, although, frankly, I'm the superior actor. Barto's the leader of the troupe, so he casts himself as First Lead. First Lead! He can barely remember his lines. Likes to mix it up with the actresses as well. Unprofessional. He's not well liked. Laurent, in point of fact, hates him. Laurent's a bit of a turd himself.

speaker: Rose (Ingenue)
en: I'm Rose, I've been acting with the troupe for some time. I'm married to Laurent. I'm worried about him. Neither he nor our lead actor have shown up today. But if he does arrive, don't let him see you talking to me. He's very, very jealous.

speaker: Letter
en: Friends of Mirabeau enacted a plan to free Queen Marie-Antoinette before her execution. The plan was foiled due to the treachery of gendarme Jean Gilbert, a Templar. Gilbert knows too much about Mirabeau's machinations. We have learned that the National Guard is to honor him at the Church of the Madeleine. Assassinate him at the ceremony. --The Council

speaker: Speaker
en: Citizens! Fellow revolutionaries! Today we honor a real man of the people! Jean Gilbert, a gendarme only doing his job within the walls of the Temple, who uncovered a plot directed against the revolution itself! A plot to slip the vile and licentous Austrian woman out of the grasp of justice! Gilbert risked his life to unmask the plotters and stop the escape attempt in its tracks! Join me, citizens, in honoring Jean Gilbert, protector of the revolution!

speaker: Gilbert
en: Yes, I put quit to that conniving bitch. Least I could do.

speaker: Crowd
en: Gilbert is a hero to the glorious revolution! Down with the widowed Capet!

speaker: Letter
en: It appears that there is some sort of secretive activity, loosely called the "Black Office" operating behind the scenes in the Post Office near Place Vendôme. Whether this Black Office exists and just what it may be up to is a matter of conjecture. Infiltrate the Post Office and investigate the existence of the so-called "Black Office". - The Council

speaker: Guard
en: Where is the letter for Captain Bonaparte? Are you reading it back there?

speaker: Spy 1
en: Don't be absurd.

speaker: Guard
en: The Captain is expecting some urgent correspondence from the front.

speaker: Spy 1
en: Of course, of course. Don't worry. Everything will be taken care of in due time.

speaker: Guard
en: See that these packages are taken upstairs. Never mind why.

speaker: Spy 2
en: Hm... more directives from the Committee of Public Safety... Best to do their bidding - they're a prickly bunch.

speaker: Arno
en: Did you see what happened?

speaker: The witness (A witness who was near the scene of the crime)
en: An artist called out and the corpse was here.

speaker: Arno
en: Can anyone tell me more?

speaker: The witness
en: There was a third man. He said the would want to speak him and ran off.

speaker: Arno
en: Where?

speaker: The witness
en: He works in the bakery one street over. You could go there.

speaker: Arno
en: Your friend told me I could find you here. Did you witness the murder?

speaker: Arno
en: He was near the corpse.

speaker: The baker
en: Then he is in danger!

speaker: Arno
en: What happened in the street?

speaker: Arno
en: Did you see who committed the crime?

speaker: The Street Performer
en: No. I was focused on my perfomance.

speaker: The Street Performer
en: I am SICK of people looking at me! Do not LOOK AT ME! Let the show begin!

speaker: Anna (Prostitute)
en: Oh, god, there's men coming and going all the time! I didn't see de Sade last night, but he coulda been here, comes here a lot. It was too dark for me to see 'em proper, but there were some odd goings-on last night. One john came in but didn't stay long enough to really do anything. And then there were two men, but only one went into Suzanna's room.

speaker: Micheline (Prostitute. Friend of victim)
en: Poor Suzanna! She was a favorite of that Citizen de Sade that came around so much. He never treated her proper. I told her, "Send him away!" But he pays so much. Look! Ropes, whip, that's de Sade all right. Randy bastard!

speaker: Etienne Clavet (Vagabond)
en: Ah, sure, I'm here all the time. I've got nowhere to go. Who you lookin' for? I saw a couple fellas meet here late last night. One of 'em was dressed all fancy. Must be a servant, I overheard him mention his master, "the Marquis." Afterwards, the other man went into that building, right there.

speaker: Civilian
en: Come on, then, you ol' reprobate!

speaker: Olivier (Valet to de Sade)
en: I'm unable to say what the Marquis was engaged in last night. It was a rare night off for me. If any of his personal effects are missing, well he gets caught up in his "activities" and becomes careless. He could have left them anywhere.

speaker: Olivier
en: Unhand my master!

speaker: Civilian 2
en: You, shut up!

speaker: de Sade
en: It's quite all right, Olivier. This may be amusing.

speaker: Marquis de Sade (Roué)
en: Back to jail! It's all too delightful. Really—murder a girl? Those days are behind me. But I do enjoy the fuss. I did visit Suzanna with some frequency, but not last night. I'm sure my valet can confirm my whereabouts. There was a young man, some days ago. Perhaps rather too taken with my philosophies. I recommended Suzanna to him. It's not impossible he might know something.

speaker: Jean-Marc (Leather worker)
en: Sure, I made that whip. I supposed it could belong to de Sade, I sell him all sorts of things. But, you know, there's a student, strange fella, he wanted to buy all the same things de Sade bought—seemed to think de Sade is some kinda god or something. I've got his address in the delivery book. Let me see... Yes. Here it is.

speaker: Quentin Legris (Student)
en: Suzanna? De Sade told me about her. I arranged a time and thought about all the things I would do to her. I started to lose my nerve, though, so I drunk a couple of bottles of wine. By the time I got there, I couldn't go through with it. I turned around and left.

speaker: Arno
en: Anything else?

speaker: Quentin Legris
en: I heard two men in the dark just when I was leaving. One of them said, "After it's done, come meet me in the church courtyard at St. Nicolas de Champs. I'll pay you there."

speaker: Olivier
en: After the degradations that I've suffered at de Sade's hand? I jumped at the change to put a gruesome end to the man.

speaker: Olivier
en: I do hope you're proud of yourself. That animal de Sade should be here instead of me!

speaker: Charles
en: A jezebel killed? Hardly a crime in my estimation. Take your due.

speaker: Madame Gerard (Wife of Deputy Gerard)
en: I am Madame Gerard. My husband and I were invited to dine, and I was looking forward to a lovely evening. The Henneberts are known as a delightful couple.

speaker: Olivier Gedet (Deputy of the Assembly)
en: I hope I'm not to blame in any respect. It was I who advised Hennebert to invite the Gerards. I hoped to calm the murderous political situation. The wine was poured and we all drank a toast to letting bygones be bygones. Hennebert immediately fell choking to the ground.

speaker: Old Woman (Mother of André)
en: My son ran to the apothecary. The one near the post office.

speaker: Robert (Glassmaker)
en: I do a lot of work for important politicians. I don't much like folks nosing about. Get on out of here.

speaker: Jaimie
en: Bella. Listen to me, you mustn't carry on this way.

speaker: Bella
en: Oh, Jaimie, he's been gone for days! What shall I do?

speaker: Jaimie
en: Yes! I turned him into mincemeat, and he deserved it. Old miser.

speaker: Jaimie
en: I shoulda chopped you up into haggis as well!

speaker: Charles
en: Chopped him up, eh? Nasty business. Well, pick a weapon.

speaker: Arno
en: Does Léon live here?

speaker: Man
en: He ain't in.

speaker: Man
en: We haven't seen him for days. Leave us in peace.

speaker: Margot
en: Has he been arrested again?

speaker: Arno
en: Not that I know of.

speaker: Margot
en: A lot of people would like to see his hands cut off. He's a vicious thief, that one.

speaker: Arno
en: I need his help.

speaker: Margot
en: He went out to the windmill yesterday, I've not seen him since. Give him my name, Madame Margot.

speaker: Margot
en: Please, tell him to come home.

speaker: Guard 1
en: There is an intruder in the tunnels.

speaker: Arno
en: Léon.

speaker: Raider 1
en: It's mine now.

speaker: Leader
en: Oy!! Small loot is not worth the blood! We find the door and we'll be bathing in coin. Back to work!

speaker: Raider 2
en: Captain Rose finally caught him.

speaker: Raider 3
en: Léon? I hear he killed two of our men.

speaker: Raider 4
en: We shouldn't be disturbing the slumber of kings.

speaker: Raider 5
en: Don't tell me you believe the ghost stories.

speaker: Raider 4
en: I've seen one down below. Late at night.

speaker: Raider 5
en: And how much had you been drinking, I wonder?

speaker: Rose
en: You ever meet a noble, Léon? You ever heard a noble talk? Descended from God, they were. Threads of gold arced from between their blessed legs into holy chamber pots. And then, Léon?

speaker: Rose
en: Fountains of rubies spilled from their necks and rained down upon all of France. Now, a man born deep within the lowest circle of hell can rise to the very top of Olympus itself.

speaker: Léon
en: Unhand me, (bastard!)

speaker: Rose
en: Is that what you want, little man, to rise up? I see it in you. Ambition. You're just like me.

speaker: Napoleon
en: Rose.

speaker: Rose
en: Commandant Bonaparte.

speaker: Napoleon
en: Any progress to report?

speaker: Rose
en: Only this.

speaker: Napoleon
en: Find me the door that this key unlocks, and I shall reward you beyond your wildest dreams.

speaker: Léon
en: What is behind the door?

speaker: Napoleon
en: This is our (little) trespasser?

speaker: Léon
en: Who are you calling little? I'm nearly as tall as

speaker: Napoleon
en: You need to learn... a bit of diplomacy. Rose, I trust you'll show the boy to the surface?

speaker: Rose
en: Of course, Commandant.

speaker: Rose
en: Kill him.

speaker: Léon
en: What?! No! Let me go!

speaker: Raider 6
en: You do it.

speaker: Raider 7
en: He's only a child.

speaker: Raider 6
en: I've children of my own.

speaker: Léon
en: The ghost of the kings!

speaker: Arno
en: So much for the element of surprise.

speaker: Léon
en: Stay back, monster!

speaker: Arno
en: I'm not a ghost. Madame Margot sent me.

speaker: Léon
en: Madame Margot? You are trying to confuse me.

speaker: Raider 8
en: Intruder!

speaker: Léon
en: Whoa!

speaker: Arno
en: Still confused?

speaker: Léon
en: Quickly, we have to hide.

speaker: Arno
en: Not so fast. I'm looking for a manuscript. It was taken from a tomb under Saint-Denis.

speaker: Léon
en: I have it. It's in my fortress, we can get it later. How did you do all that? You're the best fighter I've ever seen.

speaker: Arno
en: I wouldn't go that far.

speaker: Léon
en: Where did you train?

speaker: Arno
en: In Paris.

speaker: Léon
en: Whoa! I practice behind our house. I don't really have anyone to train with. All the freedom fighters are in Paris, like you.

speaker: Arno
en: What about your mother?

speaker: Léon
en: Madame Margot? She's not my mother. My mother is . She had to go back to Spain. That's why she had to leave me at the orphanage. I bet my parents will come back once France is safe. In here! Come.

speaker: Léon
en: For now, we are going to need weapons.

speaker: Arno
en: Just leave that to the professionals... Where did you get that?

speaker: Léon
en: I stole it from two raiders yesterday. Hid it here.

speaker: Arno
en: This is a fine gun.

speaker: Léon
en: Yes, I know. I know what I'm doing.

speaker: Arno
en: Which is?

speaker: Léon
en: Saving France. Now that you're here, it's going to be a lot easier.

speaker: Arno
en: Listen

speaker: Léon
en: What?

speaker: Arno
en: We have to get that manuscript first. To protect it from the enemies of France.

speaker: Léon
en: Oh! All right. We need to get above ground.

speaker: Léon
en: Hey! Look at me. I escaped.

speaker: Raider 9
en: Get him!

speaker: Léon
en: Catch me and the Commandant will make you rich!

speaker: Raider 10
en: Catch that little rat!

speaker: Arno
en: Nice work. Don't let it go to your head.

speaker: Arno
en: Not bad.

speaker: Léon
en: Whoa. You're better than all the stories.

speaker: Arno
en: That's because the stories aren't true.

speaker: Léon
en: This way out. I think.

speaker: Napoleon
en: No one of import has inquired after our activities?

speaker: Lieutenant
en: There were rumors around town that the Marquis de Sade was asking questions.

speaker: Napoleon
en: Never trust rumors. He is destitute and in prison.

speaker: Lieutenant
en: Why do you employ such a man as Rose to find the temple? He cares nothing for us or our aims. If I was in your place, I would not pander to such

speaker: Napoleon
en: What does a rat want?

speaker: Lieutenant
en: Food, of course.

speaker: Napoleon
en: Ah! You appeal to their self-interest. But you have miscalculated.

speaker: Napoleon
en: Your people are dead. I know the human animal. What you fear, what you love. Is Rose a bad man? Undoubtedly. But I, Napoleon, can control him and turn him to what is best for France.

speaker: Napoleon
