en: No, not here... No key here... It's not here... Nothing.

speaker: Arno
en: Hah, here it is. "Time"... "Clock"... of course.

speaker: Arno
en: I think this is what the Council is looking for...

speaker: Valet
en: Robbed, I tell you! This is madness! That tailor refuses to deliver the coat I have ordered for Louis Antoine de Saint-Just.

speaker: Arno
en: Must be a misunderstanding. I'll speak to the tailor.

speaker: Valet
en: It's either his head, or mine!

speaker: Arno
en: That man outside says you owe him a coat.

speaker: Tailor
en: No one's getting that coat until I get some answers.

speaker: Arno
en: About what?

speaker: Tailor
en: This material! There's something fishy about it. I tried to ask the tanner, but rough men outside the tannery turned me away.

speaker: Arno
en: I'll see what I can do.

speaker: Arno
en: Eugh. Smells disgusting...

speaker: Guard 1
en: They don't pay me enough for this work.

speaker: Guard 2
en: Count yourself lucky you have a job at all.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Hah. As if I could afford anything.

speaker: Tanner
en: Please! Help me...

speaker: Arno
en: What happened here?

speaker: Tanner
en: Saint-Just wanted leather, but... not from cowhide...

speaker: Arno
en: You're making leather from human skin!?

speaker: Tanner
en: My God... I was forced!

speaker: Arno
en: Saint-Just will pay.

speaker: Arno
en: That leather is made from human skin!

speaker: Valet
en: It had better be, that's why Saint-Just is paying so well.

speaker: Arno
en: You'll both pay, with your lives.

speaker: Valet
en: You know, you may become a nice coat yourself. Seize him!

speaker: Arno
en: You were right.

speaker: Tailor
en: What is it?

speaker: Arno
en: They were using human skin to make the leather for Saint-Just's coat.

speaker: Tailor
en: My God. I'll make sure this leather is used as evidence to denounce Saint-Just and bring him down.

speaker: Arno
en: Good luck.

speaker: Gouze
en: One of our informants may have been compromised. She's posing as a scullery maid near Porte St. Denis. We need you to tail the innkeepers, find out if they suspect her, and get her out if she's in danger.

speaker: Innkeeper
en: Well, what's so important, Azelma?

speaker: Azelma
en: It's the bloody scullery girl! Claude said he spotted her hiding a note under a loose cobble. I didn't even know the wretch could read.

speaker: Innkeeper
en: So? She's probably just scribbling for her gutter-rat friends.

speaker: Azelma
en: That's what I thought at first, but then I went and read the note. She knew about Renard. She had details of the operation. I think she's a spy.

speaker: Innkeeper
en: Pah! This is what we get for taking in war orphans.

speaker: Azelma
en: What do we do?

speaker: Innkeeper
en: Don't worry. I'll take care of it.

speaker: Arno
en: Madame Gouze sent me. You are discovered - you need to get out of here.

speaker: Gouze
en: Colette's already asking for a new assignment - she's indomitable, that one.

speaker: Condorcet
en: Unbelievable! Insufferable! First they twist my ideas for the constitution, now they want to arrest me!

speaker: Arno
en: How may I help, citizen Condorcet?

speaker: Condorcet
en: I must leave immediately Paris immediately, but you can retrieve my research on the history of political progress. My opponents seized it as soon as the warrant for my arrest went out.

speaker: Arno
en: I'll be back before you know it.

speaker: Rival 1
en: Good, it's all here. My thanks.

speaker: Thief 1
en: My pleasure, citizen.

speaker: Man
en: Does it make for good reading?

speaker: Rival 1
en: It will look better with my name on it. It was the Condorcet's fault, really. I told him the Girondists weren't long for this world.

speaker: Man
en: Neither is he, from what I hear.

speaker: Rival 2
en: It took you long enough!

speaker: Thief 1
en: Apologies, citizen. Condorcet wouldn't leave his office.

speaker: Rival 2
en: Condorcet can't even string a sentence together. I don't understand the fascination with him...

speaker: Thief 1
en: You are too right.

speaker: Rival 2
en: I wish I could see the look on Condorcet's face when this gets published under my name!

speaker: Thief 1
en: Would that I could paint it for you.

speaker: Condorcet
en: My papers! But how did you do it?

speaker: Arno
en: My apologies, (Mister) Condorcet, but some things must remain out of your memoirs.

speaker: Condorcet
en: Say no more. My thanks.

speaker: Arno
en: What's our plan?

speaker: Bellec
en: Our plan? You're not an apprentice anymore, boy. So study your surroundings and devise your own plan. I'm not here to hold your hand.

speaker: Bellec
en: No target's unreachable.

speaker: Sivert
en: Out of the way! Move! Where the hell is Duchesneau...?

speaker: Bellec
en: If you can't find a weakness to exploit—make one.

speaker: Duchesneau
en: You've secured the cathedral?

speaker: Guard
en: Oui, monsieur. (Yes, sir.)

speaker: Duchesneau
en: Good. Tell Sivert I'll meet him inside.

speaker: Bellec
en: Opportunity is everywhere. It's on you to take it.

speaker: Cleric
en: You! Get back here with my keys! Thieves!

speaker: Bellec
en: And if all other plans fail, why not sacrifice yourself for the cause? Your life for his. Before Altaïr, that was the Levantine approach.

speaker: Arno
en: You mean a dagger in broad daylight, as I'm cut down where I stand?

speaker: Bellec
en: It sends a powerful message...

speaker: Arno
en: I'll do it my way.

speaker: Bellec
en: Whatever you think best, Assassin.

speaker: Thug 1
en: Did you see the expression on that fat old cleric's face?

speaker: Thug 2
en: Priceless! Turned the color of an ! I thought he'd faint with outrage!

speaker: Thug 2
en: Well, seeing as how I stole his keys, why not raid the Archbishop's wine cellar?

speaker: Thug 1
en: You never!

speaker: Thug 2
en: To reason, and freedom from superstition!

speaker: Thug 1
en: Here, here! There's one for the Church!

speaker: Thug 2
en: They may have signed the Civil Constitution, but everyone knows the bishops are in bed with the royalists!

speaker: Thug 1
en: I'll drink to that!

speaker: Thug 1
en: What have we here? An altar boy, or just a common cutpurse? Get him!

speaker: Duchesneau
en: You've secured the cathedral?

speaker: Guard
en: Oui, monsieur Duchesneau (Yes, Mister Duchesneau). This is the only way in or out, and we've paid off the guards.

speaker: Duchesneau
en: Good. With Arpinon dead, I don't want to take any chances. When Monsieur (Mister) Sivert arrives, tell him I've gone to arrange matters with the priest. I'll join him inside. Where the hell is that priest? What the hell is keeping this priest? Bastard priest could bother showing up on time...

speaker: Priest
en: That bastard wants thirty percent? God only gets ten! Who the hell does Sivert think he is?

speaker: Duchesneau
en: What choice do you have? How long will it be before the revolutionaries descend on Mother Church like locusts?

speaker: Priest
en: Very well.

speaker: Duchesneau
en: I'll make arrangements with Monsieur (Mister) Sivert. And see that the confessionals are closed. My employer prefers to discuss business away from prying eyes.

speaker: Priest
en: Oui, monsieur. (Yes sir.)

speaker: Arno
en: I think, monsieur (sir), you are going to miss that meeting.

speaker: Cleric
en: Merci. Que Dieu vous bénisse. (Thank you. May God bless you.)

speaker: Sivert
en: Move! Out of my way! One side!

speaker: Sivert
en: Where the hell is Duchesneau? What the hell is keeping him? Does he expect me to wait forever? Intolerable! This is getting absurd!

speaker: Arno
en: Everything's in place.

speaker: Sivert
en: Finally saw reason, did he? What's our cut?

speaker: Arno
en: Thirty percent.

speaker: Sivert
en: Good, good. This is our moment, my friend. Petty nobles are ripe enough fruits, but the Church has been leeching off the people for centuries. If we crack their vaults, the Grand Master cannot fail to recognize our work.

speaker: Arno
en: As you say, monsieur (sir).

speaker: Sivert
en: Good. Now, if we're done here, I'll take my leave and wait for our holy friend to deliver the goods.

speaker: François
en: Wait here. See that we're not disturbed.

speaker: La Touche
en: Sivert.

speaker: Sivert
en: Monsieur (Mister) La Touche. I'm here to see the King of Beggars.

speaker: La Touche
en: Come with me.

speaker: Roi des Thunes
en: "The intrigues of rats?" Pompous fool! If I could lay my hands on him....

speaker: François
en: Well? What's so important you had to pull me away from my daughter's

speaker: Arno
en: You all right, Monsieur (Mister)? Too much of the King's champagne?

speaker: Roi des Thunes
en: Sivert, come away!

speaker: Élise
en: Charming place. What do you hope to find here?

speaker: Arno
en: This is where the apothecary says he delivered the poison. I'm hoping I can pick up a trail and follow it back to the source.

speaker: Élise
en: Pick up a trail? Are you a bloodhound now?

speaker: Arno
en: Something like that.

speaker: Élise
en: Let's go. I'll follow your lead.

speaker: Arno
en: The trail ends here.

speaker: Élise
en: Are you sure?

speaker: Arno
en: I'm sure.

speaker: Arno
en: No. Wait here.

speaker: Élise
en: Don't be ridiculous, I'm not letting you go in there alone.

speaker: Arno
en: Élise. I have to do this myself. Please.

speaker: Élise
en: I understand.

speaker: Élise
en: You'd better come back to me. Go. Do what you must. It's all right. I understand.

speaker: Bellec
en: Took you long enough, pisspot.

speaker: Arno
en: Bellec?

speaker: Bellec
en: Should have known it'd be you that find me. The only question is what happens now.

speaker: Arno
en: You poisoned Mirabeau!

speaker: Bellec
en: He poisoned us! Peace with the Templars is a fairy tale!

speaker: Arno
en: And you're the only one who can "save the Brotherhood."

speaker: Bellec
en: Do you think it's the first time this's happened? The first time that the Assassins have been forced to purge their leadership? The first time that the Order has been forced to build itself back up from nothing to power? No. Masyaf, Monteriggioni, the American Colonies... it's all happened before, and we've risen anew, stronger than ever. But now... We've lost our purpose, Arno. We mired ourselves in politics and revolutions. But we're not a nation. We're an army. And in an army, "making peace with the enemy" is called "treason." But no. I'm not the only one that can save the Brotherhood. We can. Together.

speaker: Arno
en: Bellec... you know I can't do that.

speaker: Bellec
en: That's a pity.

speaker: Arno
en: Bellec, please! Come back to the Council with me, we can resolve this like reasonable men!

speaker: Bellec
en: Reasonable men don't treat with Templars, boy.

speaker: Bellec
en: Bah! You're a stubborn little fuck, aren't you?

speaker: Arno
en: Ask anyone.

speaker: Bellec
en: Never should have plucked you out of the Bastille! Your father'd be ashamed of you! Traitor! Damn it! Fuck! You're weak! Bastard! Get up! You disappoint me, pisspot. I taught you better than this. Get up!

speaker: Bellec
en: I had hopes for you! I thought you could think for yourself!

speaker: Arno
en: I can, Bellec! I just don't think like you!

speaker: Bellec
en: Open your eyes, boy! I've seen Templars put entire villages to the sword, just for the chance of killing one Assassin! Tell me, in your vast experience - what have you seen?

speaker: Arno
en: I've seen the Grand Master of the Templar Order take in a frightened orphan and raise him as his own son!

speaker: Élise
en: Arno!

speaker: Arno
en: I'm fine. Stay there.

speaker: Bellec
en: I should have left you to rot in the Bastille. Tell me, did you ever really believe in the Creed, or were you a Templar-loving traitor from the start?

speaker: Arno
en: It doesn't have to be this way, Bellec!

speaker: Bellec
en: You're the one who's making it so! If you'd just see sense, we could take the Brotherhood to a height we've not seen in two hundred years!

speaker: Arno
en: Yes, killing everyone who disagrees with you is a brilliant way to start your rise from the ashes!

speaker: Élise
en: Look out!

speaker: Bellec
en: So... Now we see the heart of it. It's not Mirabeau that's poisoned your mind, it's her. She's the last piece of this god-fucked lunacy.

speaker: Arno
en: Bellec....

speaker: Bellec
en: You'll thank me for this. One day.

speaker: Bellec
en: Should have listened to me, boy. You had your chance, pisspot. Time to end this.

speaker: Élise
en: Behind you! Arno!

speaker: Bellec
en: Do it. If you've got an ounce of conviction and you're not just a love-addled milksop, you'll kill me now. Because I won't stop. I will kill her. To save the Brotherhood, I'd see Paris burn.

speaker: Arno
en: I know.

speaker: Bellec
en: Taught you better than this. Make it a clean kill. Well fought, pisspot. Now at least have the balls to finish it. Finish it!

speaker: Charles
en: Thank you, my friend.

speaker: Bellec
en: Got to get you back to that boy of yours in one piece, don't we pisspot?

speaker: Bellec
en: You dropped this.

speaker: Bellec
en: Well, I'll be damned.

speaker: Bellec
en: So you're really going through with this?

speaker: Mirabeau
en: Your protégé vouches for her. Don't you trust him?

speaker: Bellec
en: With my life. It's the girl I don't trust. Nothing I can say to convince you?

speaker: Mirabeau
en: I'm afraid not.

speaker: Bellec
en: Thought not. Tchin. (Cheers.)

speaker: Mirabeau
en: Tchin. (Cheers.)

speaker: Bellec
en: Repose en paix. (Rest in peace.)

speaker: Arno
en: Repose en paix. (Rest in peace.)

speaker: Sanson
en: Sir! I'm Sanson, the Official Executioner! I need help. Some brigands have stolen parts of a new execution machine I'm building. They hope to lure me into a trap. Could you recover all the items for me?

speaker: Thug 1
en: Chop off heads humanely? What's the point? I say, you want to lop off a head, why pussy-foot around? Do it fair and square with a two-handed blade!

speaker: Thug 2
en: Amen to that.

speaker: Sanson
en: Tobias! We've recovered all the pieces.

speaker: Schmidt
en: All right, then. Give me a hand, would you? We'll see if it works.

speaker: Sanson
en: This ingenious device will save me much labor, my friend. Can you imagine, executing so many aristocrats by the sweat of my brow?

speaker: Schmidt
en: I just hope this doesn't make killing people too easy.

speaker: Sanson
en: It's an ambush! Dear Lord!

speaker: Thug 3
en: Get them!

speaker: Sanson
en: Ah, keep them back!

speaker: De Choisy
en: What's taking so long?

speaker: League member
en: We have to be certain that everything is ready.

speaker: De Choisy
en: It is.

speaker: League member
en: Be prepared. It will take several days to get to England.

speaker: De Choisy
en: Can't you hurry it along? I'd like to dine with my cousin, Lord Percy.

speaker: League member
en: Remember, our story is that we've got goods to deliver. Textiles.

speaker: De Choisy
en: How humiliating.

speaker: Crimson Rose
en: You blackguard! You're an Assassin! Could you please fight with a litlle more panache? I'll see that you're properly dressed for your funeral! Was it really so bad before the Revolution? Peasants starved, I suppose, but that sort of thing happens. You never understood. I was trying to return society to its rightful order! Certain classes of people were meant to lead and others to follow. And you, dear boy, were meant to follow!

speaker: Beaumarchais
en: Ah! Hello! Could I have your ear for a moment? Pierre Beaumarchais, playwright, diplomat and bon vivant. I'm told you can help me. The Public Censors are repressing new plays, including one of mine. They've paid a critic to give it a bad review and are planning to censor the production itself. Could you steal the review before it goes to press, and then, um, suppress the censors?

speaker: Critic
en: Ha! People love to read a bad review! This one'll sink Beaumarchais for good. And I haven't even seen the play!

speaker: Review
en: "See that this review is printed in your journal under your name. Payment enclosed. -- Office of the Public Censor, Le Petit Arsenal MARRIAGE of FIGARO is ROYALIST SCREED Some of our theatre artists absurdly believe that plays such as M. Beaumarchais wrote during the full monarchy are still to be enjoyed now that we have a republic! His play, The Marriage of Figaro, was thought to stand as an attack on the aristos a decade ago, but its time has passed and it will soon be forgotten. Cannot our play-smiths concoct theatre in accordance with the new principles? Must we view this musty dredge filled with the extravagant costumes of those that should lose their heads? No, I say! Enough! M. Beaumarchais should look to his own head, and anyone who attends this farce should look to theirs!"

speaker: Chief Censor
en: Ah. Time to clear the ol' windpipes.

speaker: Arno
en: Now for that artifact.

speaker: Rose
en: Allow me.

speaker: Rose
en: What skill stealing the key. Much obliged!

speaker: Raider 1
en: Should I notify the Commandant?

speaker: Rose
en: Tell him that I resign.

speaker: Arno
en: What now?

speaker: Léon
en: To light your way!

speaker: Arno
en: Léon, how did you find me?

speaker: Léon
en: I know what I'm doing. All of France is counting on you.

speaker: Arno
en: Little man. Thank you. Now get out of sight, I mean it.

speaker: Léon
en: Why?

speaker: Arno
en: It's time to find out what's inside that temple.

speaker: Léon
en: And the (captain)?

speaker: Arno
en: He shall fall... for I am an Assassin.

speaker: Arno
en: Merde. (Shit.)

speaker: Rose
en: Look around! What are we missing? A hundred to the first man to solve the enigma.

speaker: Rose
en: How the devil do I get it? Open damn, you!

speaker: Arno
en: The artifact will never be yours.

speaker: Rose
en: I have commandeered the artillery required to break the siege.

speaker: Soldier
en: Steal the artifact, and your reward shall be far greater than anything Commandant Bonaparte has offered.

speaker: Rose
en: Where do I deliver it?

speaker: Soldier
en: To the lady Eve.

speaker: Raider 2
en: Get him!

speaker: Raider 3
en: Steal the artifact!

speaker: Arno
en: Now old friend, we shall see why they're after you.

speaker: Arno
en: What dark magic is this? That Commandant must never have it.

speaker: De Sade
en: Ah, dear Arno. Our hopes as to the condition of the human species may be reduced to three points...

speaker: Soldier
en: Napoleon Bonaparte. You are under arrest for treason and deserting your post.

speaker: De Sade
en: ... The destruction of inequality between nations, the progress of equality in one and the same nation...

speaker: Assassin
en: Final passengers!

speaker: Arno
en: This must reach Al Mualim in Cairo.

speaker: Assassin
en: Ha!

speaker: De Sade
en: ... and lastly, the real improvement of man.

speaker: Recruiter
en: If you wish to join the Cult of Baphomet, you must steal two holy chalices from the Cathedral of Notre Dame and bring them to me.

speaker: Recruiter
en: Well done. You are now a follower of Baphomet. Come to our ritual. The password is: "The father of understanding."

speaker: Gilles Benoit (A patient at La Salpêtrière)
en: What happened? I had a paper cut, but my whole arm got infected because it's so filthy in here! Some surgeon thought he had the right to hack it clean off! The pain almost killed me!

speaker: Edgard Duchamp: (A local butcher)
en: Murders? Well some crazy man came by here rambling about a corpse. That's all I know, but how about some fresh pork? My assistant can give you a perfect cut. He's a little slow in the head, came in here a few weeks ago begging for work, but I tell you, the boy has a gift. A gift that finally leaves me some time to get some fishing in!

speaker: Byron Latour (A local fisherman)
en: I was fishing a f-few days ago and I found a body floating in the river...cut up arms and legs too. It must have floated here from upstream. I-I didn't kn-know what to do with it so I took it to the cemetery. I'm-I'm sorry.

speaker: Bernard Lasalle (Supervisor of La Salpêtrière Aslyum)
en: Those papers are for a patient that we just released. He always blabbered on about being a fisherman, so your best bet is to check the river. We also had a patient escape a few weeks ago. You can check their cells inside, just down the steps.

speaker: Dr. Lenard Erny (A local surgeon)
en: Of course that's my journal. Proof my assistant is taking jobs behind my back. He's always late and off doing God-knows-what. I don't care how good he is with a blade, I can't trust a man who's stealing clients. Best to let him go.

speaker: Thierry Dion (Assistant to Dr. Erny)
en: What can I say? My boss is a good barber but a horrible surgeon. I was using his clients to make a little money on the side. Cut the middle man.

speaker: Gouze
en: The Queen's dressmaker, Rose Bertin, agreed to make costumes for the theatre. But it seems her royal past wasn't enough to spare her the attentions of radicals. Les Actes des Apôtres vandalized her shop, and now Rose is nowhere to be found. Go to the Marais and see what you can find out - I'm worried about her.

speaker: Arno
en: Madame Bertin, I presume?

speaker: Bertin
en: Oh, you must be Charlotte's friend. I came here to recover my work from these scoundrels, but, well...

speaker: Arno
en: Say no more. Get yourself to safety, I'll deal with this.

speaker: Bertin
en: Merci.

speaker: Arno
en: Now then... how the hell do I get all this back to the theatre?

speaker: Gouze
en: With Madame Bertin's costumes on the rack, we're sure to draw a more fashionable crowd.

speaker: Bishop
en: Paris, 1794. Every day is execution day.

speaker: Danton
en: You follow us shortly, Robespierre! Your house shall be beaten down and sowed with salt!

speaker: Bishop
en: Georges Danton, hero of the revolution, and he's headed to the guillotine.

speaker: Bishop
en: Danton's real crime was pissing off this guy - Maximilien Robespierre. Father of the Terror.

speaker: Robespierre
en: Give me that.

speaker: Bishop
en: Danton's friends printed an article comparing Robespierre to a bloodthirsty dictator. The truth hurts.

speaker: Danton
en: It's not my usual taste, but as a man of state, you get used to dealing with... rats.

speaker: Robespierre
en: My old friend, you are an enemy of the state. Look what Hanriot found among you papers...

speaker: Bishop
en: ...Danton's private letters.

speaker: Bishop
en: It's not enough to arrest Danton - Robespierre is going to kill his friends, too.

speaker: Bishop
en: Rescue Danton, then get to his friends. Danton's already been taken to the guillotine. You've got a few minutes before he's executed, but I'd get a move on.

speaker: Guards
en: Stay back! Stay away! Back, or we'll fire! We will fire if you don't keep back! Stay away, or we will fire! Get back, all of you!

speaker: Danton
en: Don't cry, Camille! Today, we die for France! We save France by our deaths, my friend, remember that. Remember ! Show her your bravery. Come on then, Camille, there's no hope for it now. We must show them that we are not defeated.

speaker: Desmoulins
en: We are defeated.

speaker: Danton
en: Ha! Not while the revolution rages on. Come on, then! What's taking so long? Why are we waiting? On with the show! Hurry! My public awaits! The wait times for the guillotine are unbearable! I wish to lodge a complaint! These quarters are terrible! Today, they will witness the death of Danton! But in six weeks, they will see the death of Robespierre!

speaker: Danton
en: I knew you'd try to rescue me. But I have to die today. Robespierre' reputation will die with me. I do have a request. Robespierre's stolen my personal letters. He'll use them to arrest my friends. I need you to find my friends. And get the letters, if you can.

speaker: Bishop
en: Personally, I'd have taken the rescue. But Danton's made the call - let's go get his friends.

speaker: Citizen 1
en: Well, Danton got what he deserved.

speaker: Citizen 2
en: Poor Robespierre. Imagine how you'd feel having a friend turn against you.

speaker: Extremist
en: You're a friend of Danton's.

speaker: Friend 1
en: And it seems you won't leave me alone, even on the day of his death.

speaker: Friend 1
en: You're a little late, but thank you. Time for me to leave Paris, I gather. Thank you for your help. I think... I think it's time to get my family out of the city. I can't thank you enough.

speaker: Bishop
en: All clear here, but Danton has allies who weren't in that crowd. Find them. You don't have much time.

speaker: Friend 2
en: I thought I'd never get away. Thank you. My God, I thought that was the end of me. Thank you. Thank you... oh, thank you.

speaker: Extremist
en: Where are those letters?

speaker: Friend 3
en: Cowards. They wouldn't have dared attack when Danton were still alive.

speaker: Extremist
en: There! That one! He's the traitor.

speaker: Friend 4
en: What? Me? No! Leave me alone!

speaker: Extremist
en: You're enemies of the state!

speaker: Friend 4
en: Can't we mourn Danton in peace?

speaker: Extremist
en: You shouldn't even speak Danton's name in public! Fighting does you no good!

speaker: Friend 4
en: Leave us be!

speaker: Extremist
en: Traitors never come quietly...

speaker: Friend 4
en: How dare you attack us? Today of all days!

speaker: Extremist
en: The revolution doesn't need the likes of you.

speaker: Friend 4
en: Thank you. We were about to leave the city when they caught us.

speaker: Bishop
en: Now we need to get those letters. I'm thinking Robespierre's house is a good bet.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Has Citizen Robespierre seemed distracted to you?

speaker: Guard 2
en: It's those letters he took from Danton. I imagine he's not pleased with what he's reading.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Where's Citizen Robespierre?

speaker: Guard 2
en: He's retired to his rooms for the day.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Doesn't like what happened to his friend.

speaker: Guard 2
en: That, or... you know, I think he may be sick.

speaker: Guard 1
en: What if he really is ill?

speaker: Guard 2
en: Are you going on about that again?

speaker: Guard 1
en: Well, what would we do if he died?

speaker: Guard 2
en: Stop worrying about nothing!

speaker: Guard 1
en: I think Citizen Robespierre isn't getting enough rest.

speaker: Guard 2
en: He does seem a bit tired, recently. And he's been wandering around with those letters. He's left them everywhere. It's not like him.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Do you think he regrets it?

speaker: Guard 2
en: Who regrets what?

speaker: Guard 1
en: What happened to Danton?

speaker: Guard 2
en: Well, he did retire to his rooms for the day...

speaker: Bishop
en: Nice work. Time to get out of there.

speaker: Bishop
en: Danton's allies are safe. Well done.

speaker: Samuel Maran (The Doctor)
en: That's not my tonic. You see the cork there? I always mark mine when counting stock. No mark means its Mme. Beaudry's. That wretched merchant dilutes her tonic with all sorts of chemicals to keep her prices down. It's putting me out of business! You take too much of that poison and you'll be a dead man!

speaker: Adrien Piet (The local apothecary)
en: Philibert? I sent him to retrieve supplies from the merchant days ago and he's not returned. You'd have to ask Philibert where the hell Philibert has gone. I'll write down the address, but first I'll take my keys back thank you very much.

speaker: Noel Pommier (A gravedigger)
en: This graveyard's been too busy for my liking. I've got missing tools, and someone even broke into the catacombs. Found a pretty rosewood cross down there though, I thought I'd give it to the convent.

speaker: Guillaume Pinard (A merchant)
en: Philibert? I haven't seem him. But what do you have there? Chartreuse! Quite rare. You know the Carthusian monks are famous for making it, and the Carthusian nuns are just as famous for hiding it as well!

speaker: Antoine Danis (A frequent customer to the tavern)
en: Philibert!!! I love that fool! Buy me a drink and I might remember! Maybe.

speaker: Catherine Doyère (A customer at the tavern)
en: Yeah, Philibert was here, bought us a few rounds. Kept going on and on about his sister. I thought he was an orphan, but who knows.

speaker: Navarre Cavery (A musician and master Lute player)
en: Can't say I talked to him. My music keeps me busy enough.

speaker: Jérôme Tolbert (A barkeep)
en: Sure, Philibert was here last night; I had to cut the bastard off! That dumb drunk owes me plenty of coin. Promised he'd pay with enough Chartreuse to last me a year. I was dumb enough to believe him. Check with the regulars, they might know more.

speaker: Mathieu Rochon (A witness who lives near the tannery)
en: A few days ago I heard some strange noises outside my window late in the night. When I looked outside I saw someone going into the tannery carrying something quite large. I just assumed it was Citizen Gilbert, working late as always, I had no clue he was vacationing and someone broke in, otherwise I'd have told someone.

speaker: Citizen Gilbert (Owns the tannery where the body was found)
en: I finally get a vacation, only to find a headless corpse rotting in my tannery. That...thing's been sitting here at least a few days. But the wound on his chest, only a custom blade could do that. I've heard rumors those awful gangs love to leave their mark on their victims.

speaker: Citizen Touchet (Owns the jewelry shop)
en: Ah! This ring! How could I not recognize my own masterpiece. Of course, it belongs to Warden Leroux. You must return this, I'm sure he'll be looking for it. You'll find him working at the prison at La Salpêtrière or home with his wife, Mme. Camille. I'll write down the address for you.

speaker: Hugo Soulière (The Deputy to Warden Leroux)
en: The horror! The gall of these vermin! Look at what they've done! Poor Warden Leroux's head placed on a pike for all in the prison to see. Surely a message to me who must follow his brave tenure. I'd wished him a goodnight just yesterday. I'd heard rumors of his gambling debt with Les Marcheurs Morts, that wretched gang.

speaker: Olivier Rivett (The barkeep who runs Le Creux)
en: Hey, I know nothing, say nothing. I just serve Les Marcheurs Morts their ale and carry about my business. You can take it up with their leader upstairs.

speaker: Danton Marotte (Leader of the gang Les Marcheurs Morts)
en: I was expecting someone to come by and pin Leroux's death on us. Sure the warden had some debt. But we were negotiating the release of some of my men in return. Why would I toss away a deal like that? I'm not a fool.

speaker: Mme. Camille (Wife of Warden Leroux)
en: My husband had many enemies. Running a prison made sure of that. I must admit, he'd been missing two nights before I could bring myself to tell the police. It's not secret that I wasn't... faithful. But I would never do such a horrible thing!

speaker: Citizen 1
en: It's happened again! The fountains are cursed! There are three such fountains. If you drink the water, the Devil comes to you and lures you away with promises. One of the fountains is right there.

speaker: Citizens
en: Careful, citizen. These fountains are dangerous. That man isn't gonna drink from the fountain, is he?

speaker: Voice
en: Come to me. I can give you untold riches. Eternal life can be yours. Everything you desire. Just come to me. Yes. Closer. Closer. Yes. This way. Don't leave me. Come closer. Come, come, you will find peace at last.

speaker: Voice
en: Come to me. I can give you untold riches. Eternal life can be yours. Everything you desire. Just come to me. Yes. Closer. Closer. Yes. This way. Don't leave me. Come closer. Come, come, you will find peace at last.

speaker: Voice
en: Come to me. I can give you untold riches. Eternal life can be yours. Everything you desire. Just come to me. Yes. Closer. Closer. Yes. This way. Don't leave me. Come closer. Come, come, you will find peace at last.

speaker: Élise
en: Are you sure about this?

speaker: Arno
en: Not particularly, no. But the Marquis is on the National Convention with le Peletier. He might have some insight.

speaker: De Sade
en: Ah... Which is a more incisive commentary on corruption in the bishopric? Seven nuns seducing a parish priest into debauchery, or an enourmously-endowed Benedictine sodomizing a goat named Pius?

speaker: Arno
en: No force in heaven or on earth will make me answer that question.

speaker: De Sade
en: Quite right, Arno, the goat it is. So, what can I do for you and your charming companion?

speaker: Élise
en: Louis-Michel le Peletier. What can you tell us about him?

speaker: De Sade
en: Ah, dear Louis. He went from abolishing the death penalty to calling for the King's head in two short years.

speaker: Arno
en: Where can we find him?

speaker: De Sade
en: I'm afraid I don't often socialize with my fellow deputies. Something about my distaste for the beheading of the innocent. Speaking of innocents...

speaker: Arno
en: De Sade...

speaker: De Sade
en: Hum?

speaker: Arno
en: Le Peletier.

speaker: De Sade
en: Well, I believe he often takes meals at a certain café near le Palais-Royal. I believe you can find him there.

speaker: Arno
en: If we don't, I'll be back.

speaker: De Sade
en: Really? Well then, I hope I'm mistaken.

speaker: Élise
en: No, you don't.

speaker: Driver
en: Wine delivery for the palace.

speaker: Guard
en: Take it 'round back.

speaker: Washer
en: Make sure you clean those windows properly this time, or Monsieur le Peletier will have my head.

speaker: Remy
en: Yes, Madame.

speaker: Tallien
en: , Citizen le Peletier.

speaker: Le Peletier
en: Citizen Tallien.

speaker: Citizen 1
en: What do you think the Austrians will do?

speaker: Citizen 2
en: You read Brunswick's little . "If the least violence be offered to their Majesties the king, the queen and the royal family, we will inflict an ever memorable vengeance by delivering over the city of Paris to military execution and complete destruction, and the rebels guilty of the said outrages to the punishment that they merit."

speaker: Citizen 1
en: Hmph. It'll be the Huguenots all over again.

speaker: Merchant
en: Are you trying to poison my customers?

speaker: Driver
en: I'm sorry, sir?

speaker: Merchant
en: This wine is cut with ! One glass of this, and

speaker: Driver
en: I don't know what

speaker: Merchant
en: I've been doing this for thirty years, boy, I think I know what tainted wine tastes like!

speaker: Driver
en: There's 50 livres worth of wine here! What am I supposed to do with it?

speaker: Merchant
en: Well, you can sell it as a remedy for sore nipples for all I care, but I'm not buying a drop of it. Trying to poison my customers.... Ought to call the gendarmes.... Poisoned wine! What's next? Infected bread? This is criminal, this is! You're lucky to escape a murder charge.

speaker: Driver
en: Sorry, sir. I'll have it taken away as soon as the cart returns. Forgive me. Yes, sir. Pardon, monsieur.

speaker: Arno
en: This may come in handy.

speaker: Washer
en: le Peletier complained of streaks last week! See that it's spotless this time! Get the grime out of the corners! (Mister) le Peletier is a fastidious man! I expect (Mister) le Peletier to be able to see himself in that glass when you're done! That window better be sparkling when Mister le Peletier arrives! Mind you don't leave it open! (Mister) le Peletier hates a draft!

speaker: Arno
en: Pardon, (Miss.) (Mister) le Peletier has complained of stuffiness in his office. Could you open the window?

speaker: Washer
en: What are you on about? (Mister) hates a drafty room!

speaker: Arno
en: I understand. (Have a good evening.)

speaker: Arno
en: Would this persuade you?

speaker: Washer
en: Remy! Open the window! (Mister) le Peletier finds his office a bit stuffy!

speaker: Remy
en: B... But you said

speaker: Washer
en: Just do it!

speaker: Remy
en: Alright

speaker: Citizen 3
en: Mark my words, the Americans will throw in with us.

speaker: Citizen 4
en: You think so?

speaker: Citizen 3
en: How could they not? Like them, we're throwing off the yoke of tyranny!

speaker: Citizen 4
en: The yoke of tyranny is one thing. The yoke of finance is quite another.

speaker: Citizen 5
en: Will you be attending the execution tomorrow?

speaker: Citizen 6
en: Of course. Won't you?

speaker: Citizen 5
en: Thought I might give it a miss. Crowds, you know.

speaker: Citizen 6
en: Crowds. For that you'd miss the defining event of the age?

speaker: Citizen 5
en: There'll be engravings.

speaker: Le Peletier
en: Suzanne! Run! Guards! Guards! Stop that man! Assassin! Don't let him escape! Arrest him!

speaker: Le Peletier
en: Waiter!

speaker: Le Peletier
en: A bottle of your finest wine. Tonight, we celebrate the death of tyranny!

speaker: Waiter
en: At once, sir. David! Get me a bottle of the d'If! Quickly!

speaker: Waiter
en: Well done, David. Didn't even see you arrive.

speaker: Waiter
en: Here you are, sir. The '74 Chateau d'If. A lovely vintage, if I may say.

speaker: Louise-Suzanne
en: Papa? What's wrong?

speaker: Le Peletier
en: Nothing, my dear. Just a bit of a stomachache. Go... go and find your nurse and tell her to take you home. I'll be along soon.

speaker: Louise-Suzanne
en: Yes, Papa.

speaker: Le Peletier
en: So. I thank you at least for sparing my daughter the sight of this. All that I've done has been for the good of my country, my people, and my family. Ah. But you are unmoved. So be it. If it must be done, let it be done swiftly. Do it! End it!

speaker: Germain
en: The King must be seen as a criminal and a traitor. Only then, when he is executed like a common villain, can we show the world Jacques de Molay's great truth.

speaker: Le Peletier
en: You may show the world what truths you like, Grand Master. What I do, I do for the good of France.

speaker: Rouille
en: You were right. King Louis has been talking to all sorts he shouldn't have.

speaker: Speaker
en: Citizen le Peletier, the vote stands at 360 for execution to 360 for clemency. How do you vote?

speaker: Le Peletier
en: Execution.

speaker: Le Peletier
en: The vote is cast and counted, Grand Master.

speaker: Germain
en: And?

speaker: Le Peletier
en: The King will die.

speaker: Germain
en: I had no doubt. I shall very much look forward to witnessing the end of tyranny.

speaker: Le Peletier
en: I shall see to it you have the finest view.

speaker: Letter
en: The unscrupulous Duc de Barrois uses his influence to have his rivals executed. He then takes possession of their properties. He is celebrating his success by hosting a theatrical performance at the Hôtel de Sully. Disrupt the performance and make a dramatic example of the duke. - The Council

speaker: Désirée
en: I have made a grievous mistake! You must help me! I have done my best to write down what must be done.

speaker: Bernadotte
en: I've nothing to live for! Well, except another drink... I've lost the live of my life. Oh, well! Might as well make the best of it! Here's mud in yer eye!

speaker: Bernadotte
en: Uh, just what array of services are available?

speaker: Prostitute
en: Look, girls, Jean is here! We're always happy to see you, Jean. Interested in having a little party? Just you and me?

speaker: Bernadotte
en: No need to get angry, I'm coming! Oh, very well. I'll come along.

speaker: Désirée
en: Jean! Please forgive me! I have been such a fool!

speaker: Bernadotte
en: Can it be true? Do my ears deceive me?

speaker: Désirée
en: I cannot live without you!

speaker: Bernadotte
en: But Désirée, it cannot be. You are promised to another!

speaker: Désirée
en: I will prove my love for you, Jean. You! Go to Captain Bonaparte's house! Find my love letters and bring them back that I may destroy them!

speaker: Napoleon
en: But what am I to do about Désirée? I need a strategy. Perhaps a tactical retreat on the Désirée front, and as for Joséphine, "March to the sound of the guns!" Yes, with Joséphine, a flanking manoeuvre. And, oh, what flanks!

speaker: Napoleon
en: What? Oh, those old letters? Get rid of them. Joséphine has conquered me now!

speaker: Désirée
en: Oh! You found them! Many thanks. And now, my dear Jean, watch as I burn them to cinders!

speaker: Bernadotte
en: Gads! What a woman of passion! Désirée! My love for you burns as bright as your love letters to Bonaparte! Could you ever-?

speaker: Désirée
en: Oh, Jean!

speaker: Bernadotte
en: Would you-?

speaker: Désirée
en: Yes! Yes, yes, yes!

speaker: Napoleon
en: Ah! Arno! Could you help me in a personal matter? It concerns my fiancée, Désirée Clary. Some sans-culottes plan to abduct her for a ransom. Captain Bernadotte knows the particulars. Join him in front of the post office and ensure that Désirée escapes her house unharmed.

speaker: Bernadotte
en: Ah! Bonaparte sent you. We are to rescue his fiancée. Let us make haste!

speaker: Bernadotte
en: Again I find myself running errands for Bonaparte. And yet he and I are of equal rank! How does he do it?

speaker: Bernadotte
en: Gads! I've got a beautiful sword! Crafted in Spain! But a man can't marry his sword, you know. I need a woman to sooth my brow! And here Bonaparte has already found a fiancée! Damn, he's a lucky dog. I wonder if he'll amount to anything? Ah! The fighting life. I love it so. Sans-culottes? Get yourselves some culottes, then! Good god. You there! You cannot stop us! We're here to rescue someone! Come on. Don't laze about. We need a challenge! Amateur! I am here on a mission of gallantry! These dogs are no challenge for me. You will not sully Mademoiselle Clary!

speaker: Sans-culottes 1
en: We got her trapped on the top floor!

speaker: Sans-culottes 2
en: Stay back! They're covering the stairs!

speaker: Sans-culottes 3
en: There's plenty of loot here!

speaker: Sans-culottes 4
en: Grab what you can, then we'll get her!

speaker: Bernadotte
en: Mademoiselle! We're sorry to disturb you, but your fiancé sent us to ensure your well-being!

speaker: Désirée
en: I can take care of my own well-being, thank you.

speaker: Bernadotte
en: I see that, in you, Captain Bonaparte has secured a precious victory. Gad! Your ankle is exceptionally well-turned!

speaker: Désirée
en: You are impertinent, sir! ... I like that. I like that very much.

speaker: Bernadotte
en: And those flashing eyes! We must go, before I say something I regret! Or I sustain a mortal injury!

speaker: Désirée
en: You fight with great panache, captain!

speaker: Bernadotte
en: And you with an alluring fire! May I compliment you, Mademoiselle, on your bold thrusts!

speaker: Désirée
en: Sir! That is hardly appropriate, I am engaged!

speaker: Bernadotte
en: Fighting with you has made me quite giddy with delight.

speaker: Désirée
en: Ah! (Dear) Bernadotte! If this had been another time, another place...

speaker: Bernadotte
en: Say not another word! I dare not even dream.

speaker: Désirée
en: You are right. There can be no dreams for us. Goodbye, dear sir, goodbye!

speaker: Napoleon
en: Arno! A favor. I suspect that Captain Bernadotte has fallen in love with my fiancée, and I cannot abide the thought. As I must dine with her this evening, I would ask that you search Bernadotte's house near the Palais-Royal and determine his feelings on the matter.

speaker: Receipt
en: "Payment received for one silver pendant inscribed 'for Désirée.'"

speaker: Letter
en: "Captain Bernadotte, I must present regrets for my mistress, Mlle. Clary. She is not able to entertain this evening as she is to dine at the Restaurant Boulanger with Captain Bonaparte."

speaker: Diary
en: "I am in continual torment because of my love for Désirée. I have learned that she dines with Bonaparte this evening. I am a man of action! I must go to her, present my gift and declare my affections!"

speaker: Citizen 1
en: That Bonaparte fellow is dining with a lovely young thing.

speaker: Citizen 2
en: That one. She'll cavort with anyone.

speaker: Désirée
en: Bernadotte! What a surprise to see you here!

speaker: Napoleon
en: Captain Bernadotte, I'm having a private dinner with my fiancée. Arno, can you escort the Captain outside?

speaker: Citizen 1
en: She seems taken with Captain Bernadotte, if you ask me.

speaker: Citizen 3
en: I can't imagine she'd be faithful to him. Who would marry that Corsican?

speaker: Citizen 4
en: I'm told she admires Bernadotte's muscular legs!

speaker: Citizen 3
en: How delightfully scandalous!

speaker: Bernadotte
en: Enough gossip! I will teach you to speak of Mademoiselle Clary in such terms!

speaker: Citizen 1
en: He fights fiercely for the reputation of another man's woman.

speaker: Citizen 2
en: Look! He's brought a gift for Bonaparte's fiancée.

speaker: Désirée
en: What is all this?! The scandal! The shame!

speaker: Bernadotte
en: But I have a... gift for you.

speaker: Désirée
en: I never want to see you again!

speaker: Arno
en: Do you have a copy of the (Encyclopedia) Diderot?

speaker: Café owner
en: Yes, I believe I do.

speaker: Arno
en: A relief. I'm looking to borrow a section of it, one focusing on secret societies...

speaker: Café owner
en: Give me a moment to

speaker: Café owner
en: Thief! Stop him!

speaker: Arno
en: Got you!

speaker: Thief
en: Fine! Keep it!

speaker: Thief
en: Help! Help!

speaker: Arno
en: Wondeful. He has friends.

speaker: Arno
en: Now I just need to find time to read it...

speaker: Letter
en: The Templars have procured a rubbed transfer of the missing section of the Rosetta Stone. Friend of the Brotherhood Jean François Champollion informs us that this rubbing contains sensitive information concerning the Assassins. However, the rubbing has not yet been translated. Understanding its importance, the Templars have split the rubbing into three sections. Champollion knows their whereabouts. Go to Champollion near the Luxembourg Gardens and use him to help you recover the three-part rubbing before the Templars learn its contents. – The Council

speaker: Champollion
en: Capital! I'm here, my friend! The three parts of the rubbing are scattered, awaiting the translators. I want to help, Arno. I can distract the Templar guards at each encampment. Follow me, and we'll recover those rubbings in an instant!

speaker: Champollion
en: You there! You men! I know what you're up to! What's gotten into you? Rubbing stones like children! Have you no dignity?

speaker: Guard 1
en: Who in hell are you?

speaker: Champollion
en: I am one who understands the importance of antiquity. I have read the crumbling texts, I have delved into the rituals of the ancients, I know secrets undreamt of!

speaker: Guard 1
en: Shut up, you ranting idiot!

speaker: Champollion
en: Idiot, am I? We shall see, my dear fellows. We shall soon see!

speaker: Champollion
en: Gentlemen! I am convinced that the same hieroglyphic-phonetic signs used to represent the sound of Greek proper names were used in hieroglyphic texts long carved long before the Greeks came to Egypt!

speaker: Guard 2
en: Bullshit!

speaker: Champollion
en: These are articulated in the same way as the cartouches carved under the Greeks! The discovery of this decisive fact is due to my work on pure hieroglyphic script.

speaker: Guard 2
en: You don't know your arse from a cuneiform tablet!

speaker: Champollion
en: I could prove this to you quite conclusively, but it would require going into lengthy detail. Good-day!

speaker: Champollion
en: I have a tale to tell you! Come, come listen to my tale of adventure and woe!

speaker: Guard 3
en: What's he on about?

speaker: Champollion
en: I have followed the course of the Nile from it's mouth to the second cataract, and I have seen sights unimaginable!

speaker: Guard 3
en: Like what?

speaker: Champollion
en: Egyptian monuments dating from Roman and Ptolemaic times. Temples, palaces and tombs of the pharaonic era!

speaker: Guard 3
en: Describe them, please!

speaker: Champollion
en: I shall write it all down, gentlemen. You can purchase it and read at your leisure.

speaker: Champollion
en: Well done. I shall translate these myself and report the results to the Brotherhood.

speaker: Arno
en: You knew the victim?

speaker: Arno
en: Were you alone?

speaker: The sad soldier
en: Just as I arrived someone ran. I'm sure he wore a soldier's uniform.

speaker: Arno
en: Were you in town last night?

speaker: Arno
en: A soldier has been found dead there. You look like the killer.

speaker: The young musician
en: Not me, I was at the bar the whole time! And why would I kill a soldier? I want to join the army! Who would hit a woman anyway? There's no fun in hitting a woman!

speaker: Arno
en: Were you downtown last night?

speaker: The young musician
en: This is a man's world. These Revolutionary libertines must be stopped. I was certain you saw things my way. But you are worse than a woman.

speaker: Arno
en: What...?

speaker: Élise
en: No time to explain. Run!

speaker: Woman
en: Will we be taking a ride this evening, Professor?

speaker: Professor
en: No, no, no... he! I'm afraid not; these older models are entirely at the mercy of the breeze, and there is far too much of it I'm afraid to be safe. Now, this particular example

speaker: Professor
en: What do you think you're doing? Get out of there this instant!

speaker: Élise
en: Cut the ropes! I'll cover you!

speaker: Professor
en: Oh my.

speaker: Élise
en: Hurry! Watch out!

speaker: Élise
en: Good! Just one more!

speaker: Élise
en: Arno!

speaker: Arno
en: I'll come to you. Hang on...

speaker: Élise
en: I'll try to stay put.

speaker: Élise
en: It certainly is lovely up here. You should see the view.

speaker: Arno
en: Oh, you don't say!

speaker: Élise
en: The wind is picking up! You'd better hurry!

speaker: Arno
en: Yes, thank you! Have you thought at all about how you plan to get down?

speaker: Élise
en: Oh, these things tend to work themselves out. You're going to run out of roof soon! I hope you've got a plan!

speaker: Arno
en: Does "watch and laugh as you crash into the river" count?

speaker: Élise
en: Leave them, just run! I can handle them, you keep running! Leave them!

speaker: Arno
en: What happened?

speaker: Élise
en: I think the rope's caught!

speaker: Arno
en: Just hang on!

speaker: Élise
en: You'll have to cut the rope.

speaker: Élise
en: Arno! Are you all right?

speaker: Arno
en: Oof!

speaker: Élise
en: Arno!

speaker: Arno
en: I'm alright!

speaker: Arno
en: They might actually be trying to hit me. What did you do back there?

speaker: Élise
en: It's a long story!

speaker: Arno
en: I really should talk to Napoleon about this.

speaker: Élise
en: Run! Hurry up! Are you coming or not? This hardly seems like the time! Stop playing around! We're almost at the river! Hurry!

speaker: Arno
en: Just... coming...

speaker: Arno
en: Next time, I plan the escape route.

speaker: Arno
en: It's beautiful.

speaker: Élise
en: From up here, you'd never know the nation is tearing itself apart.

speaker: Arno
en: Can... can things ever go back to the way they were before, do you think?

speaker: Élise
en: Do you? After everything that's happened? Everything we've lost?

speaker: Arno
en: So that's it, then? The course of history forever altered, never again to return?

speaker: Élise
en: Maybe we can't go back. But going forward isn't necessarily an ending.

speaker: Arno
en: Élise, I

speaker: Arno
en: You cheated.

speaker: Élise
en: You took too long.

speaker: Arno
en: I love you.

speaker: Arno
en: ... Someone will come and collect it. Surely.

speaker: Théroigne
en: Arno! I've had a very good idea. I want to raise up an army, a whole army of women! Women have had the worst of it, and it's women who will know how to set things right! Now, when I say women, I mean the women of the streets. You know... prostitutes. Street-walkers. I need you to go to the brothels. Give them these recruitment handbills. They'll join up in droves.

speaker: Prostitutes
en: An army of women? About time! I'm in. Tell her I'll be there. As long as I get out of this hellhole, yes.

speaker: Guard
en: Keep out the riff-raff. You wanna play, you gotta pay.

speaker: Prostitute 1
en: Tough day at the revolution?

speaker: Prostitute 2
en: Dear God, this is backbreaking work.

speaker: Prostitute 1
en: Ain't it the truth, sister.

speaker: Patron 1
en: What can I get for three francs?

speaker: Prostitute 3
en: A flirty wink and a peek at my stocking.

speaker: Patron 1
en: Sold!

speaker: Patron 2
en: You don't sleep with royalists, do you?

speaker: Prostitute 4
en: Their money's as good as yours.

speaker: Prostitute 5
en: Hey, handsome. Need to stretch your legs?

speaker: Prostitutes
en: For Méricourt? All right. Do we get uniforms? It's gotta be more fun than this. Let's go! I'm at her command!

speaker: Auctioneer
en: How much am I offered for this sweet little parsnip? Come on, gentlemen. She'll brighten up your miserable, disgusting life! She'll perform feats of salaciousness the likes of which you never dared dream! Don't let the innocent look fool you, gentlemen! She's a wildcat, aren't you, Babette?

speaker: Babette (prostitute)
en: You disgust me.

speaker: Auctioneer
en: See? She's got spirit!

speaker: Prostitutes
en: Women's army? Where do I sign? That Théroigne! She's always got somethin' goin'. Women's army? That's crazy. I'll join. Different kind of grunt work. Shooting instead of screwing? Sounds good. A chance to get off my back? Sure.

speaker: Olivier
en: Thrown out onto the street yet?

speaker: Arno
en: Oh, you would love that, wouldn't you?

speaker: Olivier
en: It'd break my heart.

speaker: Arno
en: Olivier, if I weren't here, who'd do all your work for you?

speaker: Olivier
en: The horses need brushing, boy. Get to it.

speaker: Arno
en: Certainement, Monsieur. (Yes, sir).

speaker: Perrault
en: Messire! Messire de la Serre! Attendez! Nom de Dieu... Nom de Dieu... Nom de Dieu (My lord! Lord De La Serre! Wait! Jesus Christ all mighty lord!)

speaker: Arno
en: Some trouble, mon ami (my friend)?

speaker: Perrault
en: A letter... for Messire (Lord) De La Serre... it's very important!

speaker: Arno
en: Calm yourself Perrault! That letter won't reach Monsieur (Mister) De La Serre any faster if you drop dead of exhaustion. Give it here—I'll catch him.

speaker: Perrault
en: He must receive it today! It's very

speaker: Arno
en: Very important, yes. I heard you the first time. I'll see that he gets it.

speaker: Arno
en: Monsieur (Mister) De La Serre! Stop! Make way, make way! Dammit, slow down! Apparently walnut is a popular finish this season. Who is driving this carriage? Pelops? Arretez! (Stop!)

speaker: Arno
en: Monsieur (Mister) De La Serre!

speaker: Arno
en: Mes excuses (Apologies). Wrong carriage. What I need is a bird's eye view.

speaker: Arno
en: There you are!

speaker: Guard
en: Back of the line!

speaker: Guards
en: No entry! Are you deaf as well as stupid? Du vent! (Piss off!) You're not getting in, boy!

speaker: Louis XVI
en: Messieurs, ce jour que mon cœur attendait depuis longtemps est enfin arrivé et je me vois entouré des représentants de la nation à laquelle je me fais gloire de commander. Un long intervalle s'était écoulé depuis les dernières tenues des états-généraux et, quoique la convocation de ces assemblées parût être tombée en désuétude, je n'ai pas balancé à rétablir un usage dont le royaume peut tirer une nouvelle force et qui peut ouvrir à la nation une nouvelle source de bonheur. La dette de l'État, déjà immense à mon avènement au trône, s'est encore accrue sous mon règne. Une guerre dispendieuse mais honorable en est la cause. L'augmentation des impôts en a été la suite nécessaire et a rendu plus sensible leur inégale répartition. Une inquiétude générale, un désir exagéré d'innovations se sont emparés des esprits et finiraient par égarer totalement les opinions si on ne se hâtait de les fixer par une réunion d'avis sages et modérés. C'est dans cette confiance, Messieurs, que je vous ai rassemblés et je vois avec sensibilité qu'elle a déjà été justifiée par les dispositions que les deux premiers ordres ont montrées à renoncer à leurs privilèges pécuniaires. L'espérance que j'ai conçue de voir tous les ordres, réunis de sentiments, concourir avec moi au bien général de l'État, ne sera point trompée. J'ai déjà ordonné dans les dépenses des retranchements considérables. Vous me présenterez à cet égard des idées que je recevrais avec empressement. Mais, malgré la ressource que peut offrir l'économie la plus sévère, je crains, Messieurs, de ne pas pouvoir soulager mes sujets aussi promptement que je le désirerais. Je ferai mettre sous vos yeux la situation exacte des finances et, quand vous l'aurez examinée, je suis assuré d'avance que vous me proposerez les moyens les plus efficaces pour y établir un ordre permanent et affermir le crédit public. Ce grand et salutaire ouvrage, qui assurera le bonheur du royaume au-dedans et sa considération au-dehors, vous occupera essentiellement. Les esprits sont dans l'agitation, mais une assemblée de représentants de la nation n'écoutera sans doute que les conseils de la sagesse et de la prudence. Vous aurez jugé vous-mêmes, Messieurs, qu'on s'en est écarté dans plusieurs occasions récentes, mais l'esprit dominant de vos délibérations répondra aux sentiments d'une nation généreuse et dont l'amour pour ses rois a toujours fait le trait distinctif. J'éloignerai tout autre souvenir. Je connais l'autorité et la puissance d'un roi juste au milieu d'un peuple fidèle et attaché de tout temps aux principes de la monarchie. Ils ont fait la gloire et l'éclat de la France. Je dois en être le soutien et je le serai constamment. Mais tout ce qu'on peut attendre du plus tendre intérêt au bonheur public, tout ce qu'on peut demander à un souverain, le premier ami de ses peuples, vous pouvez, vous devez l'espérer de mes sentiments. Puisse, Messieurs, un heureux accord régner dans cette assemblée et cette époque devenir à jamais mémorable pour le bonheur et la prospérité du royaume ! C'est le souhait de mon cœur, c'est le plus ardent de mes vœux, c'est enfin le prix que j'attends de la droiture de mes intentions et de mon amour pour mes peuples. Mon garde des Sceaux va vous expliquer plus amplement mes intentions et j'ai ordonné au directeur général des Finances de vous en exposer l'état. (Gentlemen, the day my heart as long waited for has finally arrived and I see...)

speaker: Citizen 1
en: Can we just... leave?

speaker: Citizen 2
en: That may be considered treason.

speaker: Citizen 3
en: Do you understand any of this?

speaker: Citizen 4
en: God, is he still talking?

speaker: Arno
en: Where the devil are they?

speaker: Arno
en: Finally!

speaker: Arno
en: Not these two again. Must have tailed me from the Estate.

speaker: Citizen 5
en: How long do you think he'll keep talking?

speaker: François
en: So, who or what will take its place? Another King? A council of capable men?

speaker: Mirabeau
en: That is the question, isn't it?

speaker: François
en: A truce, then?

speaker: Arno
en: What the devil was that about?

speaker: Arno
en: Now now... we can resolve this without recourse to violence...can't we?

speaker: Victor
en: Get him, Hugo!

speaker: Arno
en: I suppose not.

speaker: Hugo
en: Rragh!

speaker: Victor
en: Damn cabinet!

speaker: Arno
en: Easy, big fella!

speaker: Victor
en: Think you can steal from me?

speaker: Hugo
en: No rich old man to save you now.

speaker: Victor
en: Let's see you run away this time!

speaker: Hugo
en: You can't take us both at once.

speaker: Victor
en: Hand over the watch!

speaker: Arno
en: Not your day, is it Victor?

speaker: Guard
en: Open up in there!

speaker: Arno
en: To your health, gentlemen.

speaker: Guard
en: You, boy! Stop! What are you doing there?!

speaker: Arno
en: Running.

speaker: Guard
en: He's getting away!

speaker: Arno
en: No getting back in there now. I'll catch them back at home, I suppose.

speaker: Élise
en: They're bringing the king up now. Are you sure Germain will be there?

speaker: Arno
en: Yes, I'm sure.

speaker: Élise
en: Then what are we waiting for?

speaker: Arno
en: Let's split up. We'll cover more ground that way.

speaker: Speaker
en: Bring forth the condemned!

speaker: Speaker
en: Silence! Silence all! Before God almighty, let justice be served upon this stage with dignity! Heed here this fallen man! This tyrant! This profaner of the brotherhood of man. Wretched and false friend of beleaguered France! Wicked and deceitful! Here you pay through death the debt incurred by your thoughtless reign. Bear witness all. This is the punishment that awaits ALL CITIZENS - man or woman, lord or peasant - who would betray the principles of our young nation, by deed or by thought! Any citizen who conspires against our new won liberty with loose talk... any citizen who tarnishes the gleam of our glorious Revolution shall meet this same fate. What we do here today will ring through the vaults of history! Our children, and our children's children, will look back upon this day as the birth of freedom! May all mankind be so liberated! Bring forth the condemned!

speaker: Germain
en: Hello, Arno.

speaker: Arno
en: Germain.

speaker: Germain
en: It's fitting you're here to witness the rebirth of the Templar Order. After all, you were there for its conception.

speaker: Arno
en: de la Serre.

speaker: Germain
en: Ah, I tried to make him see. But the Order had become corrupt, clutching at power and privilege for their own sake.

speaker: Arno
en: But you could set it right, is that it? All by killing the man in charge.

speaker: Germain
en: No, de la Serre's death was only the first stage. This is the culmination.

speaker: Louis
en: (People, I die innocent. Gentlemen, I am innocent of everything I have been charged with. My wish and hope is that my blood may consolidate the well-being of the French people.)

speaker: Germain
en: The King is... merely a symbol. A symbol can inspire fear, and fear can inspire control - but men inevitably lose their fear of symbols. As you can see.

speaker: Germain
en: This was the truth de Molay died for: the is nothing but the reflection of sunlight upon gold. When the Crown and Church are ground to dust, we who control the gold will decide the future.

speaker: Germain
en: Jacques de Molay, vous êtes vengé. (Jacques de Molay, you are avenged.)

speaker: Germain
en: I must take my leave. Good day to you. Kill him.

speaker: Élise
en: GO!

speaker: Arno
en: Quite an entrance.

speaker: Élise
en: What are you doing? Go after him!

speaker: Arno
en: I'm not leaving you here to die!

speaker: Guards
en: Protect the Grand Master! Kill her!

speaker: Arno
en: Élise, it's time to go!

speaker: Élise
en: I can handle it! Go after Germain!

speaker: Arno
en: Élise....

speaker: Élise
en: No, dammit!

speaker: Élise
en: Go after him!

speaker: Arno
en: Not without you!

speaker: Arno
en: More of them!

speaker: Élise
en: I can handle it! Go after Germain! Just go! Follow Germain!

speaker: Arno
en: It's not worth it! Don't be absurd, you can't fight so many on your own!

speaker: Élise
en: Go! I'll buy you time!

speaker: Arno
en: Élise! Wait!

speaker: Arno
en: Élise, it's over! Let's go!

speaker: Élise
en: I'm not letting him get away! Dammit, he's getting away!

speaker: Élise
en: Empty. He must have gone on foot!

speaker: Arno
en: Élise!

speaker: Élise
en: He's gone. Dammit! Our one chance....

speaker: Arno
en: It's not over. We'll find another lead

speaker: Élise
en: No, we won't! You think he'll be so careless now, knowing how close at heel we are? You were given a golden opportunity to end his life, and you refused to take it!

speaker: Arno
en: To save your life!

speaker: Élise
en: It isn't yours to save!

speaker: Arno
en: What are you saying?

speaker: Élise
en: I'm willing to risk everything to put Germain down. If you don't have the stomach for revenge... then I don't need your help!

speaker: Arno
en: Élise - Élise!

speaker: Charlotte
en: Something I can help you with?

speaker: Arno
en: What is this place?

speaker: Charlotte
en: It connects to the sanctuary. Less flashy than the Sainte-Chapelle entrance, but we own the building. Used to be part of our intelligence network. But the place has fallen on hard times...

speaker: Arno
en: How can I help?

speaker: Charlotte
en: I'll keep an ear out for any opportunities that come up. You might also speak to the intendant about renovating the building itself.

speaker: Arno
en: I'm not exactly flushed with coin just now.

speaker: Charlotte
en: Any revenues the café generates are yours to do with as you see fit. The money is deposited in the chest in the study. And the more improvements you make...

speaker: Arno
en: The more revenue.

speaker: Charlotte
en: Quite. You might also find that expanding our reach into other districts will pay dividends.

speaker: Arno
en: Merci. (Thanks.)

speaker: Augustin
en: Here for a fight, monsieur? (sir?)

speaker: Arno
en: Come again?

speaker: Augustin
en: A training match, that is. An Assassin can never be too well-prepared.

speaker: Arno
en: Isn't our mandate to work in the shadows? Stay undetected and all that?

speaker: Augustin
en: Call this the fallback option. Better to practice here in safety than pick a fight with ruffians in the streets, no?

speaker: Arno
en: Touché.

speaker: Hervé
en: Welcome to the Assassin clubhouse, monsieur. (sir.)

speaker: Arno
en: I assume these quarters aren't open to the public.

speaker: Hervé
en: No indeed. This is a private clubhouse for our brother and sister Assassins.

speaker: Arno
en: Because belonging to just one secret society is passé?

speaker: Hervé
en: Hm. Certain missions are too much for any one Assassin to take on alone. In those instances, many prefer to work with the same team consistently. You develop a sense of each other's strengths and weaknesses, an understanding of what each will do in a crisis. Keeping a club makes it easier to organize such teams.

speaker: Arno
en: I suppose that's better than rousting whoever happens to on hand.

speaker: Hervé
en: Quite so.

speaker: Hervé
en: Impressive, no?

speaker: Arno
en: What is it?

speaker: Hervé
en: An heirloom of the Brotherhood. That armor was worn by Thomas de Carneillon.

speaker: Arno
en: I have no earthly idea who that is.

speaker: Hervé
en: He led the raid that captured Jacques de Molay. Broke the Templars' power in Europe for over a century. It used to be that an Assassin who did a great service for the Brotherhood and for France would be given his armor in thanks. The seal that opens the vault was lost two hundred years ago—it hasn't been opened since.

speaker: Arno
en: I can see why calling a locksmith was out of the question. Tell me about this seal.

speaker: Hervé
en: It consisted of three rings: one for each of the three doors. But the seal was broken before it was lost—the fragments are no doubt scattered around Paris, with only the vaguest clues as to their whereabouts.

speaker: Arno
en: And if someone were to find all of them? Would you say that he had done a great service for the Brotherhood and France?

speaker: Hervé
en: I suppose I would, at that.

speaker: Letter
en: A group of criminals has taken advantage of the current disarray of the city government to oppress citizens along the Bièvre. They can be found extorting merchants in the north of the district. Find the thugs and follow them to their captain. Assassinate him. —The Council

speaker: Citizen 1
en: I just paid! Leave me alone!

speaker: Arno
en: I'm here to help.

speaker: Citizen 1
en: Oh, thank god. Those damn thugs come by every few days, tell me "pay up or else" and what am I gonna do? I-I pay. I pay through the nose.

speaker: Citizen 2
en: What do you want?

speaker: Arno
en: What happened?

speaker: Citizen 2
en: Oh, I thought you were another one of 'em. They come in here, toss things around, demand money. I have to pay! Otherwise, I'll lose everything.

speaker: Arno
en: Who are they?

speaker: Citizen 2
en: Bunch of hooligans. They've got some place they take the money and the things they steal, but god knows where it is.

speaker: Citizen 3
en: God-damn them all to hell!

speaker: Arno
en: Let me guess.

speaker: Citizen 3
en: I wouldn't pay. They got no right. Broke up the place and damn near broke my arm. It's got to stop!

speaker: Citizen 4
en: The thugs! I know where they are! They went through here. Come on, I'll show you!

speaker: Thug 1
en: Yeah? Don't let it happen again!

speaker: Thug 2
en: Don't worry, we'll be around.

speaker: Cultist 1
en: An intruder!

speaker: Cultist 2
en: He does not belong!

speaker: Cultist 3
en: Protect the Guest!

speaker: Arno
en: The Guest. Louis XIV. I don't think he is coming back.

speaker: Arno
en: I got your message. What's going on?

speaker: Élise
en: We may have gone too far in discrediting Robespierre.

speaker: Arno
en: What happened?

speaker: Élise
en: He's been arrested.

speaker: Arno
en: What?

speaker: Élise
en: Apparently he made vague threats about a purge against "enemies of the state" and the Committee turned on him. They're taking him to Luxembourg prison. He's scheduled for execution in the morning.

speaker: Arno
en: Then we'd best get to him first.

speaker: Jacobins
en: Death to the enemies of freedom! Paris for Robespierre!

speaker: Protesters
en: Down with the tyrant Robespierre! Paris for the guillotine, more like. The blood of Danton choke him!

speaker: Arno
en: What in the hell...?

speaker: Élise
en: These men were National Guard. Robespierre's escort. Damn, if we've lost him....

speaker: Arno
en: Let's not panic just yet. We might be able to find some sign of what happened.

speaker: Arno
en: Élise! What happened here?

speaker: Guardsman 1
en: We were ambushed. Troops from the Paris Commune attacked us en route. They were trying to free the prisoners.

speaker: Arno
en: Did they take Robespierre?

speaker: Guardsman 1
en: I'm not sure. The fighting left me behind. They fell back that way.

speaker: Arno
en: Go find yourself a doctor.

speaker: Élise
en: If he's still in custody, they'll have taken him to the Luxembourg prison.

speaker: Arno
en: But if not, they'll need to hole up somewhere nearby. They won't get very far with half the city turned out against Robespierre.

speaker: Élise
en: I'll check the prison. You follow the riots, see if you can pick up a trail.

speaker: Arno
en: Right.

speaker: Arno
en: Where is Robespierre?

speaker: Guardsman 2
en: They took him that way.

speaker: Arno
en: Where did they go?

speaker: Guardsman 3
en: They went that way.

speaker: Protesters
en: Bastard! Murderer! Tyrant!

speaker: Commune guard 1
en: Run, sir! We'll hold this lot until reinforcements arrive!

speaker: Robespierre
en: You are a hero of France, (my friend!)

speaker: Protesters
en: Never again the tyranny! Remember the Girondists!

speaker: Jacobins
en: The Commune stands for Robespierre! The Supreme Being save us! Robespierre! Robespierre! Traitors! Is this how you thank the savior of France?

speaker: Protester
en: Remember Danton!

speaker: Commune guard 2
en: Thank God you made it, sir. The Commune stands with you.

speaker: Robespierre
en: Thank you, Sergeant. Your loyalty does you credit.

speaker: Commune guard 3
en: Best get inside, sir. The Convention's soldiers will be here soon.

speaker: Robespierre
en: Yes, of course. I place myself in your capable hands.

speaker: Official
en: Be it known that the Paris Commune, by dint of its actions protecting the criminal Robespierre, is now in open rebellion against the nation. Soldiers under the command of the National Convention have been dispatched to apprehend the traitor Robespierre and his followers. Citizens are advised to stay in their homes while justice is carried out. Be it further known that Citizen Robespierre, Citizen Hanriot, and all their allies are declared outlaw! Any citizen found to be aiding these criminals will share their fate upon the guillotine. Revolutionary justice shall prevail!

speaker: Commune guard 4
en: What the Hell was that?

speaker: Commune guard 5
en: Robespierre's . He just jumped out the window!

speaker: Commune guard 6
en: I didn't sign up for this...

speaker: Commune guard 7
en: How long does Hanriot think he can hold them off?

speaker: Commune guard 8
en: Robespierre's going to get us all killed.

speaker: Commune guard 9
en: Any news?

speaker: Commune guard 10
en: The Convention's called out Barras.

speaker: Commune guard 12
en: We'll never hold this place if the Convention attacks.

speaker: Commune guard 13
en: First sign of Convention troops, I'm out of here.

speaker: Commune guard 14
en: Shh, Someone'll hear!

speaker: Commune guard 15
en: Five more were missing at last muster. At this rate, the Convention won't have to fire a shot.

speaker: Robespierre
en: Damn him! I sent for Germain hours ago!

speaker: Robespierre
en: Shit!

speaker: Robespierre
en: Germain warned me about you. You're one of them, aren't you? An Assassin.

speaker: Arno
en: Not anymore. Where is Germain?

speaker: Arno
en: Élise?

speaker: Élise
en: We don't have much time. Where's Germain?

speaker: Robespierre
en: I will never talk.

speaker: Élise
en: Then write.

speaker: Élise
en: The Temple. I should have known. I hope you enjoy revolutionary justice, (sir.)

speaker: Guardsman 4
en: Seize him!

speaker: Arno
en: It is a little confusing.

speaker: Dueler 1
en: But of course, my friend! A duel it is!

speaker: Judge 1
en: I'll serve as a second to both of you.

speaker: Judge 1
en: Stop! A hit!

speaker: Dueler 1
en: Well fought! You are the victor.

speaker: Judge 1
en: We have a champion!

speaker: Dueler 2
en: Oh, my! A duelist, are we? How amusing. This man will judge the hits. I have an appointment presently. But this shan't take much time.

speaker: Dueler 2
en: Enough! Leave me alone!

speaker: Judge 2
en: Come back, coward!

speaker: Dueler 3
en: Duel you? Preposterous! Oh, very well.

speaker: Judge 3
en: I will oversee the contest. He who draws first blood, wins.

speaker: Dueler 3
en: I could use a bit of practice.

speaker: Judge 3
en: A hit! The challenger wins!

speaker: Dueler 3
en: I will not yield!

speaker: Judge 3
en: Cease! The fight is over!

speaker: Dueler 3
en: Rubbish. To the death!

speaker: Alphonse
en: I accept your challenge, upstart!

speaker: Second
en: A duel it is! I shall be your second, Alphonse!

speaker: Judge 4
en: I'll adjudicate!

speaker: Alphonse
en: I was first in my class at the School of Gentleman Cadets!

speaker: Second
en: Indeed he was! And well deserved!

speaker: Second
en: Yes, Alphonse! Well played!

speaker: Second
en: Bastard! Take that!

speaker: Alphonse
en: I shall never yield!

speaker: Judge 4
en: Stop! This is highly irregular!

speaker: Second
en: You can't defeat Alphonse!

speaker: Alphonse
en: Come on!

speaker: Judge 5
en: I'll adjudicate!

speaker: Lenormand
en: You are ready for the next step? odd. I did not foresee that at all! I have an acquaintanceship with Denis Molinier, who dabbles in alchemy. I suspect that it is he who possess the other part of the missing mechanism. I advise you to go to his house on the Ile St. Louis and steal it! Yes! Steal it!

speaker: Guard
en: Sir. The order of monks we spoke about. It appears they may have obtained the first part of Flamel's mechanism.

speaker: Molinier
en: Track them down and take it! With the complete mechanism, we'll have access to the last of Flamel's laboratory. Say nothing to anyone!

speaker: Guard
en: Understood.

speaker: Arno
en: This rusty bit of metal must be part of the mechanism that Mademoiselle Lenormand was talking about. And this completes the mechanism. So much for the Templars.

speaker: Lenormand
en: Ah! The second part of the device. You have the necessary pieces. Return to me when you are ready to take the final step!

scene: Flamel's Secret: The Elixir of Life
speaker: Lenormand
en: Ah! I foresaw your return! Come, I have something to tell you! This card here, the Key! And here, the Sun! Against these other cards, it is quite clear that many people are in search of Nicolas Flamel's secret laboratory that has remained hidden these hundreds of years. You are ready? I commend you, but I cannot help you. The final mystery of where to find Flamel's laboratory is beyond my powers. Only you can solve the enigma. My intuition tells me you will do well!

scene: Flamel's Secret: The Elixir of Life
speaker: Monk
en: Spirit of Nicolas Flamel! We await the interloper to take vengeance upon him!

scene: Flamel's Secret: The Elixir of Life
speaker: Lenormand
en: Have you brought the Elixir? Of course you have! I knew you would not fail me. Many thanks, my dear Arno. I foresee a great future for you.

en: Yes, a giant! He killed a man! Huge! Blue and green skin. Dressed in black. Terrifying!
