en: I saw him just now! He'd just killed someone! A huge, blue, cavernous mouth with no teeth at all! May the Supreme Being save us!

speaker: Citizen 5
en: My dear husband! Look! Crushed to death, for what? He refused to give everything he had to the Giant Iscariotte.

speaker: Giant Iscariotte
en: Who disturbs me here? Come, my blood-lust is not yet quenched.

speaker: Bishop
en: That's Luxembourg Palace. Before the revolution, it was Paris' first museum. The artwork inside was supposed to be transferred to the Louvre, but some of it went missing. It seems the local nobility kept it for their own personal stash. Find the artwork, and get it out. The Assassins will return it to the Louvre. More Assassins, more loot! Well, actually all but one are fake - you need to find the right one. Go. I'm ratcheting up the difficulty for this. Think of it as training. You need to find where the loot's hidden first.

speaker: Bishop
en: Your princess is in another castle. Wah-Waaaaaah! Nope! Try the next one. Fake. Sorry. Yeah, that's a fake. Sorry. That's one of the fakes. This one's a dud... Not what you're looking for.

speaker: Bishop
en: That's the one. That's what you're looking for. You got it. Nice job. Nice work. This is it. We have a winner! That's it. Good work. Right on. You got it.

speaker: IV - Natura
en: was a virtual representation of one of Arno Dorian's genetic memories, relived by a Helix initiate through the Helix Navigator.

speaker: Trenet
en: , Honoré! If it weren't for General Lafayette

speaker: Mirabeau
en: Enough, enough! The room is fogged with your bluster! All hot air and no action. Yet here's a man with good news, I think. Arno, what did you learn from the silversmith?

speaker: Bellec
en: Poison. They're catching up.

speaker: Arno
en: Germain made that pin, and others like it, for a man named Lafrenière.

speaker: Mirabeau
en: Are you sure?

speaker: Arno
en: Certain.

speaker: Mirabeau
en: Grand Master de la Serre spoke highly of his loyalty. Hm, very well. I suppose the course is clear, Arno. Find (Mister) Lafrenière

speaker: Arno
en: I have done so already, (Mister). He is no threat.

speaker: Bellec
en: What are you saying, pisspot?

speaker: Arno
en: I had a lead on Lafrenière. I followed it, and I killed him.

speaker: Quemar
en: Unthinkable!

speaker: Bellec
en: What the hell were you thinking?

speaker: Trenet
en: I've never heard of such phenomenal hubris!

speaker: Beylier
en: How dare you defy the Creed?!

speaker: Trenet
en: The arrogance of it is just astounding!

speaker: Quemar
en: Bloody-handed murder!

speaker: Beylier
en: What gives you the right?

speaker: Bellec
en: The next time you circumvent the Council, I'll rip you a new arsehole!

speaker: Mirabeau
en: While this Council admires your zeal, it is not your place to choose your own targets. You should have reported your findings to us.

speaker: Arno
en: Forgive me, Mentor. I believed I had found the man who ordered (Mister) de la Serre's murder. When I discovered further evidence that suggested he was about to strike at the Brotherhood in force, I took action.

speaker: Quemar
en: Believed? Suggested?

speaker: Arno
en: I am... no longer certain of Lafrenière's motivations. In his memories, I saw him writing the letter that would have warned (Mister) de la Serre of his betrayal. When he spoke of his impending attack, he mentioned a club in the Marais - not one of our safehouses.

speaker: Mirabeau
en: What do you make of this?

speaker: Arno
en: I cannot say. I would like to investigate further.

speaker: Beylier
en: I don't like this. The boy is a gifted Assassin, but I fear he is obsessed with a private vendetta. Let another follow this lead.

speaker: Arno
en: We don't have time! Whatever Lafrenière was planning, it happens tonight!

speaker: Mirabeau
en: He did ask permission this time, Guillaume.

speaker: Mirabeau
en: Go then. See what you can learn. But no more rash action, hmm?

speaker: Arno
en: Yes, Mentor.

speaker: Arno
en: This is the place. What was Lafrenière so interested in?

speaker: Rouille
en: Get him upstairs. Quickly.

speaker: Arno
en: La Touche, old friend. You do get about, don't you?

speaker: Guard 1
en: Why in God's name are we patrolling the catacombs? Have corpses suddenly become worth more than gold?

speaker: Guard 2
en: It's the renovations. Until they've finished, the tunnels open right up into the basement. We can't very well have thieves coming up through the floor and robbing the place blind, can we?

speaker: Guard 3
en: What's going on in the back room?

speaker: Guard 4
en: Dunno. And if you're smart, you'll let it lie.

speaker: Guard 3
en: What's that supposed to mean?

speaker: Guard 4
en: Just that some folk don't like other people prying into their affairs. Savvy?

speaker: Guest 1
en: How late you think they'll go tonight?

speaker: Guest 2
en: Lord knows. Get these politicians talking and they never shut up.

speaker: Guest 1
en: I guess I'd better put some coffee on then.

speaker: Robespierre
en: It was a crime worthy of death under Tiberius to praise Brutus. Caligula condemned to death those who were so sacrilegious as to undress before the image of the emperor. Once tyranny invented the crime of —which were actions either indifferent or heroic—who could have dared to think that it merited a punishment more gentle than death without rendering himself guilty of the same crime? When fanaticism, borne of the monstrous union between ignorance and despotism, invented in its turn the crime of sacrilege, when it conceived in its delirium the project of avenging God himself, was it not necessary that it offer him blood, and bring him down to their level of the monsters who said they were his image? The death penalty is necessary, say the partisans of ancient and barbarous routine. Without it, there is no brake strong enough for crime. Who told you this? Have you calculated all the gears by which penal laws can act on human sensibility? Alas, before death, how much physical and moral pain can man endure? The desire to live cedes before pride, the most imperious of all the passions that master the heart of man. The most terrible of all punishments for social man is opprobrium, is the overwhelming sight of public execration. When the legislator can strike the citizen in so many sensitive places and in so many ways, why would he reduce himself to employing the death penalty? Punishments are not imposed to torment the guilty, but in order to prevent crime by the fear of incurring. It has been observed that in free countries, crime was more rare and penal laws more gentle. All ideas hold together. Free countries are those where the rights of man are respected and where, consequently, the laws are just. Where they offend humanity by an excess of rigor, this is proof that the dignity of man is not known there, that that of the citizen doesn't exist. It is proof that the legislator is nothing but a master who commands slaves and who pitilessly punishes them according to his whim. I thus conclude that the death penalty should be abrogated. (Thank you. Thank you. Many thanks.)

speaker: Guest 3
en: Lovely speech.

speaker: Guest 4
en: Quite. The man's a visionary.

speaker: Guest 5
en: Abolish the death penalty? Next he'll be saying we should do away with branding!

speaker: Guest 6
en: Perhaps we should start sending criminals off to the tropics, like the British.

speaker: Guest 5
en: Hah!

speaker: Guest 6
en: That will turn some heads at the Assembly.

speaker: Guest 5
en: If Mirabeau will actually yield the floor.

speaker: Guest 6
en: True enough.

speaker: Lévesque
en: How much longer must we wait? I do have other business to attend to.

speaker: La Touche
en: Just a little longer. The Grand Master wants the politicos thinned out before we begin.

speaker: Le Peletier
en: I trust we'll finally learn the meaning behind our recent... activities?

speaker: La Touche
en: All will be made clear.

speaker: Lévesque
en: I don't like it. The plan is still too vulnerable—and let's not forget Lafrenière is still out there somewhere, waiting to burn us all at the stake.

speaker: La Touche
en: So, you haven't heard yet, then?

speaker: Lévesque
en: Heard what?

speaker: La Touche
en: Lafrenière is dead. Hours ago, in fact. Assassins.

speaker: Le Peletier
en: That seems... convenient.

speaker: La Touche
en: Ah. That's the thing about Assassins. Point them at a Templar conspiracy and they ask no questions. They go right for the killing. Predictable that way.

speaker: La Touche
en: Come, we'll fetch the Captain and get started.

speaker: Rouille
en: Come on, speak up! I need an answer, friend. It's a simple question. Just tell me what I want to know. Tick tock, mate. No need to make this any harder, eh?

speaker: La Touche
en: Have you finished?

speaker: Rouille
en: Near enough. Now, here's the thing. I can go on like this all day. But you... You've got an hour left in you. Two at the most. Half if I bring out the sharp bits. So why not skip the endgame and go directly to mate? Tell me where it is and all this can be over.

speaker: Prisoner
en: Luxembourg....

speaker: Rouille
en: What was that?

speaker: Prisoner
en: Palais du Luxembourg.

speaker: Rouille
en: You are a smart man.

speaker: La Touche
en: Rouille? Clean up your mess. It's time.

speaker: Rouille
en: Be right there. You heard the weasel, boys.

speaker: La Touche
en: Did you really throw him out the window?

speaker: Rouille
en: Trash belongs in the gutter.

speaker: La Touche
en: Sloppy. Someone might have seen.

speaker: Rouille
en: Who? My boys are watching the whole place. They'll deal with any good Samaritans.

speaker: La Touche
en: They'd better. The Grand Master won't be happy if the whole plan comes unraveled because of one dead peon.

speaker: Rouille
en: You were right. King Louis has been talking to all sorts he shouldn't have. Plotting against the Revolution out of one side of his mouth while he promises to support the Constitution out the other.

speaker: Germain
en: Good. I trust you can get this information into the proper hands, Monsieur le Peletier?

speaker: Le Peletier
en: Of course, Grand Master. With this evidence in hand, the King's conviction is certain.

speaker: Rouille
en: Told you I could make him talk.

speaker: Germain
en: You've done well, Captain. Marie?

speaker: Lévesque
en: The price of grain is higher than ever, Grand Master. Our agents are in place to divert the shipments to our docks. They await only your command.

speaker: Germain
en: Good... Starve them. Through famine and fury they will see their false masters for what they are... But do it gradually. Too quickly and we'll draw the wrong sort of attention, yes?

speaker: Lévesque
en: What you're asking will take at least a year, Grand Master. If not two.

speaker: Germain
en: The Great Work requires patience, my friend. If Paris must suffer a while longer so the world might be remade, then so be it.

speaker: Rouille
en: Why not just kill him and be done with it? One of my boys, a knife, a dark hallway... easy peasy.

speaker: Germain
en: We want a condemned man, Captain, not a martyr. Have patience.

speaker: Le Peletier
en: Respectfully, Grand Master, patience is all well and fine, but the longer we wait, the greater the chance of discovery.

speaker: La Touche
en: The Assassins already found Sivert and le Roi des Thunes.

speaker: Germain
en: Sivert and le Roi already served their purpose. Their destruction, while inconvenient, is no obstacle. And the Assassins have already proved useful when properly led.

speaker: Rouille
en: What about the de la Serre brat? She could be dangerous if she manages to rally the old guard.

speaker: Germain
en: That situation will be resolved.

speaker: Lévesque
en: How so?

speaker: Germain
en: Mademoiselle de la Serre will soon be on her way to l'Hôtel Voysin, eager to speak with Monsieur Lafrenière. Sadly, Monsieur Lafrenière has nothing left to say.

speaker: Arno
en: Élise...

speaker: Rouille
en: Clever, Grand Master. But you've had your brush with the Assassins as well. Respectfully, you won't always be so lucky.

speaker: Germain
en: Quite right. I shall leave the execution of our work to you good ladies and gentlemen. For my part I will retire to the Sanctuary and await the final phase. Will that satisfy you, Captain?

speaker: Rouille
en: I'll see the watch tripled.

speaker: Germain
en: Very well. May the Father of Understanding guide you.

speaker: All
en: May the Father of Understanding guide us.

speaker: Guard 5
en: Come on. We'll lock up down here and go for a pint.

speaker: Guards
en: Stop him! He's a royalist spy! There's a spy on the loose! Find the spy! Don't let the spy escape! The spy's still here! Catch him! Watch the exits! The spy will be making a run for it! Seems we have a spy, boys! No spy's escaping on my watch!

speaker: Méricourt
en: Jacobins! It is your turn to bleed!

speaker: Bishop
en: Théroigne de Méricourt. A revolutionary out for revenge.

speaker: Théroigne
en: We declared the Rights of Man - but what of WOMEN!

speaker: Jacobin leader 1
en: Robespierre names you an enemy of the Republic, harlot. You have no rights.

speaker: Bishop
en: Jacobins had it in for Méricourt. Whipped her to within an inch of her life.

speaker: Méricourt
en: The Terror ends tonight!

speaker: Jacobin leader 1
en: Save a bullet for yourself, and pray you have better aim than Robespierre.

speaker: Bishop
en: This is what's left of the Jacobins, the radical party behind the Reign of Terror. Hasn't been their week. Maximilien Robespierre, Jacobin leader, died the day before.thumb|right|250px|Robespierre's execution.

speaker: Jacobin 1
en: Tunnel is ready.

speaker: Jacobin leader 1
en: Good.

speaker: Bishop
en: The Jacobins are making their last stand here, and plan to flee Paris. Infilitrate the Jacobin hideout and end the Reign of Terror.

speaker: Bishop
en: The Jacobin Club is too well-guarded. Méricourt will get cut to pieces unless you thin the ranks.

speaker: Jacobin 2
en: Who is this woman to threaten us?

speaker: Jacobin 3
en: That's Théroigne de Méricourt.

speaker: Jacobin 2
en: Never heard of her.

speaker: Jacobin 3
en: Méricourt was the Girondist war chief. She's killed dozens of men in battle.

speaker: Jacobin 2
en: Who, her?!

speaker: Jacobin 3
en: She's no woman. She's a devil in a dress.

speaker: Théroigne
en: My thanks, but I ask you for another favour. Find their escape tunnels, and kill the Jacobins before they escape.

speaker: Bishop
en: Shit! There's more upstairs.

speaker: Bishop
en: You've got to find the entrance to the tunnels.

speaker: Bishop
en: Get down into those tunnels and take out the Jacobin leaders.

speaker: Jacobin 4
en: Are we going West?

speaker: Jacobin 5
en: I heard we are going to Normandy, then across the channel.

speaker: Jacobin 4
en: I guess we will find out soon.

speaker: Jacobin leader 1
en: That bitch Méricourt is at our heels. I can't believe those idiots couldn't keep that scum at bay.

speaker: Jacobin leader 2
en: She had help, from whom I don't know.

speaker: Jacobin leader 1
en: I don't need excuses; I need to get out of this tomb. We need to move!

speaker: Jacobin leader 3
en: The Italians have promised safe passage to Corsica. We must reach by morning.

speaker: Jacobin leader 4
en: I've just received word that the church has been taken, we must move quickly! Get the men ready to move at my signal!

speaker: Bishop
en: Good work, you got 'em. Time to get out of these sewers.

speaker: Bishop
en: The Jacobins never did regain power in France. The Assassins can take some credit for that.

speaker: Jupiter
en: was a virtual representation of one of Arno Dorian's genetic memories, relived by a Helix initiate through the Helix Navigator.

speaker: Arianne (friend of victim)
en: Who would do such a thing? Oh, my poor Alexandre! We had a rendez-vous. I arrived at the stroke of noon and that cannon suddenly fired! He was instantly killed. As far as I know, he hadn't an enemy in the world!

speaker: Gilbert Duchamps (daily visitor to park)
en: I come by everyday to set my pocket-watch. I saw the young man waiting over there, holding a bouquet of flowers. Then BAM! Very upsetting as you can imagine... I did notice one thing, the cannon usually points in a different direction.

speaker: La Grouille (vagabond)
en: Last night I did manage to wake up and I swear I saw somebody fiddling with the cannon! Then he limped away. A cripple, I guess. Then I conked out.

speaker: Olympe ("lady of the evening")
en: Hey, good-lookin. Oh, the murder? I feel sorry for the poor guy, but heh! It was a real show! Pretty much blew a giant hole in him! You know who you should talk to? Sergeant Saint-Bris. He's the veteran loads that cannon every morning. Check Café Fevrier, table by the window.

speaker: Guy Langin (frequent customer)
en: I come here quite often. I was here this morning, in fact. It's the only time I've seen someone sitting with the sergeant over there. As it happens, I think I know the man from my army days. Don't recall the name, but I believe he became a scientist of some sort. He may actually work at the Collège de Quatre Nations.

speaker: Café server (At the Café Février)
en: Dammit, I missed the whole thing!... No, otherwise today pretty much like any other. Unless you count the old colonel who came limping in this morning. Had a coffee with the sergeant. They seemed like old pals.

speaker: Sergeant Saint-Bris (semi-retired veteran)
en: I am Sergeant Saint-Bris, veteran of the , and I don't take kindly to jokes, young man! It is my honor and duty to load that damn solar contraption every damn morning. I load it with scraps of paper. Paper! Couldn't hurt a child. Today was a day like any other. Now, leave me alone.

speaker: Robert Roussea (Clock-maker and inventor)
en: I heard the shot and all the screaming. I'm the inventor of that cannon, you know. Quite ingenious, I think. Unfortunate business, the killing, but it will bring attention to my invention!

speaker: Honorine Sagne (neighbor)
en: I've just heard. Poor man. I can't understand it, he was such a pleasant fellow.

speaker: Institute Clerk (Overseer of chemistry competition)
en: Good morning, citizen! I'm afraid that we cannot accept any more entries into the contest. However, you can still make a monetary pledge to the revolutionary cause! Just sign here.

speaker: Secretary (Aide to Colonel Frolois)
en: Whoever you are, take care to speak to citizen de Frolois with the greatest respect. He is a veteran of the Corsican campaign, and his military prowess is only matched by his scientific expertise in chemistry, and ballistics.

speaker: Arno
en: You summoned?

speaker: Trenet
en: Dorian. We have a task for you.

speaker: Arno
en: More fetch and carry work, I imagine?

speaker: Quemar
en: Two Master Assassins are dead. One by your own hand, in defense of a Templar. Count yourself lucky this is the extent of your punishment.

speaker: Arno
en: And Germain?

speaker: Beylier
en: He's none of your concern. Last night, the Paris Commune declared itself in open insurrection against the King. As we speak, twenty thousand armed revolutionaries are laying siege to the Tuileries. Even the National Guard are on the brink. Some of them have thrown in with the revolutionaries. France is splitting at the seams.

speaker: Arno
en: And this doesn't please us? The people are fighting for what is owed them. (Liberty, Equality...)

speaker: Trenet
en: If we danced about on a simple scale in need of balancing, you'd be right. But the truth is more complicated. In putting Mirabeau's affairs in order, we've come across certain correspondences... of a royal nature.

speaker: Arno
en: Mirabeau was in contact with the King?

speaker: Trenet
en: And he was rather less discreet than he should have been. If the King's copies of these letters were made public, the Templars would be in a position to expose and purge our agents across France.

speaker: Arno
en: And I'm to slip in and find them first?

speaker: Beylier
en: And quickly. The Swiss Guard are badly outnumbered. It's likely they'll be overwhelmed before nightfall.

speaker: Arno
en: Won't be the first palace I've broken into.

speaker: Leader
en: Ready! Aim! Fire!

speaker: Leader
en: Good work. Back to your posts.

speaker: Citizen
en: Long live the nation! Long live the Revolution! Long live the Revolution!

speaker: Crowd
en: The royals must be here somewhere! Where's the king?! Find the king! Bring out the tyrant! Death to the king!

speaker: Arno
en: Honestly, the quality of rhetoric among bloodthirsty rioters these days.

speaker: Republican 1
en: Heavy bastard, ain't ya?

speaker: Republican 2
en: Any sign of the tyrant?

speaker: Republican 3
en: Must've buggered off.

speaker: Republican 2
en: Bleedin' coward.

speaker: Republican 4
en: Would you look at that?

speaker: Republican 5
en: Gold, is it?

speaker: Republican 4
en: Reckon it must be.

speaker: Republican 5
en: Fucking hell.

speaker: Republican 6
en: Search everywhere! The Captain wants those papers!

speaker: Republican 7
en: There's nothing here!

speaker: Republican 6
en: Keep looking. It's in here somewhere.

speaker: Guard
en: Back! Back! Stay away!

speaker: Napoleon
en: Ah-ah.

speaker: Napoleon
en: You certainly don't look like a blood-crazed revolutionary. The hood is a bit sinister though, if you don't mind my saying.

speaker: Arno
en: Serving as rear guard, are you? Convenient how that puts several locked doors between you and the fighting.

speaker: Napoleon
en: Oh, I'm not here at all. Not officially anyway. But how often does one find the opportunity to poke about in a king's private study?

speaker: Arno
en: Looking for anything in particular?

speaker: Napoleon
en: State secrets. Private correspondences. Personal treasures. That sort of thing.

speaker: Arno
en: I do hope we're not eyeing the same prize.

speaker: Napoleon
en: Name it.

speaker: Arno
en: Certain letters written to the King. Ripe for... misunderstanding should the wrong men find them.

speaker: Napoleon
en: I see. Well, then perhaps we can help each other. I believe the King has built a hidden vault somewhere in here. If only we could find it....

speaker: Arno
en: You were saying?

speaker: Napoleon
en: Very nicely done, my friend.

speaker: Napoleon
en: Incredible...

speaker: Arno
en: Find your prize?

speaker: Napoleon
en: A cornucopia, yes. And you?

speaker: Arno
en: I believe so... yes! This is it!

speaker: Arno
en: That should take care of that.

speaker: Napoleon
en: Then may I suggest we leave?

speaker: Napoleon
en: Quickly.

speaker: Arno
en: What is that?

speaker: Napoleon
en: Our way out. Cover me, would you?

speaker: Napoleon
en: You are a demon with a blade. Well done! Where did you learn to fight? Just a bit longer. Almost done!

speaker: Napoleon
en: Let's go.

speaker: Rouille
en: Search everything! I want those documents!

speaker: Arno
en: Him! Damn!

speaker: Napoleon
en: Yes, Captain Rouille has that effect on people.

speaker: Arno
en: Friend of yours?

speaker: Napoleon
en: A persistent thorn I haven't quite managed to pluck out.

speaker: Arno
en: He has information I need! I need to get back up there!

speaker: Napoleon
en: In this mess? You'll never find him again. Come with me. I have a better idea.

speaker: Napoleon
en: You handled yourself well back there. I don't suppose you've ever considered military service?

speaker: Arno
en: I'm not much for following orders.

speaker: Napoleon
en: Ah, the bane of generals and statesmen everywhere: an individualist. I know the feeling. Men like us have a great advantage over most in the Army. You see: we can think for ourselves. If you joined up today, you'd be a Marshall in ten years. Guaranteed.

speaker: Arno
en: A generous offer. But no.

speaker: Napoleon
en: Where the heart leads, a man must follow. Look me up if you ever change your mind. Bonaparte is my name. Napoleon Bonaparte. Second Lieutenant of Artillery. For now.

speaker: Arno
en: Arno Dorian.

speaker: Napoleon
en: A pleasure. And, as a personal favor: if anyone asks, I was never here. Watched the whole thing from a furniture shop across the Carousel.

speaker: Arno
en: A face in the crowd. Of course.

speaker: Arno
en: What now?

speaker: Napoleon
en: Just a moment.

speaker: Napoleon
en: You may want to take cover.

speaker: Corporal
en: Everything all right, sir?

speaker: Napoleon
en: Fine, Corporal. Superb shot!

speaker: Napoleon
en: Regular drills are critical to a regiment's success.

speaker: Corporal
en: We should be going, sir.

speaker: Napoleon
en: We part ways here.

speaker: Arno
en: What about Rouille?

speaker: Napoleon
en: Give me a few days. I'll see what I can learn of his current posting. Perhaps I can arrange an introduction. Be well.

speaker: Mirabeau
en: Parishioners found a body in Notre-Dame today. The wags are already calling him the Penitent. I take it justice has been done?

speaker: Arno
en: Not entirely. Sivert had an accomplice the night of (Mister) de la Serre's murder. He struck the killing blow.

speaker: Mirabeau
en: This raises troubling questions—what have you learned?

speaker: Arno
en: He was working with a man called le Roi des Thunes.

speaker: Beylier
en: The King of Beggars? Are you sure?

speaker: Arno
en: You know him?

speaker: Beylier
en: Of him. The beggars pay him tribute, the man himself is a ghost. We've sent three Assassins after him. The first two found no trace. The third never returned.

speaker: Arno
en: I can find him. Sivert met with one of his lieutenants. I owe it to the memory of (Mister) de la Serre to uncover the truth.

speaker: Mirabeau
en: Perhaps you can at that. You've proved yourself a true Assassin today—and a true Assassin must have the proper tools.

speaker: Arno
en: So the concealed blade and the smoke bombs were just, what you had on hand, then?

speaker: Mirabeau
en: The phantom blade. A modest little update from the traditional Assassin's blade. Where you're going, you may not wish to get too close to your enemies. Now then. Assassin, this Council charges you to go to la Cour des Miracles. Find there the Templar agent le Roi des Thunes. Learn his secrets, and bring him peace.

speaker: Guard 1
en: This your first time in the Cour des Miracles?

speaker: Guard 1
en: Cheer up—it's not the worst posting. I was in the Colonies a few years ago—now that was ugly. Just keep one hand on your purse and you'll be fine.

speaker: Beggar
en: Please, no! I've done all I can, it's the times! No one wants to

speaker: La Touche
en: His Grace doesn't care about excuses. He cares about results. If you can't make your quotas, he makes... adjustments. Doctor, cut his foot off.

speaker: Beggar
en: No! No, please, God no!

speaker: Arno
en: There you are. Le Roi des Thunes' lieutenant. La Touche.

speaker: De Sade
en: Oh, I wouldn't do that. Look. Lovely, no? The good folk of Paris give more money to crippled beggars than whole ones. Le Roi des Thunes sees in that bit of trivia an opportunity to motivate his less-successful employees.

speaker: Arno
en: That man

speaker: De Sade
en: Has lost a foot. Now, you can charge in there, cause a great disturbance, and send all the rats scurrying back to their holes. Or you can disappear into the swarm, and follow the rats back to their king. Either way, that man has lost a foot.

speaker: Doctor
en: It's done.

speaker: La Touche
en: Take him to the clinic for a proper cauterization, then send him back to the street.

speaker: Guard 3
en: Come on, up you get.

speaker: Arno
en: I appreciate the advice.

speaker: De Sade
en: Not yet.

speaker: Arno
en: Who are you precisely? And why help me?

speaker: De Sade
en: Oh, I've had my eye on you for some time now, Arno. I feel it my sovereign duty to aid all those who suffered in cruelest bondage with me at the Bastille. And I have a vested interest in seeing the King of Rats caught in a trap. As to my name, I have the pleasure of being Donatien Alphonse François, Marquis de Sade. Do pay me a visit when you have tired of chasing vermin. Oh, he's left a lovely trail. Good luck.

speaker: Beggar 1
en: Nights are getting cold again.

speaker: Beggar 2
en: Mmm.

speaker: Beggar 1
en: You don't seem worried.

speaker: Beggar 2
en: I know where the chimneys are.

speaker: Beggar 1
en: What chimneys?

speaker: Beggar 2
en: The ones His Grace had put in when he took over down below. Sleep on one of those and you'll be as warm as a babe in arms.

speaker: La Touche
en: Double-time, lads. His Grace isn't fond of tardiness. Who are you? No closer! Don't touch me! Get back!

speaker: De Sade
en: La Touche. Still bringing medical care to the disenfranchised?

speaker: La Touche
en: Your day will come, libertine.

speaker: De Sade
en: Rather sooner than you think, I'm sure.

speaker: Guard 4
en: Fancy a drink later?

speaker: La Touche
en: Do I know you?

speaker: Guard 5
en: Is it true what he did to Thierry?

speaker: La Touche
en: I remember the man's screams and how long they lasted. And that was for an accounting error.

speaker: Guard 5
en: You're joking. I thought he'd skimmed off the take or some such.

speaker: La Touche
en: No. He misplaced a 1 in a ledger.

speaker: Guard 5
en: Right. Double-time it is.

speaker: La Touche
en: Get him inside, quickly. Something doesn't feel right.

speaker: Guard 3
en: Uh... he's dead, sir.

speaker: La Touche
en: Then toss him in the gutter and get yourselves inside.

speaker: Guard 6
en: Quotas are up again. I don't know who His Grace's new friends are, but they're squeezing us drier than stones.

speaker: Guard 7
en: Hope I've got enough....

speaker: Guard 6
en: Wonder what they'll take this week?

speaker: Guard 7
en: More "tribute" for His Grace.

speaker: Guard 6
en: Better this than the king's "modifications".

speaker: Guard 8
en: Hold him steady.

speaker: Beggar 3
en: No! No! Please! Please!

speaker: Guard 9
en: What's the order for unfortunate in bed 6?

speaker: La Touche
en: "Horribly burned in a fire that killed his family and drove him mad."

speaker: Guard 9
en: A burn job? Do you know how hard those are to get right without burning half the district to ash?

speaker: La Touche
en: Use a few drops of the strong acid. Laymen can't tell the difference.

speaker: La Touche
en: No! No, please!

speaker: Arno
en: Give me le Roi des Thunes, and I'll spare you your life.

speaker: La Touche
en: The catacombs! He's in the catacombs beneath the old church!

speaker: Arno
en: La Touche, I expected a stronger spine than yours! What will your Master say?

speaker: La Touche
en: Oh God... God help me!

speaker: Dossonville
en: Looks like another scam auction. I'm going to foul their little game. Care to watch?

speaker: Auctioneer
en: And now, let us sell of this dilapidated church. I hope it remains standing until we finish.

speaker: Dossonville
en: Three hundred livres!

speaker: Auctioneer
en: Who are you?

speaker: Dossonville
en: Citizen Dossonville! And I bid three hundred livres! No, four!

speaker: Auctioneer
en: You can't bid against yourself!

speaker: Dossonville
en: I bid seven! And mine aren't counterfeit!

speaker: Auctioneer
en: I must ask you to leave, Citizen!

speaker: Dossonville
en: So you can pretend to sell this fine building to your friend?

speaker: Auctioneer
en: That's an outrageous accusation!

speaker: Dossonville
en: Take that back!

speaker: Auctioneer
en: Make me! You men, get him out of here!

speaker: Arno
en: All right, Lafrenière. Where are you hiding?

speaker: Guard 1
en: Bloody miserable draft.

speaker: Guard 2
en: What good's a ceiling that can't even keep the rain off you?

speaker: Guard 3
en: Psst. Look what I've got.

speaker: Guard 4
en: Is that...?

speaker: Guard 3
en: The '74 . Just the thing to make guard duty bearable.

speaker: Guard 4
en: If the captain sees....

speaker: Guard 3
en: Then we take it round the back. Anyone asks, we saw an unguarded entrance and decided to plug the gap in security.

speaker: Guard 4
en: "Plug a gap in security." I like that.

speaker: Guard 5
en: With all this, we could take on an army.

speaker: Guard 6
en: Like to see them try and stop us.

speaker: Guard 7
en: Where are we supposed to put all these?

speaker: Guard 8
en: Don't even think about lighting a pipe in here.

speaker: Arno
en: That is a distressingly large number of gunpowder. Lafrenière must be planning something big. Guns from . Hm.

speaker: Arno
en: Whatever he's planning, it's big. And now I know where to find you, "Grand Master."

speaker: Arno
en: It hardly seems safe just to leave these lying around.

speaker: Guard 10
en: The powder stores! They're going to blow!

speaker: Arno
en: No, of course it can't be that easy, can it?

speaker: Arno
en: Maybe I should have thought this through... Up is good.

speaker: Arno
en: Hide in plain sight. Right.

speaker: Raider 1
en: The funeral procession moves through the center of town today.

speaker: Raider 2
en: It will be simple. We attack, they die, we are rich.

speaker: Raider 3
en: I'm not certain. Something doesn't sit right with me.

speaker: Raider 1
en: Perhaps that whore from last night... Heh ha ha ha.

speaker: Arno
en: He should learn to trust his instincts.

speaker: Raider leader
en: Today's not Rousseau's day! Our benefactor has been generous to us! Each of you, get one and use it well! I'm the lord of hellfire! Let's bring them down fellas!

speaker: Guard
en: The road is clear! Let's head to Paris!

speaker: Official
en: Finally. We can leave this wretched city. What did Rousseau have in mind when he lived in this rathole?

speaker: Arno
en: Suger, the architect of the Basilica's last will: to be buried where monks would pass over him each day. Where is he now?

speaker: Arno
en: Where is the headstone? Someone moved it.

speaker: Defrocked monk
en: And keep an eye out. I don't want nobody following us.

speaker: Arno
en: The second part of the Abbot's last will. There are many mysteries left to unravel.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Piss off, you lot!

speaker: Guard 2
en: Where do you think you're going?

speaker: Beggar 1
en: I-it's time for Mass.

speaker: Guard 2
en: Your souls will keep. No one enters without His Grace's permission.

speaker: Beggar
en: But

speaker: Guard 2
en: Get out of my sight, dog!

speaker: Guard 3
en: Takes the chill right off, that does.

speaker: Guard 4
en: Why do you suppose it's so hot?

speaker: Guard 3
en: It's ventilation from the catacombs.

speaker: Guard 4
en: Huh. What do they need that for?

speaker: Guard 3
en: Because if they didn't, the whole place would fill with smoke.

speaker: Guard 4
en: Oh, ok. And that's bad, is it?

speaker: Guard 3
en: Yes, you could charitably describe it as bad.

speaker: Guard 4
en: All right, all right. We didn't all "study with the Montgolfiers before drink brought us to ruin," you know.

speaker: Guard 3
en: One time! One time I mentioned that!

speaker: Guard 4
en: Whatever you say, Professor.

speaker: Arno
en: Informative, to say the least.

speaker: Guard 5
en: More of His Grace's "special projects" on the streets these days.

speaker: Guard 6
en: I've scarcely made a (penny) all week. How the hell can I compete with triple amputees and "wounded veterans?"

speaker: Guard 5
en: Miss another tribute and you'll be remembering your own brave service at .

speaker: Arno
en: That should smoke them out.

speaker: Arno
en: Those bastards will cut them to ribbons. The poor devils are completely outmatched. They'll never suvive without help.

speaker: Beggar 2
en: Let's see the bastards push us around now!

speaker: Beggar 3
en: These'll do the trick.

speaker: Beggar 2
en: I want that one! Let's go! Come on!

speaker: Guard 7
en: Goddamn, that's a ripe whiff! Let's get out of here!

speaker: Guard 8
en: What do you expect? Some idiot dug too deep, broke through into the sewer.

speaker: Guard 7
en: Let's get out of here.

speaker: Guard 9
en: What's happened?

speaker: Guard 10
en: The beggars! They're rioting all throughout the district. You men, with me!

speaker: La Touche
en: My lord! My lord! My lord! I've heard, uh, reliable reports that... That an Assassin is nearby, and that... you are his intended target.

speaker: Arno
en: The worm has grown a spine... now he's a snake.

speaker: Roi des Thunes
en: Damn it! It was only a matter of time, I knew that much. But this is far too soon.

speaker: La Touche
en: , my Lord... the Assassins are ah... well connected.

speaker: Roi des Thunes
en: But we have the advantage now, don't we? Muster the guard and lead the hunt for this Assassin. Bring me his head.

speaker: La Touche
en: But my Lord! Half our men are out dealing with uprisings among the beggars! Y-You men, with me! Find him! Maybe he's given up... Where is he? Stay together, men! Spread out! Find him! Keep a watchful eye! Stay on your guard! Show yourself, Assassin! Do not let him pass! Come out, coward!

speaker: La Touche
en: He's through there!

speaker: Arno
en: Embarrassing.

speaker: Guard 11
en: Hold your positions, men.

speaker: Arno
en: That explains what happened to Beylier's last agent.

speaker: Roi des Thunes
en: Beylier's last apprentice brought me the most wonderful gift. I do hope you have something to compare.

speaker: Roi des Thunes
en: Perhaps not as clever as you think? There you are. What trophy shall I take from you? Lovely to see you, Assassin. Hmm. Tricky tricky, Assassin. (I see you.) Tut tut! Not so close! I should have known it would come to this. Still relying on those silly little hidden knives? So it is down to the two of us, Assassin.

speaker: Roi des Thunes
en: My subjects have eyes everywhere, my lord. I offer their knowledge to the service of the Order.

speaker: De la Serre
en: What knowledge could a king of the gutters offer us? The intrigues of rats? You may go.

speaker: Roi des Thunes
en: "The intrigues of rats?" Pompous fool! If I could lay my hands on him...

speaker: Sivert
en: My master would be pleased to arrange that. Brother.

speaker: Arno
en: You all right, (Mister)? Too much of the king's champagne?

speaker: Roi des Thunes
en: Sivert, come away!

speaker: Sivert
en: It is done. De la Serre is dead... Grand Master.

speaker: Germain
en: Good.

speaker: Guards
en: Put out the torches! Bastard could be right under our noses... Someone douse the fires! How are we supposed to find anything in this? Can't see a damn thing in here.

speaker: De Sade
en: Ah... You're just in time for the commencement of my reign.

speaker: Arno
en: Your reign?

speaker: De Sade
en: As long as there's a Cour des Miracles, we must have a Roi des Thunes. Since there seemed to be a vacancy, I stepped in.

speaker: Arno
en: With remarkable speed. The body is not yet cold.

speaker: De Sade
en: I may have set things in motion a trifle early. Say, when you first arrived in la Cour des Miracles.

speaker: Arno
en: You used me.

speaker: De Sade
en: Your target is dead? We used one another.

speaker: Arno
en: Quite a kingdom you've inherited.

speaker: De Sade
en: It is, isn't it? So... Is justice served? Are the dead avenged, is your soul soothed, all that rot?

speaker: Arno
en: Rot is a fine description. Every time I think I'm getting close to the truth, it seems another layer of filth presents itself.

speaker: De Sade
en: Conspiracy! Intrigue! A rapidly-thickening plot! Add some bestiality and a lecherous priest and I'd say you have the beginnings of a beautiful novel.

speaker: Arno
en: I'd settle for a solid lead.

speaker: De Sade
en: So young. And yet so serious. Well, best of luck to you.

speaker: De Sade
en: You have, I trust, looked into this?

speaker: Arno
en: Where did you get that?

speaker: De Sade
en: One of my newly loyal subjects brought it to me as a... token of esteem, as it were. It's a curious piece. I know of only one silversmith who works metal like this.

speaker: Arno
en: A blade of this make killed (Mister) de la Serre. I can only assume you know this already. Why didn't you say?

speaker: De Sade
en: Where would man be if he never had to ask questions? If everything he could ever want to know were simply handed to him? He might no longer think to ask questions.

speaker: Arno
en: Or he might accomplish a great deal more, unburdened by ignorance.

speaker: De Sade
en: Perhaps. The smith's name is François-Thomas Germain. You'll find his shop near Les Halles.

speaker: Arno
en: Thank you.

scene: The League of the Crimson Rose
speaker: Arno
en: What ambush?

scene: The League of the Crimson Rose
speaker: Guests
en: One must enjoy these soirées while one can. Soon, the lunatics will have our heads. The Crimson Rose and his League saved my dear uncle from the guillotine.

scene: The League of the Crimson Rose
speaker: League member 1
en: Are you here to meet with "Sir Reginald"? Want to join the Crimson League, eh? Good man.

scene: The League of the Crimson Rose
speaker: League member 2
en: The Crimson League? I may be a member. Not about to say.

scene: The League of the Crimson Rose
speaker: Crimson Rose
en: May I compliment your cravat? Very stylish, although I recommend an underhand know in the future. I have an eye for such things. Sink me if the ladies don't pay more attention to you when you've an underhand knot, eh?

scene: The League of the Crimson Rose
speaker: Guest
en: Oh, Sir Reginald! Your observations are so amusing!

scene: The League of the Crimson Rose
speaker: Crimson Rose
en: I speak not to amuse, but to inform, my dear fellow! Overhand knots are a relic of the past!

scene: The League of the Crimson Rose
speaker: Crimson Rose
en: An ambush? I cannot be apprehended just as my plans are coming together! You, sir, if you help me hold them off, you shall have my gratitude!

scene: The League of the Crimson Rose
speaker: Guard
en: After him, men! Kill the Crimson Rose!

scene: The League of the Crimson Rose
speaker: Crimson Rose
en: Well done! You seem the sort of fellow I could use in my organization. I shall call on you in the future!

speaker: Leo
en: was a virtual representation of one of Arno Dorian's genetic memories, relived by a Helix initiate through the Helix Navigator.

speaker: Roux
en: I've decided, child, to hear your confession.

speaker: Supplicant
en: Thank you, Father. As I protect you on earth, may you protect me in the afterlife.

speaker: Roux
en: You think you protect me... Who will protect you?

speaker: Bishop
en: That's Jacques Roux, basically the angriest priest in history.

speaker: Roux
en: Kill the food hoarders!

speaker: Bishop
en: He was extreme. Too extreme for Robespierre even.

speaker: Bishop
en: As bad as the Reign of Terror was, Roux would have taken things to a whole new level. Templars kept Roux in their back pocket for when Robespierre fell.

speaker: Extremist
en: I'm running out of guards, Roux.

speaker: Roux
en: Those Assassins will be coming back for me.

speaker: Extremist
en: We're counting on it. Stretch your legs. Tomorrow you lead the Terror in a new direction.

speaker: Roux
en: Make sure your masters hold up their end of the bargain.

speaker: Extremist
en: They always do.

speaker: Bishop
en: Some Assassins already failed once trying to kill Roux. We think they were captured. Find them, and then finish the job. If the Assassins are alive, they never left the asylum. Check the lists of prisoners and try to find them.

speaker: Enragé 1
en: I heard Roux is out.

speaker: Enragé 2
en: Better get ready to move then. I hear he's getting impatient.

speaker: Enragé 1
en: Hah! That's an understatement.

speaker: Enragé 3
en: Think Roux's actually getting out today?

speaker: Enragé 4
en: I hear he's on his way down now.

speaker: Enragé 3
en: Finally, been waiting long enough.

speaker: Enragé 5
en: How'd we get stuck on graveyard patrol?

speaker: Enragé 6
en: Shut your mouth before I put you in a coffin too.

speaker: Enragé 5
en: Just asking...

speaker: Enragé 7
en: We had better get ready to move.

speaker: Enragé 8
en: Roux's out?

speaker: Enragé 7
en: Yeah.

speaker: Bishop
en: Looks like the Assassins are still alive, and they're being held in the prison. You'll want to free them before things get too crazy.

speaker: Enragé 9
en: Get back to work!

speaker: Enragé 10
en: Just resting a moment.

speaker: Enragé 9
en: I hear Roux's out of his cell. Want him to see you slacking?

speaker: Assassin 1
en: Brother, free me! Unlock my cell, and I can aid you.

speaker: Assassin 1
en: You must be looking for Roux.

speaker: Bishop
en: Okay, Initiates, that's one Assassin free.

speaker: Enragé 11
en: When Roux gets out of here we can just kill all these poor bastards finally.

speaker: Enragé 12
en: I can't wait.

speaker: Assassin 2
en: Arno? Is that you?! Quickly, unlock my cell.

speaker: Assassin 2
en: Give Roux my regards.

speaker: Bishop
en: Two free.

speaker: Enragé 13
en: If I have to stay down here much longer, you'll have to lock me in those cells soon.

speaker: Enragé 14
en: You and me both, brother.

speaker: Enragé 13
en: I hear Roux's out of his cell. Want him to see you slacking?

speaker: Assassin 3
en: Brother! Over here! Free me, please!

speaker: Assassin 3
en: My thanks, Brother.

speaker: Bishop
en: Ok, all the Assassins are freed. You're clear to take out Roux, you just need to find him...

speaker: Bishop
en: There's Roux. Looks like he's making the rounds before he leaves the grounds. Get him before he makes it to his carriage. Looks like Roux's collecting some cash from his Enragés. This might be a good chance to take him out.

speaker: Roux
en: I hope you two didn't miss me.

speaker: Enragé 15
en: Of course not!

speaker: Enragé 16
en: We have been waiting eagerly for your return, Father.

speaker: Roux
en: Everything ran smoothly while I was gone?

speaker: Enragé 15
en: Smoothly!

speaker: Enragé 16
en: So smoothly!

speaker: Roux
en: Then what is this I hear about money going missing? You two wouldn't know anything about that, would you?

speaker: Enragé 15
en: No!

speaker: Enragé 16
en: Never, Jacques!

speaker: Roux
en: I just couldn't bear it if I found out you two stole from me. You're like sons to me.

speaker: Enragé 15
en: We did everything we could to keep the business running.

speaker: Roux
en: When I met you both, you were street urchins. I trusted you, clothed you. Look at you now.

speaker: Enragé 16
en: All of the money is there, Father. Down to the sous!

speaker: Roux
en: Hm. Good. Glad I can count on you two.

speaker: Enragé 15
en: Thank you, Father.

speaker: Bishop
en: Roux's moving on. Look for another window to open up.

speaker: Bishop
en: Roux's stopped again. I guess some of his fans missed him while he was locked up.

speaker: Roux
en: Good to see you, men.

speaker: Enragé 17
en: It's good to see you too, Father. The men are getting restless.

speaker: Roux
en: Patience is a virtue. I trust the preparations are going well?

speaker: Enragé 17
en: The city is in chaos, and we have men stationed throughout Paris. At your signal, we will move in and take over Paris.

speaker: Roux
en: So goes Paris, so goes France. Soon the Bourgeois will have good reason to fear the Enragés. now. And Robespierre?

speaker: Enragé 17
en: His government is weak. The people have turned against him.

speaker: Roux
en: I knew that bastard couldn't rule this city.

speaker: Enragé 17
en: The Jacobins are not long for this world.

speaker: Roux
en: And neither is Robespierre. Good. Good. You have done well, expect to be rewarded when this is over.

speaker: Enragé 17
en: Father.

speaker: Enragé 18
en: Thank you, Father.

speaker: Bishop
en: Damn, he's on the move again. You're not going to get many more chances like that.

speaker: Bishop
en: Alright, Roux is dead! Now get out of there.

speaker: Bishop
en: The Templars just lost another weapon in the fight for the Revolution. Good work.

speaker: Letter
en: It is well known that intendant Foullon is hoarding foodstuffs and selling them at exorbant rates. We have discovered one of his warehouses in Les Halles. Eliminate the hoarders, open the warehouse and give the people access to the food. -The Council

speaker: Guards
en: There's nothing for you here, get away! Shut up or you'll be eating dirt. Get away! Beggars. Go die elsewhere!

speaker: Guard 1
en: This is mighty tasty.

speaker: Guard 2
en: Don't let Foullon catch you eating that. He'll make ground beef of you.

speaker: Guard 3
en: A good haul today, lads!

speaker: Guard 4
en: Foullon will be pleased.

speaker: Libra
en: was a virtual representation of one of Arno Dorian's genetic memories, relived by a Helix initiate through the Helix Navigator.

speaker: Newspaper
en: There are rumors that the son of the former King, Louis Capet, lives and is in Paris. Any information is to be brought immediately to a member of the Committee of Public Safety.

speaker: Man
en: The Prince is still alive!

speaker: Woman
en: I can't believe it!

speaker: Man
en: My god, the Prince...

speaker: Assassin
en: Some people will believe anything, won't they? You shouldn't believe everything you read. The Templars are holding the Prince as a bargaining chip, but have lost interest.

speaker: Arno
en: Bad news for the Prince.

speaker: Assassin
en: The Assassins want what he knows, but the Templars will kill him unless we can get him on a boat out of Paris.

speaker: Arno
en: Consider it done.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Time's up for the little prince.

speaker: Guard 2
en: Shame.

speaker: Prince
en: Please, my uncle is the Count of Provence, he can pay.

speaker: Warden
en: He's paying alright, who do you think wants you dead?

speaker: Prince
en: But, why?

speaker: Warden
en: You'll be king... for a day... and that uncle of yours will take your place.

speaker: Prince
en: Please, I've done nothing wrong.

speaker: Warden
en: Snort! Then you must be the first innocent royal in history! Never killed a prince before...

speaker: Prince
en: Please, don't harm me!

speaker: Warden
en: No, I just do as I'm told son.

speaker: Arno
en: Prince Louis-Charles, I presume?

speaker: Prince
en: Finally! My Uncle sent you, then?

speaker: Arno
en: I serve another Master.

speaker: Prince
en: A servant nonetheless... Well? What are you waiting for? Rescue me!

speaker: Arno
en: As you say... Let's go, your boat is waiting.

speaker: Prince
en: But I get seasick!

speaker: Arno
en: Of course...

speaker: Prince
en: There's more ahead! Can't you watch where you're going?

speaker: Arno
en: Just wait here.

speaker: Arno
en: They're waiting for us at the shore.

speaker: Prince
en: I hope they have sweets!

speaker: Arno
en: You had better be worth it...

speaker: Assassin
en: Greetings, Arno, but there has been some confusion. This is not the Prince.

speaker: Arno
en: You've got to be kidding...

speaker: Impostor
en: Wait! But... I was the Prince's groom. I grew up with him!

speaker: Assassin
en: What you know is useful nonetheless. You will be safe with us.

speaker: Arno
en: Glad I could help.

speaker: Letter
en: A violent gang is robbing graves in the Île de la Cité. A letter from the powerful Jean-Paul Marat shields them from arrest. Steal the letter.

speaker: Gang member
en: Leave me alone! I've got a letter from Marat!

speaker: Marianne
en: You're wondering perhaps what I'm doing?

speaker: Arno
en: I am a little curious.

speaker: Marianne
en: My parents were denounced by our neighbor. And though they had done nothing wrong, they were executed. The neighbor then took our home. I've grieved the loss of my family long enough. I want to take back my home! Teach me how to fight!

speaker: Arno
en: All right, Marianne. Come at me and I'll parry your attacks.

speaker: Marianne
en: This training is tough. Show me again! That's better. I've got to get this right.

speaker: Arno
en: Strike through the target. Well done. Bravo!

speaker: Marianne
en: That's good enough. It is time to get my parents' house back!

speaker: Marianne

en: That was quick work. You've warned all of them. Now you need to distract the guards to help the Girondists get away. Head to the Bastille.

speaker: Bishop
en: Those woodpiles would make a perfect fire - and in my experience, nothing draws attention like fire.

speaker: Bishop
en: Nice work. The Girondists will be waiting at the Arsenal. Meet them there and smuggle them out of Paris.

speaker: Bishop
en: The Girondists are hiding in the sewers under the building. They'll probably need some help getting out.

speaker: Girondists
en: Thank you for your kindness. I never thought we'd get away. Please, thank Danton for his help. You have our thanks. Thank you. You haven't heard the last of us. You've saved us! Thank you! You'll be repaid for this. Thank you.

speaker: Bishop
en: Looks like the coast is clear, so they should be safe now. Nice work.

speaker: Dumas
en: Arno, my friend. Thank you for your help with that Joséphine imbroglio. Bonaparte is all aflutter. I thought he was engaged to someone else. I have another task, if you would. Damned upsetting. When I left the , my mother and siblings stayed behind. My only mementos of them are a few letters and things. The Templars have taken them in an effort to influence. They have a hideout near the cemetery not far from here.

speaker: Dumas
en: Yes. This is from my mother, Marie-Cessette. And here, my sister, sold into slavery as a child. There is no price I would not pay for these scribbled notes.

speaker: Guard 1
en: you'll be reinforced before the Master arrives. We'll post snipers on the roofs. The instructions are all here. Get to it.

speaker: Guard 2
en: Think we should go with them?

speaker: Guard 3
en: The Master's elite bodyguards? I think they can handle it.

speaker: Guard 2
en: Suppose you're right.

speaker: Arno
en: I'd better find myself a place to wait before the rest of them arrive.

speaker: Guard 2
en: What's going on?

speaker: Guard 3
en: A few of the groundskeepers heard more than they should have. They're hiding in the catacombs.

speaker: Guard 2
en: So the Master's bodyguards have to dig them out? Seems excessive.

speaker: Guard 3
en: Bastards are fighting back. Dug in like ticks.

speaker: Guard 2
en: They'd best be dead by the time the Master arrives. I don't want him vulnerable.

speaker: Guard 4
en: Get more men up on those walls! Make sure those gates are locked! The Master left specific instructions, and they're to be followed to the letter!

speaker: Arno
en: This shows exactly where Lafrenière will be every step of the way. They couldn't have made it easier if they'd tried. Got you now.

speaker: Gravedigger
en: You came along at just the right time. I'll gather up the others, we'll hold position here. Cover your escape, if you need it.

speaker: Arno
en: I love it when the target comes to me.

speaker: Lafrenière
en: The Truth is in peril, my brothers. She is beset on all quarters. Jacobins lay her on the rack, cruelly breaking her to their populist agenda. False prophets go among the people, promising "Liberty, equality, fraternity."

speaker: Spectator
en: Bastards!

speaker: Lafrenière
en: Within our own Order, false brothers would see us abandon her and throw in with the very forces we strive against! And always, always the Assassins lurk in their shadows, watching for signs of weakness.

speaker: Spectator
en: Traitors!

speaker: Lafrenière
en: Our enemies believe that by taking our weapons, they take our power. I think the Friends of Truth are not so easily dissuaded! Union, Strength, Virtue! Ready yourselves, brothers! Tonight, the Truth is on our side!

speaker: Spectator
en: Huzzah!

speaker: Lafrenière
en: Is all in readiness?

speaker: Guard 5
en: . The men know their duties - the bastards won't escape us tonight.

speaker: Lafrenière
en: Good. The enemy has thwarted us for the last time.

speaker: Guard 5
en: As you say, Master.

speaker: Lafrenière
en: I trust the payment was received?

speaker: Austrian Templar
en: Of course, my brother.

speaker: Lafrenière
en: You've done a great service to both France and the Order. We will not forget.

speaker: Austrian Templar
en: The Austrian Rite is always loyal to the true Templar Order.

speaker: Lafrenière
en: Brothers! Soon we will strike at the very heart of our hated enemies! They have hounded us for years, but no longer! With one stroke, we will save our Order, and rebuild our Nation! The Father of Understanding marches with us tonight! Prepare yourselves!

speaker: De la Serre
en: Then rise, my brother, and be welcome.

speaker: Lafrenière
en: You don't trust the man, do you?

speaker: De la Serre
en: Mirabeau is a good man. An honest man.

speaker: Lafrenière
en: Mirabeau is a self-aggrandizing drunk!

speaker: De la Serre
en: Do not forget who is Grand Master here, Lafrenière.

speaker: Lafrenière
en: Take this to Grand Master de la Serre immediately. Deliver it to him in person.

speaker: Perrault
en: Yes, Master.

speaker: Guard
en: Master, we have a problem. Christophe has been feeding information to our enemies. We must assume this location is compromised.

speaker: Lafrenière
en: We'll have to move up our timetable. Gather the men. We strike l'Hôtel de Beauvais tonight.

speaker: Gouze
en: Our friends, Les Actes des Apôtres, are up to their tricks again. Thanks to Colette, we know they acquired the Sancy diamond in a raid on the royal treasury. We suspect that their leader, a man known as Renard, plans to sell it to finance a major attack. We can't let that happen. One of our agents is in place to make the buy using counterfeit livres; go to Bièvre and make sure it all goes smoothly.

speaker: Arno
en: What happened?

speaker: Contact
en: Renard smelled a rat. His men took off with the diamond - you'll have to get it back. We have a man waiting to smuggle it out of the country, but only if you can get it to him within the hour. Hurry!

speaker: Smuggler
en: You have it?

speaker: Arno
en: Right here.

speaker: Smuggler
en: Nice work. Don't worry, the stone will be safely in Russia before the month is out.

speaker: Gouze
en: I've received word that the... package made it safely out of France. Well done.

speaker: Arno
en: Léon?

speaker: Léon
en: Engarde! A chakram from India.

speaker: Arno
en: What a sly thief. I've commandeered the other two.

speaker: Léon
en: So what happens now?

speaker: Arno
en: I don't know, you tell me.

speaker: Margot
en: A little light in the darkness.

speaker: Léon
en: Go away! We're busy.

speaker: Arno
en: Wait...

speaker: Arno
en: Look.

speaker: Léon
en: It's a map of the caverns!

speaker: Arno
en: I'll find out where it leads. You stay here.

speaker: Léon
en: But

speaker: Léon
en: Ahh, (shit.)

speaker: Margot
en: Léon!

speaker: Rose
en: Are you or are you not an expert lock pick?!

speaker: Rose
en: Go on. Choose one.

speaker: Raider 1
en: The Commandant told us to wait.

speaker: Rose
en: Anyone else prefer to wait?

speaker: Arno
en: Done.

speaker: Raider 3
en: The ghost of the king!

speaker: Raider 4
en: Flee if you value your lives!

speaker: Arno
en: There.

speaker: Raider 5
en: The ghost of the king!

speaker: Raider 6
en: Run!

speaker: Arno
en: The ghost! What sort of device is this? Like the map on the plates, it is made out of light.

speaker: Arno
en: Got it.

speaker: Raider 7
en: It's real! The ghost!

speaker: Raider 8
en: I quit!

speaker: Arno
en: There. The lock. Now for the golden key.

speaker: Arno
en: I suppose a simple address would be too mundane.

speaker: Arno
en: "If you can pluck your head from your own arse, come find us." What's the light supposed to illuminate? What am I supposed to do with this medallion? Perhaps the sunbeam...?

speaker: Bellec
en: Took you long enough, pisspot.

speaker: Arno
en: What is this place?

speaker: Bellec
en: A sanctuary. A place we can train and prepare, away from the eyes of our enemies.

speaker: Arno
en: Didn't we just escape from a dungeon?

speaker: Bellec
en: It's not a dungeon. It's a nerve center. From these tunnels we can get anywhere in the city, all without being seen. We have eyes everywhere.

speaker: Arno
en: Really? Seems visibility would be a problem. Wouldn't you prefer something with a view?

speaker: Bellec
en: This place has served us well for six hundred years, pisspot.

speaker: Arno
en: Uh-huh. And how long were you standing in the dark waiting for me?

speaker: Bellec
en: Not long. Guillaume spotted you from the bell tower.

speaker: Arno
en: Well, it was quite the entrance.

speaker: Bellec
en: Are you mocking me?

speaker: Arno
en: No, no! God's truth. Very theatrical.

speaker: Bellec
en: Shut up. We're here.

speaker: Mirabeau
en: The candidate will approach. So the son of Charles Dorian returns to us. Bellec thought you wouldn't come. What changed your mind?

speaker: Arno
en: I'm tired of running from my failures. Monsieur (Mister) de la Serre, my father... I want to make it right.

speaker: Beylier
en: The death of Grand Master de la Serre weighs on you. Why? Did you wield the blade yourself?

speaker: Arno
en: Does it matter? The blame still lies with me.

speaker: Trenet
en: Inna zunubahu tuthqilu kahilayh. Hal Anta muta'akidon minh? (He carries his guilt heavily. Are you sure of this one?)

speaker: Bellec
en: Ana kazalek. Innahu qadiron 'ala muwajahati elmuhakamah. Sayakounu jay'yidan. (I am. He can face the trials. He can be great.)

speaker: Mirabeau
en: Very well. Out of the dark, you come into the light. From the light, you will return to the dark. Are you prepared to travel the eagle's path?

speaker: Arno
en: If that's a fancy way of asking "do I want your help," yes.

speaker: Mirabeau
en: Then drink.

speaker: Arno
en: What's happening? Hello?

speaker: Young Arno
en: Can't I go with you, father?

speaker: Charles
en: Courage, my boy. You wait just here. I will return when this hand reaches the top. And there is to be no mischief.

speaker: Arno
en: Father!

speaker: Charles
en: Where is that boy? I'm certain I told him six o'clock—we should be well away by now.

speaker: Arno
en: Father, it's me! I'm here!

speaker: Arno
en: Father! Look out! No!

speaker: Perrault
en: He must receive it today! It's very

speaker: Arno
en: Very important. I heard you the first time.

speaker: Élise
en: You seem to have caused quite a commotion.

speaker: Arno
en: What can I say? You were always a bad influence.

speaker: Élise
en: You were a worse one. Go! I'll distract them.

speaker: Guard
en: Mon Dieu (My God), he's killed Lord de la Serre!

speaker: Bellec
en: If you can pluck your head from your arse, come find us. You'd make a fine fit!

speaker: Élise
en: Haven't you done enough to repay my father's kindness? I found that on the floor of my father's study. Unopened.

speaker: Arno
en: I didn't know.

speaker: Élise
en: Neither did my father.

speaker: François
en: Truly, I am blessed to have such a loyal companion as you, my friend.

speaker: Mirabeau
en: These are the words spoken by our ancestors. The words that lay at the heart of our creed.

speaker: Beylier
en: Stay your blade from the flesh of the innocent.

speaker: Trenet
en: Hide in plain sight.

speaker: Quemar
en: Never compromise the Brotherhood.

speaker: Mirabeau
en: Let these tenets be branded upon your mind. Follow them, and be uplifted. Break them at your peril. Rise, Assassin.

speaker: Mirabeau
en: Arno Dorian is dead. He has been culled from this world, with his sins and failures turned to dust. Tonight he is reborn, a novice of the Assassin Brotherhood.

speaker: M. Durand (Apothecary)
en: Yes, I made that elixir. It's just a few herbs tossed together to make something that stinks. A wealthy fellow, Beaudoin, came in. Wanted something to keep spirits away. I told him he was a fool, but he paid well enough for me to concoct this.

speaker: Marc André (Creditor to victim)
en: I don't care! You owe me!

speaker: Man
en: But I have no money! Please!

speaker: Marc André
en: Shut up while I beat you to a bloody pulp!

speaker: M. Sagne (card player)
en: It couldn't have been Beaudoin who cheated, he lost everything. I've seen the papers, his bank is furious! He owes his creditor thousands! Someone was cheating, but who?

speaker: Counselor Hervé LeGall (Assistant to the victim)
en: My name is LeGall, Counselor to Director of Finance Beaudoin. He locked himself in his office well over a day ago. For some weeks he's been in a state of agitation. It's very sad that it ended this way.

speaker: Second Valet (Works for the Ministry of Finance)
en: The legend must be true! Long ago a Bavarian murderer was executed nearby, and his red ghost has haunted this palace to this day! Have you seen the painting? It appeared from nowhere just yesterday.

speaker: First Valet (Works for the Ministry of Finance)
en: I've actually overheard many very ghostly noises and even the ghost speaking! Through that very door, Beaudoin alone in the room and the ghost speaking with a terrifying accent. I heard this several times.

speaker: Letter
en: The moderate political faction, the Girondists, have been executed. Visit retribution on Andrés Guzmán, an exceptionally effective purveyor of hatred against the members of the Girondist faction. Guzmán is often to be found inciting the crowd in the Louvre gardens. --The Council

speaker: Guzmán
en: They called themselves "moderate", but the Girondists were never moderate, my friends! I ask you, where is the moderation in calling for war? War!

speaker: Citizen
en: That's absurd!

speaker: Guzmán
en: They wanted war and they got it! They brought foreign armies to our borders and put the Revolution in peril! We must sweep out those who are timid in defense of the Revolution! You, citizen, are an example! You cling to the old; you are unwilling to move forward! Brissot, Madame Roland, all of them were an impediment to the Revolution! Whoever slows the Revolution is its enemy!

speaker: Citizen
en: Guzmán is fighting for revolutionary values!

speaker: Crimson Rose
en: I need a bit of assistance. The Count de Choisy is to be arrested today. He is an honorable man, certainly not deserving of the guillotine. The Crimson League and I are busy elsewhere. Could you prevent his arrest? He lives on the rue des Barres, just south of Saint Gervais Church.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Take what you please, men.

speaker: Arno
en: Too late. Damn. I'll see what I can find in there.

speaker: Letter
en: Some partially destroyed papers: "... upon reporting back to the Order, please inform the Grand Master of your intent..."

speaker: Wife
en: Who is that?! I won't come out! They've taken him! My husband. Carried him away, past the church. They spoke of the guillotine!

speaker: Guard 2
en: You're headed to the guillotine.

speaker: De Choisy
en: Damn. I'm of noble birth. I'm better than you! You won't kill me. My friend, the Crimson Rose, will save me.

speaker: Guard 3
en: Stay still!

speaker: De Choisy
en: I shall do as I please, peasant!

speaker: Guard 3
en: That's it! Not one more step!

speaker: De Choisy
en: About time someone freed me! Good God!

speaker: Victor
en: Look what you've gotten us into now.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Shut up in there!

speaker: La Touche
en: So, this is what France has come to. Parasites bleeding the Revolution dry.

speaker: La Touche
en: Your revolutionary brothers and sisters need to eat! And yet here you are, hoarding and hiding like rats! And why? Because you are greedy! You are ungrateful for the freedoms you have been given! Hoarding food is no different than stealing it from the mouths of babes. Justice must be done. Justice prompt, severe, and inflexible. Bring up the condemned! What's this? You've been pardoned! Strap 'em in. Filthy parasite! Anything to say in your defense? No? Good. Keep it moving! Another!

speaker: Prisoners
en: Psst! You! Let us out of here! We're all dead if you don't let us out! Let us go! Just let us out, we won't tell anyone! Free us! For God's sake, I only stole a loaf of bread!

speaker: Victor
en: Hugo, look. It's the watch thief.

speaker: Hugo
en: Well, well, well.

speaker: Victor
en: Come to gloat?

speaker: Arno
en: Come to help. The door...?

speaker: Victor
en: One of the guards has the key. I'm not sure which.

speaker: Arno
en: Not a problem.

speaker: Victor
en: What's this, then?

speaker: Arno
en: I believe it's called a "rescue".

speaker: Victor
en: Why?

speaker: Arno
en: Because, being a thick-headed man mountain, while doing little enough for your long-term prospects, is not actually a capital offense.

speaker: Victor
en: ... Huh?

speaker: Arno
en: Just stay back and let me go first.

speaker: La Touche
en: Next!

speaker: Guard 2
en: Let's go.

speaker: Guard 3
en: Don't I know you, boy?

speaker: Arno
en: I doubt it.

speaker: Guard 3
en: No, no - I do! You're the town drunk!

speaker: Arno
en: I - oh God, I suppose I am, aren't I?

speaker: La Touche
en: Strap him in. Wait a moment. Is that...? Shit! Stop him! Stop him! Protect me! Get him!

speaker: La Touche
en: Fired? But... but why?

speaker: Taxman
en: Because, (Mister) la Touche, your last report contained numerous... errors.

speaker: La Touche
en: Sir, I.. I triple-checked those figures! They're not in error, ten thousand livres simply vanished from His Majesty's treasury!

speaker: Taxman
en: I'm sorry, la Touche. Good day.

speaker: Roi des Thunes
en: la Touche. They tell me you were a taxman.

speaker: La Touche
en: Y-Yes, sir.

speaker: Roi des Thunes
en: Good. I have need of someone like you.

speaker: La Touche
en: It's parasitism, plain and simple.

speaker: Guard
en: Wassat mean?

speaker: La Touche
en: It means greedy bastards skimming for themselves instead of doing their jobs. If you knew half the shit our boss' rats hear...

speaker: Sivert
en: Tell me about this "boss" of yours.

speaker: Germain
en: Very well. May the Father of Understanding guide you.

speaker: All
en: May the Father of Understanding guide us.

speaker: La Touche
en: What would you have me do, Grand Master?

speaker: Germain
en: I'm placing your services at the disposal of our agent on the Convention.

speaker: La Touche
en: Le Peletier?

speaker: Germain
en: No, Le Peletier has his uses, but he is not our only friend in government. Monsieur la Touche, I present to you Monsieur Maximilien de Robespierre.

speaker: Robespierre
en: Monsieur. I understand Versailles is overrun with parasites.

speaker: Assassin
en: I've done some research. An ancient cult! Right here! It's all there on the table.

speaker: Cultist 1
en: Ah! A new initiate! We are using the chalices you stole in tonight's ritual. Enter!

speaker: Cultist 1
en: Welcome to the Cult of Baphomet.

speaker: Cultist 2
en: Sisters and Brothers of Baphomet! We here dedicate the life our beloved Sister, Jeanne, to the glory and power of the wisdom of Baphomet!

speaker: Cultist 3
en: We stand together in gratitude to you, Jeanne, for your bravery.

speaker: Jeanne
en: I yield this, my body, for the good of my Sisters and Brothers in Baphomet.

speaker: Cultist 2
en: We honor your sacrifice.

speaker: Dumas
en: Ah! Arno! A small favor! This is damned awkward, but I promised Bonaparte, damn him! Seems a lady has caught his eye, what the deuce is her name? Juliette? Joséphine! He wants to take a romantic stroll, but the royalists are after him! Bonaparte is to meet her just south of the Palais Bourbon. I need you to clear out any royalists in their path.

speaker: Joséphine
en: I'm flattered that you wished to meet. May I inquire, what is your rank?

speaker: Napoleon
en: Captain... captain for now. I have prospects, though.

speaker: Joséphine
en: I'm sure.

speaker: Napoleon
en: Very good prospects!

speaker: Joséphine
en: Well... it's a lovely day for a walk.

speaker: Napoleon
en: Oh... oh, yes. Of course. Shall we?

speaker: Napoleon
en: So... you, um... you. Damn!

speaker: Joséphine
en: I was born in Martinique, I came to France to marry, but that was a disaster. I am now a divorcée!

speaker: Napoleon
en: Oh.

speaker: Joséphine
en: And you, where did you acquire your... exotic accent?

speaker: Napoleon
en: Corsica.

speaker: Joséphine
en: How delightfully provincial of you! You are a pensive man.

speaker: Napoleon
en: What? Oh. Yes. I was just... musing about how I could manoeuvre, um, how I could...

speaker: Joséphine
en: Take my arm?

speaker: Napoleon
en: Yes!

speaker: Joséphine
en: And have you formed a plan?

speaker: Napoleon
en: No.

speaker: Joséphine
en: The life of a soldier must be terribly exciting! Cavalry charges and flashing blades!

speaker: Napoleon
en: I'm in the artillery.

speaker: Joséphine
en: Oh.

speaker: Napoleon
en: We stand at the back and lob cannon balls at people... I calculate trajectories.

speaker: Joséphine
en: Fascinating!

speaker: Napoleon
en: Well, this has been... I've... you

speaker: Joséphine
en: Yes, it has, hasn't it?

speaker: Napoleon
en: It's just that your, your, those large, luminous... those...

speaker: Joséphine
en: Eyes?

speaker: Napoleon
en: Yes! They are bewitching, I can barely breathe, talk, think! We must meet again!

speaker: Joséphine
en: Oh... yes... perhaps! Well. Ta-ta!

speaker: Napoleon
en: I think that went pretty well.

speaker: Letter
en: Les Enragés were a loose amalgram of extremist radicals. They were lead by Jacques Roux who famously incited food riots. Assassinate one of Jacques Roux's lieutenants preaching to a crowd of sans culottes in the courtyard of Hotel de Cluny.

speaker: Lieutenant
en: The Revolution has taken a wrong turn, citizens! It is left to us to set it on the right path! Jacques Roux showed the way! These bourgeois politicians only listen money and the sword, and we don't have any money! These bastards don't care if you starve; they don't care if you freeze; they don't care if you die! They're as bad as any king! Where is our food? Where is our bread? They've got the bread! They've got money! They've got the guns! But not for long, citizens! Let us go take them!

speaker: Arno
en: It is warm to the touch. This book is bound in human skin. I must find the tanner before more die.

speaker: Tanner
en: As I was saying, I should have stayed in Paris, had a deal with some really high ranking (Sirs). The market's very small in my line of work.

speaker: Guard
en: How is the loot down below? Have you found anything?

speaker: Tanner
en: Everything has been claimed... the golden era is past.

speaker: Guard
en: Right you are! But I heard that you were chasing after other things than gold.

speaker: Tanner
en: I do not know what you mean. Pardon me... there is a man following us from the tavern. Can you help?

speaker: Arno
en: I am too late for this one.

speaker: Tanner
en: RAT! I'll skin you alive!

speaker: Bishop
en: The Marais District. Beautiful mansions, wide gardens and the place to live if you were the Parisian upper crust. Then the revolution happened. Some of these mansions were taken over by the government. Some were abandoned. This one was occupied by Royalists stockpiling guns and money for a coup attempt. Cut their funding. Many chests, but only one is the right one. Do you split up, or stick together? Your choice, Initiates. More Assassins, more loot! Well, actually all but one are fake - you need to find the right one. Go. We rejigged this a bit, so it's a bit more of a training run. And I put in a few extra chests. You need to find the right one. Time to mix it up with some training. Which treasure is the right one? You need to find it, then get the goods. Rebecca and I thought you'd like a challenge - you need to find the right chest before you can get the loot.

speaker: Bishop
en: Sorry, that one's empty. Oooh, sorry. It's empty. Nothing here.

speaker: Bishop
en: Good work! Yep. That's the one. You got the goods. Yes. You found it. We have a winner.

speaker: De Sade
en: Dear fellow! I very much appreciate the inexplicable disappearance of my death warrant. Now, the joys of retribution! After your "removal" of Grignon, my political enemies became reckless. I happen to know that each one is hiding a delightfully salacious secret. Here is a list of items to blackmail them. Steal those items and Grignon's old, debauched neighborhood will remain under my gentle care.

speaker: De Sade
en: Ah, yes. Thank you, Arno. I take such pleasure imposing my will on others. Is that wrong?

speaker: Sagittarius
en: was a virtual representation of one of Arno Dorian's genetic memories, relived by a Helix initiate through the Helix Navigator.

speaker: Saturnus
en: was a virtual representation of one of Arno Dorian's genetic memories, relived by a Helix initiate through the Helix Navigator.

speaker: Beaumarchais
en: Arno! Are you in the mood to go to a party? Mademoiselle Montansier oversees several "actresses" who have intimate liaisons with important people. Any secrets their lovers tell them are sent to Montansier. Those secrets could help move the Revolution in a more fruitful direction. Mademoiselle is hosting a party at her home just north of the Temple. It would be the perfect opportunity to steal them.

speaker: Montansier
en: Welcome, friends! Wine! Wine for everyone! I'm going to perform a speech later on. Perhaps from Phaedra. Let's all get a little drunk first, though, shall we?

speaker: Politician
en: Are you an actress as well?

speaker: Woman
en: I'm sorry, what position do you hold?

speaker: Politician
en: Oh, I've just assumed a seat on the Committee of Public Safety.

speaker: Woman
en: Why yes, I am an actress. Perhaps you care to arrange for a private performance.

speaker: Newspaper
en: Le Père Duchesne May 1790 Mlle. Montansier is about to present another of her trifles. She does well to avoid any political subject matter, as her royalist tendencies cannot be hidden. But are the citizens of Paris expected to endure salacious amusements concercing infidelity among the aristos? At this critical stage of history? Leave our dear Mademoiselle to her pretty costumes and other frippery. We true Parisians have better things to do with our energies!

speaker: Letter
en: Dearest Mlle, I must say, the Count d'Erpin has unusual predilections! But he is very rich, and I'm grateful you introduced us. I have not yet succeeded in gathering the specific information you seek, but next week his wife will be away in the country, and we plan several intimate evenings. I would also like to talk to you about a part for me in the up-coming production of Les Époux mécontents. I believe I would perform charmingly as the ingénue. Bisous! Jacqueline

speaker: Page
en: Dear Diary, Everything is going well. The new play is set to open and everyone who is anybody has promised to attend. Of course, several of my former lovers will be there, and that is sometimes awkward, but c'est la vie! The agents of the Black Office are most pleased with the information I have gathered. I have become an intriguer! It's as profitable as a hit show!

speaker: Beaumarchais
en: Ah! The diary of Mademoiselle Montansier! It will prove excellent entertainment, I'm certain!

speaker: Scorpio
en: was a virtual representation of one of Arno Dorian's genetic memories, relived by a Helix initiate through the Helix Navigator.

speaker: Napoleon
en: This morning I was accosted by three men carrying some poor soul's head atop a pike. Seems they mistook my uniform for a mark of nobility, and demanded I shout "Long live the Republic" to prove my allegiance.

speaker: Arno
en: I suppose handing out tricolour cockades is now passé. What did you do?

speaker: Napoleon
en: I shouted "Long live the Republic."

speaker: Arno
en: A man of principle.

speaker: Napoleon
en: Life is more valuable than dignity. But this is what happens when you give command of the government to half-starved lunatics, and command of the army to bloodthirsty savages.

speaker: Arno
