en: Rouille.

speaker: Napoleon
en: I wanted him assigned to some out-of-the-way garrison, but the man redefines the term "friends in high places." He's untouchable.

speaker: Arno
en: But you know where I can find him.

speaker: Napoleon
en: Rumor about the barracks is that he and a unit of his cronies plan on marching on the Grand Châtelet this afternoon. If he were to meet with an accident, few in France would suffer. My career certainly wouldn't.

speaker: Arno
en: Well, practice your speechmaking.

speaker: Guardsman 1
en: Get their weapons! Nobody try anything!

speaker: Rouille
en: Come on, boys! Find me a warden!

speaker: Prisoner
en: No! No, put me back! Put me back!

speaker: Guardsman 2
en: You hear that? They make such a lovely noise on the way down.

speaker: Prisoner 2
en: Animals!

speaker: Guardsman 3
en: I wonder what a nob sounds like when his skull cracks like an egg, eh?

speaker: Guard 1
en: Sons of bitches! Bastards! Monsters! This is inhuman! You'll go to the guillotine for this! God will judge you!

speaker: Guardsman 4
en: Silence! Don't make this harder on yourselves. Don't move! Hands where I can see them! No tricks! Watch them, men. Keep an eye on them. No sudden movements! Keep still! If they try anything, shoot them.

speaker: Guard 1
en: I don't know what unit you serve with, but thank you.

speaker: Arno
en: You can thank me by getting to the walls and stopping these killings.

speaker: Guardsman 5
en: Fucking hell. What a mess.

speaker: Guardsman 6
en: What do we do with the bodies?

speaker: Guardsman 7
en: Ah, leave 'em.

speaker: Guardsman 8
en: What are we waiting for? More traitors to deal with.

speaker: Guardsman 9
en: Look at these posh bastards. Bet they weren't fed on bread and water.

speaker: Guardsman 10
en: Check their pockets - bet they've got some goodies.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Hold fast, men!

speaker: Guard 2
en: Cut them down!

speaker: Guard 3
en: Protect the prisoners!

speaker: Guardsman 11
en: Death to the traitors!

speaker: Guard 4
en: Beat them back!

speaker: Guard 3
en: Steady!

speaker: Guard 2
en: Into the breach!

speaker: Guard 4
en: Hold that line!

speaker: Guard 3
en: Kill them all!

speaker: Guardsman 13
en: Where's the warden?

speaker: Prisoner 3
en: Burn in hell!

speaker: Guardsman 13
en: Anyone else?

speaker: Prisoner 4
en: He's... He's on the roof.

speaker: Guardsman 13
en: Good lad. Come on, boys! Upstairs!

speaker: Rouille
en: Look, Warden! Your brother's here to visit! Don't you want to see him? Come now, Warden! Let's have a cheer! (Long live the Revolution!) What's the matter? Not a fan of liberty? Freedom bores you? Ah! Look, he misses you! Tut tut, Warden! Your brother will think you rude! Mind, he's lost a bit of weight since last you saw him! Oh, are you sulking, Warden? Well, I'm terribly sorry, Warden! Only, well... we couldn't find the rest of him! Well if you don't want it, I suppose... I suppose it would make a fine souvenir! (Ye sons of France, awake to glory, Hark, hark! what myriads bid you rise!) Come on! Sing! SING!

speaker: Rouille
en: At him, boys!

speaker: Mirabeau
en: If you have orders to remove us from this hall, you must also get authority to use force, for we shall yield to nothing but bayonets!

speaker: Mirabeau
en: Ah, but to administer is to govern, to govern is to reign. That is the essence of the problem.

speaker: Rouille
en: Mister Mirabeau?

speaker: Germain
en: Pathetic, isn't it? Surely France deserves better?

speaker: Rouille
en: What was that?

speaker: Prisoner
en: Palais du Luxembourg....

speaker: La Touche
en: Rouille? Clean up your mess. It's time.

speaker: Rouille
en: Told you I could make him talk.

speaker: Germain
en: You've done well, Captain. Marie?

speaker: Lévesque
en: The price of grain is higher than ever, Grand Master. Our agents are in place to divert the shipments to our docks. They await only your command.

speaker: Germain
en: Good... Starve them. Through famine and fury they will see their false masters for what they are... But do it gradually.

speaker: Lévesque
en: What you're asking will take at least a year, Grand Master. If not two.

speaker: Assassin
en: Arno. Look at that. Jean-Baptiste Rotondo escaped prison. Ever hear of him? He knows a few things about the Assassins. It's likely he'll attempt to get to the Templars and tell them what he knows. Assassinate him before the National Guard can reach him. He's right down there, escaping through the sewers.

speaker: Bartender
en: We're closed. Someone is looking for you.

speaker: Arno
en: Who? The Marquis?

speaker: Arno
en: Élise?

speaker: Arno
en: Élise! Wait! Élise! Stop!

speaker: Thief
en: Who are you? I only took a couple (coins.) Here!

speaker: Margot
en: I've been looking for you, (sir.) Thank you for returning Léon.

speaker: Arno
en: Good luck with him.

speaker: Margot
en: I once had a son.

speaker: Arno
en: I'm sorry.

speaker: Margot
en: No. He's alive. I left him. I began the orphanage afterward.

speaker: Arno
en: Now that's love.

speaker: Margot
en: Sometimes love is a prison. His father taught me that. This, the orphanage, this is my true calling. Léon tells me you could have been the savior of France. Children.

speaker: Arno
en: Madame Margot?

speaker: Margot
en: He's behind the orphanage.

speaker: Arno
en: Little man...

speaker: Arno
en: We have three days until my ship sails.

speaker: Léon
en: So what?

speaker: Arno
en: I'll get the artifact, then I'm gone.

speaker: Léon
en: Fine. But how? Do you have a map to the temple in your coat?

speaker: Arno
en: The list of relics!

speaker: Arno
en: The painting in the cavern. I knew I had seen those plates before. They're drawn here. But this one is missing.

speaker: Arno
en: I'm being serious.

speaker: Léon
en: Meet me upstairs once you find the other two.

speaker: Arno
en: Kids.

speaker: Soldier
en: A band of Royalists have captured several cannons, (my Captain!)

speaker: Murat
en: They'll rip us apart with the grapeshot if we attack.

speaker: Murat
en: I am Leftenant Joachim Murat, sir. At this moment, we are at risk of a bloody civil war. I need a capable man to slip into the Royalist position yonder and spike those cannons. When I see smoke, I'll take that as the signal to attack.

speaker: Royalist
en: Who primed this cannon? It's set to fire!

speaker: Arno
en: You look terrible.

speaker: Mirabeau
en: For months, I have been wrangling the Brotherhood, the National Assembly, and the King. Taken all together they have the political acumen of an especially stupid village council. I believe that excuses my appearance, young man.

speaker: Arno
en: I meant no disrespect, Mentor. I am only... concerned.

speaker: Mirabeau
en: Forget me, Arno. Weep for France. But enough politics. I hope you have happier news. What of (Lord) De La Serre's murderers?

speaker: Arno
en: The King of Beggars is dead. He was carrying this.

speaker: Beylier
en: . You should keep it. It'll do no one any good moldering in a forgotten crypt. Carry it with honor.

speaker: Arno
en: Thank you. I will.

speaker: Mirabeau
en: The mission...?

speaker: Arno
en: The King of Beggars and Sivert were only pawns in a larger game. Someone sent them after (Mister) De La Serre.

speaker: Mirabeau
en: Templars do nothing simply, do they? Do you have anything solid on this mysterious chess player?

speaker: Arno
en: The only lead I have is the instrument that killed De La Serre. A pin fashioned by a silversmith named Germain. But how he's involved, I can't yet say.

speaker: Mirabeau
en: It seems your course is clear. Find this silversmith, learn what part he plays.

speaker: Arno
en: Well, that's not suspicious, is it?

speaker: Guard 1
en: Well, the Pope's condemned us.

speaker: Guard 2
en: How's that?

speaker: Guard 1
en: It's all over the coffee houses. The Pope's condemned the Civil Constitution, the revolution, all of it.

speaker: Guard 2
en: What you suppose that means?

speaker: Guard 1
en: Means we lock up the priests. It's not the lawyers, but it's a start.

speaker: Guard 3
en: He still in there?

speaker: Guard 4
en: I've been here three weeks, and I've never even seen him leave that room, let alone come down the stairs.

speaker: Guard 3
en: Dedicated to his work, is he?

speaker: Guard 4
en: Obsessed, more like. I don't think he really even knows we're here.

speaker: Arno
en: Germain? The silversmith?

speaker: Germain
en: Thank God! They've been holding me for months! Please, get me out of here!

speaker: Arno
en: First, I need to know about this.

speaker: Germain
en: No time! I'll tell you all I know once we're away, but we must leave, before the guards return!

speaker: Arno
en: Fine. Let's go.

speaker: Germain
en: No! They'll be watching the front entrance. We'll have to... go downstairs and across.

speaker: Arno
en: Follow me, then. And stay quiet.

speaker: Arno
en: Follow me. Let's go. Best we move on. This way. Keep moving. Wait. Hold on. Wait here. Hold a moment. Stay there.

speaker: Germain
en: As you say. (Yes.) Very well. Yes, certainly.

speaker: Guard 5
en: You sound like hell.

speaker: Guard 6
en: Whole damn place reeks of boric acid. He swears it's not poisonous, but...

speaker: Guard 5
en: So open the upstairs window and stop complaining.

speaker: Germain
en: Keep one eye to the roofs. They often post sentries there as well.

speaker: Arno
en: Just how important are you as a prisoner?

speaker: Germain
en: Help me! Please! Help! Help! Help me! Hurry! Help!

speaker: Arno
en: Germain! Change of plans...

speaker: Arno
en: No need to do anything foolish. Let the silversmith go.

speaker: Guard
en: Stay back!

speaker: Germain
en: God be good... what have I done?

speaker: Arno
en: Only what you had to. Come, we must go.

speaker: Germain
en: Yes, of course.

speaker: Germain
en: Thank you, my friend. You've done me a great service today.

speaker: Arno
en: Perhaps you can return the favor.

speaker: Germain
en: Yes, of course. I made the first some years ago, on a private contract for a man called Lafrenière. It seemed an unusual commission, I confess curiosity got the better of me. Recently, I started looking into Lafrenière's background and... What I discovered... you wouldn't believe it.

speaker: Arno
en: He's a Templar. Is that what you found?

speaker: Germain
en: Yes, I... I believe so. I didn't know how to take it. In any case, I was careless and Lafrenière found out about my schemes. Kept me under house arrest ever since. I do as he bids. Weapons mostly.

speaker: Arno
en: Where can I find him?

speaker: Germain
en: Well, Lafrenière is a very difficult man to pin down. Not long ago, I overheard him talking about protecting the shipments at la Halle aux Blés. It sounded ominous, whatever he meant. If I may ask, why are you so interested in him?

speaker: Arno
en: He killed someone very dear to me. I want to know why.

speaker: Germain
en: I see. You have my sympathies.

speaker: Arno
en: They will come looking for you again. Make yourself scarce.

speaker: Germain
en: Yes. I believe I might.

speaker: Letter
en: Royalist Chouans are attacking neighboring vineyards in an attempt to intimidate anyone who doesn't support their movement. Go to the farmlands to the south, protect the vineyards and defeat the attacking Chouans.

speaker: Citizens
en: The royals march! Chouans! In the fields! It's the Chouans! We're defenseless! They're burning our crops! They're attacking my neighbor's fields!

speaker: Chouans
en: Back to the old ways! Bloody Jacobins!

speaker: Bishop
en: The Saint-Marcel District, full of tanneries and slaughterhouses. The real estate prices are low, and the stench is high. Nobody comes here if they can avoid it. That makes it a hotbed for shady dealings. Case in point: one of the local tanneries is smuggling out state treasures marked as shoe leather. Find the stolen goods. Many chests, but only one is the right one. Do you split up, or stick together? Your choice, Initiates. More Assassins, more loot! Well, actually all but one are fake - you need to find the right one. Go. We rejigged this a bit, so it's a bit more of a training run. And I put in a few extra chests. You need to find the right one. Time to mix it up with some training. Which treasure is the right one? You need to find it, then get the goods. Rebecca and I thought you'd like a challenge - you need to find the right chest before you can get the loot.

speaker: Bishop
en: Sorry, that one's empty. Oooh, sorry. It's empty. Nothing here.

speaker: Bishop
en: Good work! Yep. That's the one. You got the goods. Yes. You found it. We have a winner.

speaker: Letter
en: A series of brutal robberies targeting mail coaches has swept through Les Invalides. The robberies appear to have been coordinated by someone in an official position with knowledge of valuable shipments. Find the robbers and follow them to discover the leader behind the robberies. Assassinate that leader. -The Council

speaker: Jacques
en: Pluck the chicken?

speaker: Guard 1
en: We did. Here's your precious packet.

speaker: Jacques
en: We'll take it from here, chum.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Who's this go to, anyway? Who is it so important they know what's in the mails?

speaker: Jacques
en: You're not to know! Shove off.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Who're you?

speaker: Arno
en: Other guy couldn't make it. Here's the packet.

speaker: Guard 2
en: I don't like the odd man showing up without my knowledge. Tell Jacques to come himself next time.

speaker: Arno
en: Who's the head man?

speaker: Guard 2
en: You're not to know! Shove off.

speaker: Guard 3
en: Right. I'll take that to Colonel L'Au.

speaker: Letter
en: Several Templars have managed to join the ruling Council of Five Hundred in the Palais Bourbon. From this seat of power, the Templars are using their influence to continue the Reign of Terror. Assassinate the embedded Templars to curtail their influence. -- The Council

speaker: Deputy
en: Napoleon Bonaparte is a direct threat to the Council. He must be stopped somehow.

speaker: Templar
en: There's a simple solution for a problem like him.

speaker: Deputy
en: I suppose. But he's a cagey one. We'd never get close.

speaker: Arno
en: What do you know about grain merchants?

speaker: Élise
en: Good to see you too. Most of them are very poor just now. Why?

speaker: Arno
en: I have a lead on Germain. He has a woman named Marie buying up grain shipments and diverting them to a private dock.

speaker: Élise
en: Marie Lévesque?

speaker: Arno
en: You know her?

speaker: Élise
en: The Lévesques have been Templars since the Third Crusade. Marie was the only one who argued against Germain's exile; I'm not surprised she's thrown in with him.

speaker: Arno
en: Any idea where we might find her?

speaker: Élise
en: Not her, no. But what little grain makes it to Paris these days is unloaded at the Hôtel de Ville docks.

speaker: Arno
en: Promising. I'll start there.

speaker: Élise
en: Perhaps I can learn something of Madame Lévesque's whereabouts.

speaker: Guard
en: Order, order!

speaker: Citizens
en: Let us through! We're starving!

speaker: Guard
en: One at a time!

speaker: Worker 1
en: Hey! Come back here!

speaker: Worker 2
en: You've missed the quay, you dolts!

speaker: Worker 3
en: Where are you going?

speaker: Arno
en: Time to chase a boat.

speaker: Captain
en: To port! Pull! Pull! Pull! Faster, you dogs! Watch to starboard! Row, god damn you!

speaker: Woman
en: Look out!

speaker: Captain
en: Heave to! Tie off that bowline!

speaker: Lévesque
en: Captain. Any problems?

speaker: Captain
en: No, madame.

speaker: Lévesque
en: You have your orders?

speaker: Captain
en: Here, madame.

speaker: Lévesque
en: Good. And I'm instructed to tell you to make certain one of the bags leaks.

speaker: Captain
en: Err... yes, madame.

speaker: Captain
en: Get to work!

speaker: Arno
en: The Palais Luxembourg, eh? And what are you up to there?

speaker: Citizen
en: Who is writing this filth?! Good to see a friend of Mirabeau in these troubling times.

speaker: Arno
en: Who is publishing this propaganda?

speaker: Citizen
en: I don't know, but I'd love to wring their necks. Maybe you find them.

speaker: Arno
en: I'll see what I can do.

speaker: Town crier
en: Come! Read what Versailles doesn't want you to hear! Mirabeau and Marie Antoinette caught together in the Royal Bedchamber! Mirabeau's allies are shocked to discover that he has betrayed the revolution! Mirabeau betrays the revolution! Caught colluding with the King! Mirabeau sympathizes with the King! His Royalist plot exposed!

speaker: Templar
en: What's the next headline?

speaker: Printer
en: "Mirabeau's love child with the Queen revealed!"

speaker: Templar
en: Hah! Perfect, print it!

speaker: Printer
en: How many copies would you like?

speaker: Templar
en: I want to wallpaper Paris with them.

speaker: Printer
en: I think we'll need a bigger machine...

speaker: Templar
en: When will the next batch be ready?

speaker: Printer
en: I'm moving as fast as I can.

speaker: Templar
en: I'll pay double if it's ready by tonight.

speaker: Élise
en: Things have changed a great deal since you left Paris.

speaker: Arno
en: A great deal to be set right.

speaker: Élise
en: And we're no closer to finding Germain.

speaker: Arno
en: That's not entirely true. I have a name.

speaker: Élise
en: Who?

speaker: Arno
en: Robespierre.

speaker: Arno
en: What's all this?

speaker: Élise
en: Robespierre. He's declared today a "Festival of the Supreme Being." A paean to the virtue of the Nation and the citizen's duty toward it.

speaker: Arno
en: Why does that sound familiar?

speaker: Élise
en: As far as Templar doctrine goes, it's a loose interpretation.

speaker: Arno
en: We'll never get close to him in the middle of all this. We'd best retire and wait for a better opportunity.

speaker: Élise
en: Still thinking like an Assassin. This time, I have the plan.

speaker: Arno
en: Oh? And what would that be?

speaker: Élise
en: Think like a Templar.

speaker: Citizens
en: Amazing.... Thought we were supposed to be rationalists now.... What's he thinking? Vive Robespierre! Oh my, that's lovely. Bravo! (Long live the Liberty!) If "Supreme Being" ain't code for "Robespierre," I'll eat my hat. What is he thinking? Ridiculous pomp and circumstance.

speaker: Arno
en: What now?

speaker: Élise
en: Robespierre is unassailable. He's got half the Guard out in force. We'll never get within ten yards of him.

speaker: Arno
en: Just what I said.

speaker: Élise
en: But he's not as popular as he was. The purges, this Supreme Being cult... If we can discredit him, he's finished.

speaker: Arno
en: A massive public spectacle is the perfect venue.

speaker: Élise
en: Exactly. Paint him as a lunatic, and his power will evaporate like snow in April. But we'll need some convincing evidence.

speaker: Arno
en: I have an idea where to start.

speaker: Arno
en: You coming?

speaker: Élise
en: Meet me after. I have my own arrangements to make.

speaker: Robespierre
en: The eternally happy day which the French people consecrates to the Supreme Being has finally arrived. Never has the world he created offered him a sight so worthy of his eyes. He has seen tyranny, crime, and deception reign on earth. At this moment, he sees an entire nation, at war with all the oppressors of the human race, suspend its heroic efforts in order to raise its thoughts and vows to the Great Being who gave it the mission to undertake these efforts and the strength to execute them. Did not his immortal hand, by engraving in the hearts of men the code of justice and equality, write there the death sentence of tyrants? Did not his voice, at the very beginning of time, decree the republic, making liberty, good faith, and justice the order of the day for all centuries and for all peoples? He did not create kings to devour the human species. Neither did he create priests to harness us like brute beasts to the carriages of kings, and to give the world the example of baseness, pride, perfidy, avarice, debauchery, and falsehood to the world. But he created the universe to celebrate his power; he created men to help and to love one another, and to attain happiness through the path of virtue. The Author of Nature linked all mortals together in an immense chain of love and happiness. Perish the tyrants who have dared to break it! Frenchmen, Republicans, it is up to you to cleanse the earth they have sullied and to restore the justice they have banished from it. Liberty and virtue issued together from the breast of the Supreme Being. One cannot reside among men without the other. Generous people, do you want to triumph over all your enemies? Practice justice and render to the Supreme Being the only form of worship worthy of him. People, let us surrender ourselves today, under his auspices, to the just ecstasy of pure joy. Tomorrow, we shall again combat vices and tyrants; we shall give the world an example of republican virtues: and that shall honor the Supreme Being more.

speaker: Arno
en: Let's see... incriminating evidence, incriminating evidence....

speaker: Arno
en: Publiciste de la Révolution française... The day after Marat died.

speaker: Arno
en: A letter.

speaker: Arno
en: Maybe something a bit stronger. Not quite what I'm looking for. Interesting, but not particularly helpful. Hardly the sort of thing to topple a tyrant with.

speaker: Arno
en: , Tallien, ... these are all deputies of the National Convention. Lists of political figures written in the hand of a man fond of sending his rivals to the guillotine... yes, these should do nicely.

speaker: Élise
en: Well?

speaker: Arno
en: A list of names—fifty or so deputies of the National Convention. All written in Robespierre's hand and all opposed to him.

speaker: Élise
en: I imagine those good gentlemen would be quite interested to know they're on that list. But first...

speaker: Élise
en: Monsieur Robespierre has brought his own refreshments. Distract the guards. I have an idea.

speaker: Arno
en: Distract the guards. Right.

speaker: Robespierre
en: Armed in turn with the daggers of fanaticism and the poisons of atheism, they can no more tear the world from... People, fear no more their sacrilegious conspiracies! It is wisdom above all that our guilty enemies want to drive from the republic. We must be generous toward the good, compassionate toward the unfortunate, and inexorable toward the wicked.

speaker: Guard
en: Away with you.

speaker: Élise
en: Powdered . Causes hallucinations. This will make him look mad. Now we have to make him look dangerous.

speaker: Arno
en: The list of names.

speaker: Élise
en: It must fall into the right hands. Anonymously. If our involvement gets out, it'll tip Germain off.

speaker: Arno
en: Leave that part to me.

speaker: Robespierre
en: He has returned to nothingness, this monster which the spirit of kings has spewed forth over France. Let all the crimes and ills of the world disappear with him. Armed in turn with the daggers of fanaticism and the poisons of atheism, kings still conspire to assassinate humanity. If they can no longer disfigure the Divinity with superstition in order to implicate him in their transgressions, they endeavor to banish it from the earth, to reign alone with crime. People, fear no more their sacrilegious conspiracies, they can no more tear the world from the breast of its author, than the remorse from their own hearts. You who are wretched, hold up your woeful heads: you can again raise your eyes to the sky with impunity. Heroes of the country, your generous devotion is not a brilliant folly; the minions of tyranny may be able to assassinate you, but it is not in their power to annihilate you completely. Man, whoever you are, you can again think well of yourself. You can attach your transitory life to God himself and to immortality. Let nature thus regain all its magnificence, and wisdom all its empire, the Supreme Being is not destroyed.

speaker: Critic 1
en: Robespierre natters on about freedom and mercy while thousands go to the guillotine. If Danton were alive to see this, he would choke on his own grief.

speaker: Woman
en: But what can we do? For all his horrors, the Committee stands behind him.

speaker: Critic 1
en: Only so long as he condemns strangers. When he turns his gaze upon them, we shall see how well they love him.

speaker: Woman
en: Pray, monsieur (mister), might I borrow your handkerchief?

speaker: Critic 1
en: Certainly, madame. Hmm.

speaker: Woman
en: What is it?

speaker: Critic 1
en: I think it's the solution to our problems. Pardon, madame.

speaker: Critic 2
en: "Conduct unbecoming?" Me? Who the hell does Robespierre think he is?

speaker: Servant
en: Jealous of your success, most like.

speaker: Critic 2
en: Yes, yes, that would be it, wouldn't it? Someone really ought to teach that jumped up little troll a lesson....

speaker: Servant
en: Quite so, sir.

speaker: Servant
en: What is it, sir?

speaker: Critic 2
en: A pickpocket, damn your eyes!

speaker: Servant
en: Bloody hell! What did they steal?

speaker: Critic 2
en: Nothing, I....

speaker: Critic 3
en: Look at that strutting popinjay. "Cult of the Supreme Being" indeed.

speaker: Servant
en: Sir! Take care, someone might hear you!

speaker: Critic 3
en: And if they do? Robespierre is popular, but he is not God, no matter what he thinks. He can't touch me.

speaker: Servant
en: Even so....

speaker: Critic 3
en: Even so nothing. A change is coming soon. All it requires is the proper spark to light the tinder.

speaker: Arno
en: This should set things in motion.

speaker: Servant
en: What's that?

speaker: Critic 3
en: Hmm?

speaker: Servant
en: In your pocket there.

speaker: Critic 3
en: I'm not sure... oh. Pardon me, I must....

speaker: Robespierre
en: It is wisdom, above all, that our enemies want to drive from the Republic. To wisdom alone does it belong to consolidate the prosperity of empires; it is for her to guarantee the fruits of our courage. Let us therefore associate...

speaker: Critics
en: "Being a list of enemies of the Revolution....?" ...Half a hundred names here! Robespierre's gone too far this time!

speaker: Élise
en: That's set the fox in the henhouse.

speaker: Arno
en: Pity the hens. Now what?

speaker: Élise
en: We wait. It won't take long. Once Robespierre has lost the support of the people, he'll be no more use to Germain. And when Germain abandons him...

speaker: Arno
en: ...he's vulnerable. Let's go.

speaker: Citizen
en: See that fella over there? Jacques Necker. That's right, Necker! The man we all wanted in charge of the banks! Now look at 'im, poor old codger. Can't even talk his way past a border dog. Bet he's got a thing or two in his luggage, eh? Bet he's got some secrets squirreled away in his pockets, heh. Man like him.

speaker: Necker
en: My papers are in order, as you yourself can see.

speaker: Official
en: Are they?

speaker: Necker
en: Although I am a Swiss citizen, I'm sure you're familiar with the great service I have given to France.

speaker: Official
en: Did you?

speaker: Necker
en: I very nearly saved the country, my dear fellow. Damn near. As Finance Minister. You would be aware of this, no doubt.

speaker: Official
en: Would I?

speaker: Necker
en: The Bastille! They tore it down because the king sacked me. He put me back in charge in a trice after that!

speaker: Official
en: Did he?

speaker: Necker
en: So, you understand that I have every right to return to my native land and spend the remainder of my days sipping hot chocolate on the shores of .

speaker: Official
en: Do you?

speaker: Letter
en: "Monsieur Necker, I have successfully secreted your valuables with three trusted men who can be counted upon to disperse the funds in ways that will allow us to weaken the Revolution in view of returning a monarch to the throne. These men are eminently trustworthy. The locations are as follows: 7 rue St-Jacques, 14 rue St-Geneviève, and the barn at the end of rue St-Jacques. Respectfully, your servant --"

speaker: Necker
en: Really, this is impossible! I'm making a simple trip to my homeland!

speaker: Official
en: Are you?

speaker: Arno
en: Here. I've come across quite a lot of money recently. Take this and buy yourself a barrel of rum. And let this revered gentleman through. He's suffered enough.

speaker: Necker
en: Young man! That is extraordinarily kind!

speaker: Official
en: It is!

speaker: Lenormand
en: You're here! I foresaw that someone would come help me! I read the tarot for powerful friends, and now some believe I influence those friends and they wish me harm! I have seen my enemies ... in a dream! Come with me and I will sense their presence.

speaker: Lenormand
en: You, citizen, don't have long to live.

speaker: Man
en: What!?

speaker: Lenormand
en: Citizen, I sense that your husband is having an affair.

speaker: Woman
en: I beg your pardon!

speaker: Lenormand
en: In my dream, one of the murderers was from the country. Yes, a farmer of sorts. He is dangerous! I feel an evil presence! Yes, he is somewhere nearby. I am sure of it! That's him!

speaker: Lenormand
en: Efficiently done! I feel that it's about to rain ... Ah!

speaker: Lenormand
en: I remember now! A soldier! Out to kill me! Look for a man in uniform. A voice is whispering to me. A man with dark intentions in just to the east! ... Or, wait, east or north, it is not clear! Possibly south. That one! Just as in my dream!

speaker: Lenormand
en: Sent to the Great Beyond! I have the distinct sense that a man in the legal profession wishes me harm! A lawyer. I sense a man capable of unspeakable violence! Oh, I beg your pardon, it is you! Still, someone lurks about here with murderous intent! There!

speaker: Lenormand
en: He's joined the choir invisible! And a shady character! Yes, I see him in my mind's eye. A shyster! A bandit! The vibrations of danger are all about us! Even in this very spot! Ah! The man from my dream!

speaker: Lenormand
en: I thank you, my friend. I sense you have started down a difficult path. I wish you success. I thank you, my friend. I sense you have seen the deadly effects of politics. I wish you well in choosing your path. I thank you, my friend, come for a tarot reading some time, I sense you have an interesting future.

speaker: Lenormand
en: I sense you have lost a loved one. May you live in honour of her memory.

speaker: Assassin
en: There are fake Assassin relics planted in the tapestry district. We hope to lure curious Templars into the open with them.

speaker: Arno
en: How can I help?

speaker: Assassin
en: Go and check if there has been any interest in these tapestries, it may lead you to a Templar agent.

speaker: Worker
en: You won't believe it, but the tapestry you're interested in was just stolen!

speaker: Arno
en: What are the odds...

speaker: Worker
en: Ask around, someone must've seen where the thief went.

speaker: Citizen 1
en: Keep after him!

speaker: Citizen 2
en: I saw a man running!

speaker: Citizen 3
en: Sorry, I have no idea what you're talking about.

speaker: Citizen 4
en: I could swear someone just ran into those sewers in front of me.

speaker: Citizen 5
en: Yes, someone else came out of the sewers just now. They were running south, away from the Panthéon.

speaker: Citizen 6
en: That-a-way!

speaker: Citizen 7
en: He just went by!

speaker: Citizen 8
en: No, no thanks. I'm not interested.

speaker: Citizen 9
en: Saw someone running west just now. What?! No tip?

speaker: Citizen 10
en: Yes! He went left! Wait, no, right! No, left! I think...

speaker: Citizen 11
en: You're on his heels!

speaker: Citizen 12
en: Run! Get him!

speaker: Thief
en: I've got the tapestry you asked for.

speaker: Templar
en: Good, did you run into any trouble?

speaker: Thief
en: Someone tried to follow me, but I think I lost him.

speaker: Templar
en: You might have led him here? You idiot!

speaker: Taurus
en: was a virtual representation of one of Arno Dorian's genetic memories, relived by a Helix initiate through the Helix Navigator.

speaker: Arno
en: Élise! Élise! Élise? Damn it! Where was it... l'Hôtel Voysin? Merde. (Shit.)

speaker: Élise
en: Who are you?

speaker: Élise
en: What are you doing here?

speaker: Arno
en: Later!

speaker: Élise
en: What's going on? Where is Monsieur Lafrenière?

speaker: Arno
en: He's dead.

speaker: Élise
en: What?

speaker: Arno
en: Go! I'll explain later!

speaker: Thugs
en: Get her! Cut them off! Kill her! She's here! Move in!

speaker: Élise
en: No way past this one.

speaker: Arno
en: Shall we?

speaker: Élise
en: Let's.

speaker: Arno
en: What's wrong?

speaker: Élise
en: I'm... not sure how to get out again.

speaker: Arno
en: I'll climb up and take a look.

speaker: Élise
en: How do we get out of here? Just admit it. You're lost. Where to? Where do we go? Any bright ideas?

speaker: Thugs
en: Where are they? Find them! Catch them!

speaker: Thug 1
en: Dammit! Another dead end.

speaker: Thug 2
en: Can't see a damn thing in here! How the hell do we get out?

speaker: Thug 1
en: They must be in here somewhere!

speaker: Thug 2
en: Over there! No, wait, dammit, that's Claude.

speaker: Arno
en: Two of them up ahead.

speaker: Élise
en: You take that one. I'll handle his friend.

speaker: Élise
en: What now?

speaker: Arno
en: Too many of them to sneak past. We'll have to work together - take them out quietly.

speaker: Thug 3
en: Have you seen a young woman? Tall? Red hair?

speaker: Élise
en: I think that was all of them.

speaker: Arno
en: We're clear. There's a bigger group coming up, though.

speaker: Thug 4
en: Did you see a young woman come through here?

speaker: Civilian
en: No. Desole.

speaker: Arno
en: Wait. Snipers.

speaker: Élise
en: I see them. Perhaps you can get a better angle from the roof.

speaker: Élise
en: Looks like the last of them.

speaker: Arno
en: Let's get out of here.

speaker: Thug 5
en: They can't have gotten far. Find them!

speaker: Arno
en: Go on. I'll distract them. Trust me. Meet me tomorrow at Café Théâtre. I'll explain everything.

speaker: Élise
en: You're mad. I'll be there.

speaker: Arno
en: I may be a little late.

speaker: Élise
en: We should split up.

speaker: Arno
en: I'm not sure that's...

speaker: Élise
en: Less chance we both get caught that way.

speaker: Arno
en: I suppose that's true.

speaker: Élise
en: We'll rendezvous inside. If you get a shot at Germain, you take it.

speaker: Arno
en: Germain's built himself quite a fortress. I can't see any weak spots.

speaker: Guard 1
en: I don't like it. Le Peletier is dead, Rouille, Lévesque... and now I'm hearing rumors someone killed la Touche in Versailles.

speaker: Guard 2
en: You worry too much. The Grand Master has everything under control.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Robespierre thought the same thing.

speaker: Guard 3
en: Was there a storm last night?

speaker: Guard 4
en: I don't think so.

speaker: Guard 3
en: Huh. I was on patrol duty in the tower and I could have sworn I heard thunder.

speaker: Guard 4
en: I never heard anything.

speaker: Guard 5
en: It seem like the Grand Master spends a lot of time in the catacombs to you?

speaker: Guard 6
en: You haven't heard? He thinks he's Jacques de Molay reborn or some such.

speaker: Guard 5
en: You're joking.

speaker: Guard 6
en: Not even a little. He's probably down there trying to commune with his past life or something equally ridiculous. Mad as a hatter.

speaker: Guard 5
en: I don't think de Molay is even buried down there.

speaker: Guard 6
en: Like I said. Mad as a hatter.

speaker: Guard 7
en: You think something's about to happen?

speaker: Guard 8
en: Why do you ask?

speaker: Guard 7
en: The Grand Master seems unusually preoccupied lately.

speaker: Guard 8
en: With that one, it's better not to ask questions.

speaker: Guard 9
en: Look what I found!

speaker: Guard 10
en: What in God's name is that?

speaker: Guard 9
en: A bit of the king's hair.

speaker: Arno
en: What the hell was that?

speaker: Germain
en: So the prodigal Assassin returns. I suspected as much when la Touche stopped sending his tax revenues. You've become quite the thorn in my side. I assume Robespierre was your doing as well? No matter. His Reign of Terror served its purpose. The metal has been fired and shaped. Quenching it will only set its form. Why so persistent? Is it revenge? Did Bellec indoctrinate you so thoroughly that you do his bidding even now? Or is it love? Has de la Serre's daughter turned your head?

speaker: Germain
en: The direct approach from an Assassin? How refreshing.

speaker: Arno
en: How...? What?

speaker: Élise
en: What happened here?

speaker: Arno
en: Germain's got some kind of weapon... I've never seen its like before. He got away from me.

speaker: Élise
en: He didn't come past me. He must still be down there.

speaker: Arno
en: Élise!

speaker: Germain
en: And (Miss) de la Serre as well. This is quite the reunion.

speaker: Arno
en: Stay hidden. Keep him talking.

speaker: Élise
en: Did you think this day would never come? That because François de la Serre had no sons to avenge him, that your crime would go unanswered?

speaker: Germain
en: Revenge, is it? Your vision is as narrow as your father's. Revenge? Bah! Your vision is as narrow as your father's.

speaker: Élise
en: You're one to talk. How wide of vision was your grab for power?

speaker: Germain
en: Power? Don't be absurd! Power? No no no no, you're smarter than that! This was never about power. It's always been about control. Did your father teach you nothing? The Order has grown complacent. The Order has rotted from within! We've abandoned purpose for base pleasures! For centuries we've focused our attentions on the trappings of power: the titles of nobility, the offices of Church and State. So obsessed with clinging to the trappings of power we abandoned our purpose. Caught in the very lie we crafted to shepherd the masses.

speaker: Élise
en: I'll kill you.

speaker: Germain
en: Have you heard nothing I've said? And you think that will accomplish anything? You're not listening. Killing me won't stop anything. My design is larger than my own life. When our brother Templars see the old institutions crumble, they will adapt. In the wake of revolution, the Order will adapt. Through this new revolution, a new order will be born, one that chains men with gold and silver. They will retreat to the shadows and we will, at last, be the Secret Masters we were meant to be. So come – kill me if you can. I've already won. Unless you can miracle up a new King and halt the Revolution in its tracks, it does not matter. So kill me, if that will slake your thirst for revenge. It changes nothing!

speaker: Élise
en: I can't find an opening!

speaker: Arno
en: We'll have to take him together.

speaker: Germain
en: Skulk all you like. It makes no difference. I will find you. The darkness cannot protect you. Do you think yourself safe in your shadows? You cannot hide from me, boy! Do you think I won't find you? You cannot hide from me. I grow tired of waiting. Where are you hiding, Assassin? There you are! I have you now! I see you, Assassin! A waste of my time! Oh, please, you'll have to do better than that! Laughable! Jacques de Molay speaks through me. How can you to prevail? What is it you hope to accomplish here? Must we continue this pointless charade? You're trying my patience. I commend you for making it this far, but there is no victory for you here. Come, Assassin. Let's bring this to its inevitable conclusion.

speaker: Élise
en: Arno!

speaker: Arno
en: I'm stuck!

speaker: Élise
en: He's getting away!

speaker: Arno
en: Wait - I'm almost free.

speaker: Élise
en: I can take him!

speaker: Arno
en: No you can't. Not alone. Wait for me!

speaker: Élise
en: I'm sorry.

speaker: Arno
en: ÉLISE!

speaker: Arno
en: Élise! ÉLISE! Élise! No.

speaker: Germain
en: Bravo. You've slain the villain. That is how you've cast this little morality play in your mind, isn't it? I'm not really here. I'm not really there, either. At the moment, I'm bleeding out on the floor of the Temple. But it seems the Father of Understanding has seen fit to give us this time to talk.

speaker: Germain
en: Ah. A particular favorite of mine. I did not understand the visions that haunted my mind, you see. Great towers of gold, cities shining white as silver. I thought I was going mad. Then I found this place - Jacques de Molay's vault. Through his writings, I understood.

speaker: Arno
en: Understood what?

speaker: Germain
en: That somehow, through the centuries, I was connected to Grand Master de Molay. That I had been chosen to purge the Order of the decadence and corruption that had set in like rot. And to wash the world clean, and restore to the truth the Father of Understanding intended.

speaker: Arno
en: That seems to have gone over well.

speaker: Germain
en: Prophets are seldom appreciated in their own time. Exile and abasement forced me to reevaluate my strategy. Find new avenues for the realization of my purpose.

speaker: Arno
en: No matter the cost?

speaker: Germain
en: New order never comes without destruction of the old. And if men are made to fear untrammeled liberty, so much the better. A brief taste of chaos will remind them why they crave obedience.

speaker: Germain
en: It appears we part ways here. Think on this: the march of progress is slow, but it is inevitable as a glacier. All you have accomplished is to delay the inevitable. One death cannot stop the tide. Perhaps it will not be my hand that shepherds mankind back to its proper place – but it will be someone's. Think on this when you remember her.

speaker: Arno
en: The Creed of the Assassin Brotherhood teaches us that nothing is forbidden to us. Once, I thought that meant we were free to do as we would. To pursue our ideals, no matter the cost. I understand now. Not a grant of permission, the Creed is a warning.

speaker: Arno
en: Ideals too easily give way to dogma. Dogma becomes fanaticism. No higher power sits in judgment of us. No supreme being watches to punish us for our sins. In the end, only we ourselves can guard against our obsessions. Only we can decide whether the road we walk carries too high a toll.

speaker: Arno
en: We believe ourselves redeemers, avengers, saviors. We make war on those who oppose us, and they in turn make war on us. We dream of leaving our stamp upon the world...

speaker: Arno
en: ... even as we give our lives in a conflict that will be recorded in no history book. All that we do, all that we are, begins and ends with ourselves.

speaker: Terra
en: was a virtual representation of one of Arno Dorian's genetic memories, relived by a Helix initiate through the Helix Navigator.

speaker: The Lost Jewel
en: was a genetic memory.

speaker: Known Owners
en: Jean-Baptiste Tavernier, Louis XIV, Louis XVI, Marie Antoinette, Jean le Chien Current Status: UnknownThe history of this massive diamond is surrounded in mystery. The first known buyer was Jean-Baptiste Tavernier. The stone, also called French Blue (Le bleu de France), was sold to King Louis XIV of France in 1668. In 1792, during the French Revolution, the Hope Diamond was stolen from the royal treasury, alongside the other French Crown Jewels.This Piece of Eden possesses unknown powers and abilities but is said to carry a curse, leading to an early, violent death for anyone wearing it.

speaker: Bishop
en: 1793. The French Army is looking for a few good men.

speaker: Marcourt
en: Is that a sword you're holding, boy, or a spade?

speaker: Marcourt
en: Perhaps farming would be a wiser vocation.

speaker: Bishop
en: General Marcourt. Butchered people all over France in the name of liberty. Templars love this guy.

speaker: Bishop
en: The revolution wasn't moving quickly enough for Marcourt and his Templar conspirators.

speaker: Conspirators
en: For de Molay.

speaker: Bishop
en: So, they planned a military coup. What Marcourt didn't know, was that one of his Templar conspirators wasn't a Templar at all. Alexandre Dumas. Military hero of the new Republic. Friend of the Brotherhood.

speaker: Bishop
en: Dumas was hardcore. A war hero that stood alone against entire battalions. Napoleon compared him to a Roman .

speaker: Bishop
en: The tournament is Marcourt's play to recruit the best and brightest for his coup. Dumas' counter is to invite the Assassins to compete. The winners of the tournament get to meet Marcourt in person. Win the tournament and kill the Templar conspirators.

speaker: Town crier
en: Think you have what it takes, citizens? Step up and test your mettle!

speaker: Bishop
en: You're not getting into that tournament without letters of permission. You can find some nearby, but they won't be easy to get.

speaker: Bishop
en: They're expecting you to be a French soldier, so not killing other French soldiers will help you blend in. Hey! If you keep killing people, they're going to know somethings up.

speaker: Bishop
en: That's the last letter. Head over to the first event.

speaker: Announcer 1
en: The Paris guard, here to compete! Do our city proud, citizens!

speaker: Bishop
en: Time for a little parkour demonstration. I want to see how far you can push it.

speaker: Announcer 1
en: The team from Paris has passed the obstacle course! Time for the duel!

speaker: Bishop
en: No surprise you smoked the competition in a climbing contest, but Marcourt's looking for fighters. Let's give him what he wants.

speaker: Announcer 2
en: Combatants! We are ready to begin. While we are testing your skill at combat, try not to kill each other. Save your blades and bullets for the enemy!

speaker: Bishop
en: Ok. Looks like you need to raise your team's flag while the other team try to stop you. Good luck!

speaker: Announcer 2
en: Everybody ready? En garde! (On your guard!)

speaker: Announcer 2
en: One flag has been taken down! Another flag is down! One more flag is down! All of the flags are down! Paris wins the duel!

speaker: Bishop
en: Nice! Time to get to Marcourt. Talk to Dumas over there, and he'll take you past the guards.

speaker: Dumas
en: Congratulations, citizens, you have fought bravely! Follow me, warriors, and you will receive your honors. Seeing you fight reminds me of my days in the Free Legion.

speaker: Dumas
en: Good, the guards can't hear us now. It seems you were the right choice for our little plot. Marcourt is in there with some of his associates, and he doesn't suspect anything. This traitor needs to be removed, for the safety of the revolution.

speaker: Dumas
en: I was hoping you'd be a little more discreet. The fatalities you've caused have raised suspicion. Marcourt has summoned his bodyguards. It won't be easy to get close to him. You're in for a fight, but you must do what you can to make sure Marcourt and his allies don't succeed. Good luck.

speaker: Dumas
en: I made a mistake trusting you. I can't believe you have called so much attention to yourselves. The number of guards you've killed has scared Marcourt. He is in there waiting for you, you're walking into a trap. There's no turning back now. Maybe you can salvage this plan and kill him anyways. Good luck.

speaker: Marcourt
en: So these are the Parisians we've been hearing so much about. Come forward, citizens, I'd like to shake your hand. We need men like you, citizens, in the French Army. The revolution is in danger, but not from its foreign enemies. The politicians of France have put our government on the wrong course. Strong men, like us, must correct that course. Don't be shy, citizen! We have much to discuss.

speaker: Marcourt
en: Ah! The Assassins are here. You're all great warriors. It's a shame we couldn't have been on the same side... Men! Put this scum in the ground!

speaker: Marcourt
en: What? Traitors!

speaker: Bishop
en: That's a wrap. Probably time to get outta there.

speaker: Bishop
en: The revolution is safer with Marcourt gone. Nice work.

speaker: Bishop
en: The Hôtel-Dieu - the oldest hospital in Paris. Centuries older than the famous Notre-Dame Cathedral, which is down the street. Hospitals as we know them haven't exactly been invented yet, so you're more likely to get sick inside than to leave cured. The Templars are using the building's sewers to smuggle out artifacts they stole from Notre-Dame. Go in and get the goods.

speaker: Citizen 1
en: We can't take much more. Three men are terrorizing the neighborhood. Stealing, fighting, drinking, passing off counterfeit money, taking whatever and whoever they want. If we resist, they threaten us with the guillotine! They have names for themselves: the big one's the Turtle, the slimy one calls himself the Snake and the really, really brutal one is the Bear. All right in front of us, all around the marketplace.

speaker: Thug 1
en: What have we here?

speaker: Citizen 2
en: My bracelet!

speaker: Thug 1
en: So many lovely things!

speaker: Citizen 3
en: Where'd my money pouch go?

speaker: Thug 1
en: I love being out among the people! I don't like the looks of that one! Take him down.

speaker: Thug 2
en: That lot won't complain again, that's for damn sure.

speaker: Gang member
en: Did you see the face on that fish-monger? I nearly shit my pants!

speaker: Thug 2
en: Not as bad as he shit his!

speaker: Arno
en: What have you been doing?

speaker: Léon
en: Nothing. Did you find the lock?

speaker: Arno
en: Yes. Now I need the key.

speaker: Léon
en: You know the soldier carrying the chest for the little commandant? I just saw him in the market.

speaker: Arno
en: And I told you to stay here, remember?

speaker: Léon
en: "(Yes, sir.)"

speaker: Arno
en: There you are. Now lead me to the golden key.

speaker: Lieutenant
en: Alert me if you see anything unusual.

speaker: Soldier
en: Yes, sir.

speaker: Lieutenant
en: What do you have for me this time?

speaker: Raider 1
en: Silver, nearly enough to fill a chest.

speaker: Lieutenant
en: Give it to me.

speaker: Raider 1
en: The Commandant still suspects nothing?

speaker: Lieutenant
en: He is occupied in Paris. Your usual fee, plus a promotion.

speaker: Raider 1
en: Tres bon. A pleasure doing business with you.

speaker: Lieutenant
en: Guards! I will have you arrested!

speaker: Arno
en: You will do no such thing. Tell me the location of the chest containing the golden key or I shall reveal your thievery.

speaker: Lieutenant
en: I am merely seeking a harmless profit.

speaker: Arno
en: Like a rat hungry for apples?

speaker: Lieutenant
en: How did you know

speaker: Arno
en: Surely the Commandant will find the comparison... enlightening.

speaker: Lieutenant
en: The chest is under guard within the caverns. Here.

speaker: Arno
en: Merci. Now get out of my sight.

speaker: Raider 2
en: Invader! We will find you!

speaker: Arno
en: All that security for a key. What lies behind that door?

speaker: Arno
en: Where is the owner of this shop?

speaker: Man
en: The Jeweler? Gone... in the catacombs. He was attempting to open a tomb. I have heard nothing from him for days.

speaker: Letter
en: M. Robespierre, I have succeeded in beguiling some workshops near the Barrière des Martyrs into using defective materials in the manufacture of military armaments. I have further arranged for the defective arms to be delivered to the troops commanded by Captain Bonaparte. I think we can be certain that the young captain's rising star will soon begin to fall. -- St. Just

speaker: Tussaud
en: I am Madame Tussaud. I'm adept at making wax figures and death masks. I promised the Assembly I would make masks of famous victims of the guillotine. It's grisly, but it was the only way to get out of prison! And now, someone has stolen the heads I was given! Could you please find them for me?

speaker: Assistant 1
en: A friend found out something you might find important. She sent me this letter.

speaker: Letter
en: Chère Madame, I have learned that a certain politican, flushed with pride in his role over-throwing the Girondins, has procured the head of Jacques-Pierre Brissot, recently stolen from you. He works near the Conciergerie. - Your devoted friend.

speaker: Assistant 2
en: Rumor has it that a soldier who guards Sainte-Chapelle wanted the head of Olympe de Gouges. He was in love with her from afar.

speaker: Assistant 3
en: The judge at the Palais de Justice who condemned Jacques Hébert apparently wanted Hébert's head as a trophy.

speaker: Letter
en: "M. Lemaitre, I have retrieved the package. Fear not, I have hidden both our objects within the walls of the Conciergerie, each locked within a chest. I possess the single key that opens them both. --LeNôtre"

speaker: Letter
en: "Captain LeNôtre, I have purchased both heads from our friend. They are kept in chests in the Conciergerie. I have the single key that opens them both. -- M. Lemaitre"

speaker: Tussaud
en: You have them! I can make the death masks and be safe. Oh! What a world in which we live!

speaker: V - Crux
en: was a virtual representation of one of Arno Dorian's genetic memories, relived by a Helix initiate through the Helix Navigator.

speaker: Venus
en: was a virtual representation of one of Arno Dorian's genetic memories, relived by a Helix initiate through the Helix Navigator.

speaker: VI - Noctis
en: was a virtual representation of one of Arno Dorian's genetic memories, relived by a Helix initiate through the Helix Navigator.

speaker: Chénier
en: You there! Are you the muse to answer my call? The pleading of a poet with the honor of France in my heart! Say the name Jacques-Louis David and see if you don't gag on the sound. Well, I have written a series of poems satirizing the life of that most despicable propagandist. Sadly, the final verses are under lock and key in my abode. If you could retrieve them, the people of France would learn the truth about David and his confabulations! And my legacy would be assured! Go!

speaker: Guard 1
en: What sort of damage can a poet do? "Reprends ta robe d'or..."! I'm not seeing it.

speaker: Guard 2
en: Ah, it's a matter of pride, mostly. The Revolution's not a thing for humor.

speaker: Guard 1
en: So say you. I been laughing my arse off. It's the only way to keep your head on.

speaker: Guard 3
en: I never understood poems, myself. What's in these we should worry about?

speaker: Guard 4
en: Colorful metaphors, trenchant hyperbole, that sort of thing. All the sort of rubbish the overeducated adore.

speaker: Guard 3
en: We're looking to kill a man over a few metaphors?

speaker: Guard 4
en: As good as any other given reason these days.

speaker: Chénier
en: Oh, my verse! Bravo, (my friend), bravo! Now all of France may hear the conclusion of "Le Jeu de Paume" and see the true hues that color Jacques-Louis David! Ah, they'll lose their heads with laughter, I guarantee.

speaker: VII - Dies
en: was a virtual representation of one of Arno Dorian's genetic memories, relived by a Helix initiate through the Helix Navigator.

speaker: Virgo
en: was a virtual representation of one of Arno Dorian's genetic memories, relived by a Helix initiate through the Helix Navigator.

speaker: Tussaud
en: Arno! I need your help once more! The man who denounced me is furious that I've escaped the guillotine! He sent men to my shop to apprehend me, I dare not return there! Could you please go to my shop and make sure my assistants are safe? And please, please remove that horrid man.

speaker: Sans-culottes 1
en: Patience! That ol' bag will show up!

speaker: Sans-culottes 2
en: Pals around with the aristos, then makes their death masks!

speaker: Sans-culottes 3
en: Somebody's gonna have to make hers! When's she coming back? Come on, speak!

speaker: Assistant 1
en: She should've been back hours ago!

speaker: Assistant 2
en: Let us go, we don't know anything!

speaker: Sans-culottes 2
en: Sure, so you can warn her? Not likely.

speaker: Letter
en: "Keep watch over the shop. I'll take some men to her waxwork exhibition. She's sure to show up one place or the other and at last I'll exact my own measure of justice. --Jean Lessard"

speaker: Letter
en: "You escaped prison, but you cannot escape me. You flaunt your ties to the aristos and revel in your fancy gowns and refined airs, but I will never forget how you spurned me all those years ago! -- Jean Lessard"

speaker: Bishop
en: 1789. Paris is starving, and the price of bread just tripled. Working-class women are about to change the course of the revolution.

speaker: Foreman
en: Mind your business, sweetheart.

speaker: Théroigne
en: And you mind yours, citizen.

speaker: Bishop
en: Théroigne de Méricourt. She was the 18th century Joan of Arc - and she didn't take no for an answer.

speaker: Théroigne
en: That bounty could feed a hundred starving poor. Or one nobleman.

speaker: Driver
en: Villainous whore! Find a brothel and make yourself use

speaker: Driver
en: Woah!

speaker: Bishop
en: While Méricourt was fighting to keep Paris fed, Antoinette and the royals were throwing parties.

speaker: Antoinette
en: Bring us more of this cake!

speaker: Théroigne
en: Let's tell the royals that our families must eat too!

speaker: Bishop
en: For the Templars, this march isn't about bread, it's about royal blood...

speaker: Crowd
en: Bread! Bread!

speaker: Templars
en: Blood! Blood!

speaker: Bishop
en: This bread march really ignites the revolution. Protect it, and keep it peaceful.

speaker: Bishop
en: Okay, Initiates. Keep Méricourt and her Amazon alive. Powerful people don't want this march to happen.

speaker: Théroigne
en: We must march to Versailles! Citizens! Haven't you had enough? Stand up for your rights, citizens!

speaker: Guard 1
en: Who are we looking for, anyway?

speaker: Guard 2
en: Théroigne de Méricourt! I told you a hundred times...

speaker: Bishop
en: Heads up, Initiates! Check the roofs for snipers.

speaker: Guard 3
en: You remember the signal?

speaker: Guard 4
en: What signal?

speaker: Guard 3
en: The signal that they see Théroigne! The signal is the sound of an owl.

speaker: Guard 4
en: What does an owl sound like?

speaker: Guard 3
en: You've never heard an owl?

speaker: Guard 4
en: Won't they start shooting when they see Théroigne?

speaker: Guard 3
en: They had better start shooting.

speaker: Guard 4
en: I'll just keep an ear out for gunshots then.

speaker: Bishop
en: You have to take out the gatehouse captains, or this march will never make it out of Paris.

speaker: Théroigne
en: Kings and nobles pay no tax, while we shoulder the burden for them! We must band together, citizens! Citizens! We rally to be heard by the King! We do not want violence, we want the King to see how his citizens live! We speak for the hungry! We speak for the shivering! We speak for Paris! Come on, citizens! Let's show the King what it means to be hungry! We ask for food, and they feed us grapeshots! Forward to Versailles, citizens! Citizens! No more delays! To Versailles! Open this gate! The King awaits, citizens! Break down this gate!

speaker: Crowd
en: We're with you, Théroigne! They can't stop us!

speaker: Bishop
en: One down, two to go, Initiates.

speaker: Bishop
en: Just one more captain in the way.

speaker: Bishop
en: Nice one, Initiates. The gatehouses are clear. Ah, of course. The last line of defense. Fucking cannons. Get over the wall and spike the cannons before the crowd breaks through the gate.

speaker: Guard 3
en: Whiff of grapeshot at a bunch of ladies? Easiest fifty francs I ever earned.

speaker: Guard 4
en: Aye. Should be a piece of cake.

speaker: Guard 5
en: That powder dry? I don't want another misfire on my hands.

speaker: Guard 6
en: Dry as a bone, sir.

speaker: Guard 5
en: Where's this damn crowd? Said they'd be here by now.

speaker: Guard 6
en: Maybe the gate captains held them up some.

speaker: Guard 7
en: I heard it's all fishmongers marching on Versailles.

speaker: Guard 8
en: Fishmongers? I wouldn't want to be in the King's shoes right now.

speaker: Guard 7
en: I've seen those fishwives gut a carp in the blink of an eye.

speaker: Guard 8
en: Good thing there's a few cannons between us and them.

speaker: Bishop
en: One cannon down.

speaker: Bishop
en: That's two.

speaker: Bishop
en: And that's the last cannon! Méricourt leads this march all the way to Versailles. Nice work.
